Why D is not selected: A custom scheduled function is code and maintenance in place of a ready-made service.

---

79\. A company is planning to use an Amazon DynamoDB table for data storage. The company is concerned about cost optimization. The table will not be used on most mornings. In the evenings, the read and write traffic will often be unpredictable. When traffic spikes occur, they will happen very quickly.  
What should a solutions architect recommend?  
A. Create a DynamoDB table in on-demand capacity mode.  
B. Create a DynamoDB table with a global secondary index.  
C. Create a DynamoDB table with provisioned capacity and auto scaling.  
D. Create a DynamoDB table in provisioned capacity mode, and configure it as a global table.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The table sits idle for long stretches, and evening traffic is unpredictable and spikes very quickly. On-demand capacity mode adjusts throughput instantly and is billed on actual requests, so there's no charge for idle time and a spike doesn't run into a pre-set capacity ceiling.  
Why B is not selected: A secondary index solves the problem of accessing data by a different key and has nothing to do with cost under uneven load.  
Why C is not selected: Provisioned capacity auto scaling reacts on the order of minutes: during very sharp spikes, requests would be throttled with a throughput-exceeded error.  
Why D is not selected: A global table is meant for multi-Region operation and simply doubles the cost, and provisioned mode still can't keep up with the spikes.

---

80\. A company recently signed a contract with an AWS Managed Service Provider (MSP) Partner for help with an application migration initiative. A solutions architect needs ta share an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from an existing AWS account with the MSP Partner's AWS account. The AMI is backed by Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) and uses an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key to encrypt EBS volume snapshots.  
What is the MOST secure way for the solutions architect to share the AMI with the MSP Partner's AWS account?  
A. Make the encrypted AMI and snapshots publicly available. Modify the key policy to allow the MSP Partner's AWS account to use the key.  
B. Modify the launchPermission property of the AMI. Share the AMI with the MSP Partner's AWS account only. Modify the key policy to allow the MSP Partner's AWS account to use the key.  
C. Modify the launchPermission property of the AMI. Share the AMI with the MSP Partner's AWS account only. Modify the key policy to trust a new KMS key that is owned by the MSP Partner for encryption.  
D. Export the AMI from the source account to an Amazon S3 bucket in the MSP Partner's AWS account, Encrypt the S3 bucket with a new KMS key that is owned by the MSP Partner. Copy and launch the AMI in the MSP Partner's AWS account.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The image is encrypted with a KMS key, so sharing it is really two separate operations. First: allow the other account to launch the image — add its account ID to the AMI's launchPermission (which also grants access to the underlying EBS snapshots). Second: allow that same account to use the key the volumes are encrypted with — an edit to the KMS key policy. Without the second step, the partner would see the image but wouldn't be able to decrypt the volumes. The 'MOST secure' requirement means granting access to that specific account, not publishing the image.  
Why A is not selected: Making the encrypted AMI public exposes the image to the entire world. Even if the key itself is granted only to the partner, this grossly violates the requirement for maximum security.  
Why C is not selected: A key policy can't 'trust another key': the snapshots are encrypted with your key, and only that key can decrypt them. The partner can re-encrypt a copy with their own key only after they've already been granted access to yours.  
Why D is not selected: Exporting the AMI to a bucket in the other account is a roundabout, labor-intensive path, and exporting a virtual machine doesn't even work for images encrypted with a KMS key.

---

81\. A solutions architect is designing the cloud architecture for a new application being deployed on AWS. The process should run in parallel while adding and removing application nodes as needed based on the number of jobs to be processed. The processor application is stateless. The solutions architect must ensure that the application is loosely coupled and the job items are durably stored.  
Which design should the solutions architect use?  
A. Create an Amazon SNS topic to send the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that consists of the processor application. Create a launch configuration that uses the AMI. Create an Auto Scaling group using the launch configuration. Set the scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to add and remove nodes based on CPU usage.  
B. Create an Amazon SQS queue to hold the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that consists of the processor application. Create a launch configuration that uses the AMI. Create an Auto Scaling group using the launch configuration. Set the scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to add and remove nodes based on network usage.  
C. Create an Amazon SQS queue to hold the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that consists of the processor application. Create a launch template that uses the AMI. Create an Auto Scaling group using the launch template. Set the scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to add and remove nodes based on the number of items in the SQS queue.  
D. Create an Amazon SNS topic to send the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that consists of the processor application. Create a launch template that uses the AMI. Create an Auto Scaling group using the launch template. Set the scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to add and remove nodes based on the number of messages published to the SNS topic.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: Jobs need to be stored durably, the processors need to be stateless, and scaling should track the amount of work. An SQS queue holds the jobs, an AMI containing the processor application is used in the launch template, and the Auto Scaling group grows and shrinks based on the number of messages in the queue — that is, on the actual amount of work.  
Why A is not selected: SNS doesn't store messages: if no consumer is available at the moment, the job is lost, and scaling on CPU usage doesn't reflect the size of the queue.  
Why B is not selected: The queue choice is correct, but scaling on network usage is only loosely related to the number of pending jobs.  
Why D is not selected: SNS again fails to provide durable storage for jobs, and the number of published messages doesn't show how much work remains.

---

82\. A company hosts its web applications in the AWS Cloud. The company configures Elastic Load Balancers to use certificates that are imported into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). The company's security team must be notified 30 days before the expiration of each certificate.  
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?  
A. Add a rule in ACM to publish a custom message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic every day, beginning 30 days before any certificate will expire.  
B. Create an AWS Config rule that checks for certificates that will expire within 30 days. Configure Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) to invoke a custom alert by way of Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) when AWS Config reports a noncompliant resource.  
C. Use AWS Trusted Advisor to check for certificates that will expire within 30 days. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that is based on Trusted Advisor metrics for check status changes. Configure the alarm to send a custom alert by way of Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).  
D. Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule to detect any certificates that will expire within 30 days. Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to send a custom alert by way of Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).  
Answer: B  
Explanation: ACM has a managed AWS Config rule called acm-certificate-expiration-check: it flags certificates — including imported ones — as noncompliant when they're due to expire within a set window. EventBridge picks up the noncompliance event and sends a notification to the security team's SNS topic.  
Why A is not selected: ACM itself has no mechanism for rules that publish arbitrary messages to SNS on a schedule.  
Why C is not selected: Trusted Advisor only partially tracks load balancer certificates and requires a Business-level support plan or higher; the managed Config rule is the standard, more precise path.  
Why D is not selected: ACM does generate an expiration event, but by default 45 days out, and an EventBridge rule can't be configured with an arbitrary 30-day threshold — that's exactly what the Config rule is for.

---

83\. A company's dynamic website is hosted using on-premises servers in the United States. The company is launching its product in Europe, and it wants to optimize site loading times for new European users. The site's backend must remain in the United States. The product is being launched in a few days, and an immediate solution is needed.  
What should the solutions architect recommend?  
A. Launch an Amazon EC2 instance in us-east-1 and migrate the site to it.  
B. Move the website to Amazon S3. Use Cross-Region Replication between Regions.  
C. Use Amazon CloudFront with a custom origin pointing to the on-premises servers.  
D. Use an Amazon Route 53 geoproximity routing policy pointing to on-premises servers.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The backend has to stay in the company's own data center, and what needs speeding up is European users, within just a few days. CloudFront supports an arbitrary custom origin, including a server outside AWS: requests land at the nearest edge location, static content gets cached, and dynamic content travels to the origin over the AWS backbone with an already-established TLS connection. No migration is involved, and setup takes hours.  
Why A is not selected: Moving the site to an instance in the US doesn't speed things up for European users: the distance stays the same, and migration takes time.  
Why B is not selected: The site is dynamic, so it can't be hosted on S3, and cross-Region replication would only solve the problem for static content.  
Why D is not selected: Geoproximity only chooses which origin to send a user to, but there's only one origin here — the same servers in the US. Latency wouldn't change.

---

84\. A company wants to reduce the cost of its existing three-tier web architecture. The web, application, and database servers are running on Amazon EC2 instances for the development, test, and production environments. The EC2 instances average 30% CPU utilization during peak hours and 10% CPU utilization during non-peak hours.  
The production EC2 instances run 24 hours a day. The development and test EC2 instances run for at least 8 hours each day. The company plans to implement automation to stop the development and test EC2 instances when they are not in use.  
Which EC2 instance purchasing solution will meet the company's requirements MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Use Spot Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use Reserved Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.  
B. Use Reserved Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use On-Demand Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.  
C. Use Spot blocks for the production EC2 instances. Use Reserved Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.  
D. Use On-Demand Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use Spot blocks for the development and test EC2 instances.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: Production instances run around the clock and predictably — they're most cost-effectively covered by Reserved Instances, with savings of up to 72 percent. The development and test instances run for a few hours and will be stopped by automation, so On-Demand pricing suits them: committing for a year to intermittent workloads isn't worthwhile.  
Why A is not selected: Interruptible instances are risky for production: AWS can reclaim the capacity at any time, and reserving irregular environments isn't cost-effective.  
Why C is not selected: Spot blocks (pre-paid blocks of Spot capacity for a fixed duration) are no longer offered to new customers, and that kind of capacity isn't suited to round-the-clock production anyway.  
Why D is not selected: Full-price production is overpaying, and interruptible capacity for development environments risks losing the instance mid-task.

---

85\. A company has a production web application in which users upload documents through a web interface or a mobile app. According to a new regulatory requirement. new documents cannot be modified or deleted after they are stored.  
What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?  
A. Store the uploaded documents in an Amazon S3 bucket with S3 Versioning and S3 Object Lock enabled.  
B. Store the uploaded documents in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to archive the documents periodically.  
C. Store the uploaded documents in an Amazon S3 bucket with S3 Versioning enabled. Configure an ACL to restrict all access to read-only.  
D. Store the uploaded documents on an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume. Access the data by mounting the volume in read-only mode.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: 'Cannot be modified or deleted after they are stored' describes WORM storage, and in S3 that's handled by Object Lock. It works on top of versioning: the object is stored as an immutable version, and a retention period or legal hold prevents that version from being deleted or overwritten. That's why both are enabled together — versioning as the foundation and Object Lock as the actual restriction. The mode is chosen based on how strict the requirement is: compliance mode, when no one can bypass it, or governance mode, when a privileged user is allowed to.  
Why B is not selected: A Lifecycle rule changes the storage class. It doesn't prevent an object from being overwritten or deleted.  
Why C is not selected: Versioning makes deletion reversible, but doesn't prevent it, and an ACL is a legacy permissions mechanism that doesn't stop the owner or an administrator from deleting the object.  
Why D is not selected: Mounting EFS as read-only is a client-side setting: the same file system can be mounted for writing from another machine. That's not data immutability.

---

86\. A company has several web servers that need to frequently access a common Amazon RDS MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance. The company wants a secure method for the web servers to connect to the database while meeting a security requirement to rotate user credentials frequently.  
Which solution meets these requirements?  
A. Store the database user credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Grant the necessary IAM permissions to allow the web servers to access AWS Secrets Manager.  
B. Store the database user credentials in AWS Systems Manager OpsCenter. Grant the necessary IAM permissions to allow the web servers to access OpsCenter.  
C. Store the database user credentials in a secure Amazon S3 bucket. Grant the necessary IAM permissions to allow the web servers to retrieve credentials and access the database.  
D. Store the database user credentials in files encrypted with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) on the web server file system. The web server should be able to decrypt the files and access the database.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The requirement to "rotate user credentials frequently" combined with secure password retrieval by the web servers points to Secrets Manager. The password is stored encrypted with a KMS key, the servers retrieve it by calling GetSecretValue under the instance role, and rotation for RDS MySQL is handled by a managed, scheduled function. A useful operational detail: during rotation, Secrets Manager keeps secret versions labeled AWSCURRENT and AWSPREVIOUS, so a request that arrives right as the password changes does not break.  
Why B is not selected: OpsCenter in Systems Manager is a workspace for triaging operational incidents (OpsItems). It is not a secrets store.  
Why C is not selected: A password in an S3 object does not rotate itself: rotation would have to be built with custom code, and access would have to be restricted manually.  
Why D is not selected: Files on each web server's file system mean a copy of the secret on every machine, plus manual redistribution of the new password on every rotation.

---

87\. A company hosts an application on AWS Lambda functions that are invoked by an Amazon API Gateway API. The Lambda functions save customer data to an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. Whenever the company upgrades the database, the Lambda functions fail to establish database connections until the upgrade is complete. The result is that customer data is not recorded for some of the event.  
A solutions architect needs to design a solution that stores customer data that is created during database upgrades.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Provision an Amazon RDS proxy to sit between the Lambda functions and the database. Configure the Lambda functions to connect to the RDS proxy.  
B. Increase the run time of the Lambda functions to the maximum. Create a retry mechanism in the code that stores the customer data in the database.  
C. Persist the customer data to Lambda local storage. Configure new Lambda functions to scan the local storage to save the customer data to the database.  
D. Store the customer data in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue. Create a new Lambda function that polls the queue and stores the customer data in the database.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: During the upgrade the database is unavailable, and records that arrive during that window are lost. A buffer solves the problem: the function invoked from API Gateway places the customer data on an SQS FIFO queue, and a separate function polls the queue and writes to the database. While the database is upgrading, messages simply accumulate in the queue and are processed once it comes back; ordering is preserved throughout.  
Why A is not selected: RDS Proxy smooths over failovers and manages the connection pool, but during a version upgrade the database is still unavailable, so there is nowhere to write the data.  
Why B is not selected: Retries inside the function run into the function's execution time limit: the upgrade takes longer than that, so the data is lost anyway.  
Why C is not selected: A function's local storage is ephemeral and belongs to a specific execution environment instance: another function invocation won't see it, and it disappears once that instance is gone.

---

88\. A survey company has gathered data for several years from areas in the United States. The company hosts the data in an Amazon S3 bucket that is 3 TB in size and growing. The company has started to share the data with a European marketing firm that has S3 buckets. The company wants to ensure that its data transfer costs remain as low as possible.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Configure the Requester Pays feature on the company's S3 bucket.  
B. Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication from the company's S3 bucket to one of the marketing firm's S3 buckets.  
C. Configure cross-account access for the marketing firm so that the marketing firm has access to the company's S3 bucket.  
D. Configure the company's S3 bucket to use S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Sync the S3 bucket to one of the marketing firm's S3 buckets.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The bucket owner pays for outbound data transfer from S3, and that's exactly what needs to change. Requester Pays shifts the cost of requests and outbound transfer to whoever downloads the data: the marketing firm accesses the bucket with its own credentials and pays for its own downloads. The owner continues to pay only for storage. One limitation worth remembering: with Requester Pays enabled, anonymous access is not possible — every request must be signed and include a header confirming acceptance of the charges. The same answer applies in {{q:960}}.  
Why B is not selected: Cross-Region Replication would make the company pay for both cross-region transfer of every object and storage of the second copy. Costs would go up, not down.  
Why C is not selected: Granting cross-account access solves the permissions problem, but the bill for outbound transfer would still go to the bucket owner.  
Why D is not selected: Storage class has no effect on outbound transfer pricing, and syncing to someone else's bucket is still a transfer paid for by the company.

---

89\. A company uses Amazon S3 to store its confidential audit documents. The S3 bucket uses bucket policies to restrict access to audit team IAM user credentials according to the principle of least privilege. Company managers are worried about accidental deletion of documents in the S3 bucket and want a more secure solution.  
What should a solutions architect do to secure the audit documents?  
A. Enable the versioning and MFA Delete features on the S3 bucket.  
B. Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) on the IAM user credentials for each audit team IAM user account.  
C. Add an S3 Lifecycle policy to the audit team's IAM user accounts to deny the s3:DeleteObject action during audit dates.  
D. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to encrypt the S3 bucket and restrict audit team IAM user accounts from accessing the KMS key.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The concern is specific — accidental deletion of documents, not a data leak. That calls for reversibility and a second factor: versioning preserves prior versions on deletion and overwrite (a delete creates a delete marker), and MFA Delete requires a one-time code for irreversible operations — deleting a specific version and disabling versioning. Encryption and permission tweaks don't address this problem: whoever has delete permission can delete the encrypted object just as easily.  
Why B is not selected: MFA on console sign-in protects the account itself. It does not stop a DeleteObject call made with that account's access keys — that's exactly what MFA Delete on the bucket is for.  
Why C is not selected: Lifecycle rules apply to objects in a bucket, not to "IAM accounts," and they can only transition or expire objects. They can't enforce a deny.  
Why D is not selected: Blocking the audit team's access to the key means they can no longer read their own documents. It does nothing to prevent the object from being deleted.

---

90\. A company is using a SQL database to store movie data that is publicly accessible. The database runs on an Amazon RDS Single-AZ DB instance. A script runs queries at random intervals each day to record the number of new movies that have been added to the database. The script must report a final total during business hours.  
The company's development team notices that the database performance is inadequate for development tasks when the script is running. A solutions architect must recommend a solution to resolve this issue.  
Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Modify the DB instance to be a Multi-AZ deployment.  
B. Create a read replica of the database. Configure the script to query only the read replica.  
C. Instruct the development team to manually export the entries in the database at the end of each day.  
D. Use Amazon ElastiCache to cache the common queries that the script runs against the database.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The script's queries are interfering with the developers' work. A read replica removes that load from the primary instance: the script queries only the replica, while development continues to work against the primary database. It's set up with a single operation, and no code needs to change.  
Why A is not selected: The standby instance in a Multi-AZ configuration is not available for reads: the load would remain on the primary.  
Why C is not selected: A manual daily export is manual work, and the data goes stale.  
Why D is not selected: The queries run at random times and count new records: the cache would miss constantly, and the application would still have to be modified.

---

91\. A company has applications that run on Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC. One of the applications needs to call the Amazon S3 API to store and read objects. According to the company's security regulations, no traffic from the applications is allowed to travel across the internet.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Configure an S3 gateway endpoint.  
B. Create an S3 bucket in a private subnet.  
C. Create an S3 bucket in the same AWS Region as the EC2 instances.  
D. Configure a NAT gateway in the same subnet as the EC2 instances.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The requirement is categorical: none of the application's traffic may travel over the internet. S3 is a regional service with public endpoints, so "putting the bucket in a private subnet" isn't possible — what gets hidden is the path to it, not the bucket itself. A gateway endpoint adds a route to the VPC's route table pointing to the S3 prefix over the AWS network itself: packets never leave to the internet, and the instances don't need public addresses. Access can be further restricted with an aws:SourceVpce condition in the bucket policy, so the bucket only accepts requests through that endpoint.  
Why B is not selected: S3 buckets don't live inside VPC subnets: it's a regional service with its own namespace. That configuration simply doesn't exist.  
Why C is not selected: Being in the same Region only avoids cross-region transfer. The path still goes through the public S3 endpoint.  
Why D is not selected: A NAT gateway exists precisely to send traffic out to the internet. That's a direct violation of the requirement.

---

92\. A company is storing sensitive user information in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company wants to provide secure access to this bucket from the application tier running on Amazon EC2 instances inside a VPC.  
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to accomplish this? (Choose two.)  
A. Configure a VPC gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 within the VPC.  
B. Create a bucket policy to make the objects in the S3 bucket public.  
C. Create a bucket policy that limits access to only the application tier running in the VPC.  
D. Create an IAM user with an S3 access policy and copy the IAM credentials to the EC2 instance.  
E. Create a NAT instance and have the EC2 instances use the NAT instance to access the S3 bucket.  
Answer: AC  
Explanation: Two independent layers of protection. Network layer: a gateway endpoint for S3 (A) routes traffic from the VPC to the bucket over the internal AWS network, without going out to the internet. Authorization layer: a bucket policy (C) that permits access only to requests coming from this VPC or through this endpoint (using the aws:SourceVpc or aws:SourceVpce conditions) and only to the application tier's role. Together they provide both a private path and a denial of access from anywhere else. The instances operate under a role rather than stored keys throughout.  
Why B is not selected: Making a bucket with sensitive data publicly accessible is the direct opposite of the requirement.  
Why D is not selected: Copying an IAM user's keys onto the instance creates a long-lived secret sitting on disk. The proper approach is an instance role with temporary credentials.  
Why E is not selected: A NAT instance sends traffic out to the internet and adds a node that has to be maintained. The endpoint solves the same problem privately and without a server.

---

93\. A company runs an on-premises application that is powered by a MySQL database. The company is migrating the application to AWS to increase the application's elasticity and availability.  
The current architecture shows heavy read activity on the database during times of normal operation. Every 4 hours, the company's development team pulls a full export of the production database to populate a database in the staging environment. During this period, users experience unacceptable application latency. The development team is unable to use the staging environment until the procedure completes.  
A solutions architect must recommend replacement architecture that alleviates the application latency issue. The replacement architecture also must give the development team the ability to continue using the staging environment without delay.  
Which solution meets these requirements?  
A. Use Amazon Aurora MySQL with Multi-AZ Aurora Replicas for production. Populate the staging database by implementing a backup and restore process that uses the mysqldump utility.  
B. Use Amazon Aurora MySQL with Multi-AZ Aurora Replicas for production. Use database cloning to create the staging database on-demand.  
C. Use Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ deployment and read replicas for production. Use the standby instance for the staging database.  
D. Use Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ deployment and read replicas for production. Populate the staging database by implementing a backup and restore process that uses the mysqldump utility.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The problem is the full export every four hours: it loads the production database and locks the staging environment for a long time. Aurora can create a database clone almost instantly using storage-level copy-on-write, so the clone appears within minutes, doesn't physically copy the data, and doesn't add load to the source cluster. Developers get a fresh copy on demand.  
Why A is not selected: A mysqldump export is exactly the operation causing the load and the delay. The problem remains.  
Why C is not selected: The standby instance in a Multi-AZ configuration isn't available for reads or writes: it can't be used as a staging environment.  
Why D is not selected: Again a full export and restore: both the load on production and the long wait for developers remain.

---

94\. A company is designing an application where users upload small files into Amazon S3. After a user uploads a file, the file requires one-time simple processing to transform the data and save the data in JSON format for later analysis.  
Each file must be processed as quickly as possible after it is uploaded. Demand will vary. On some days, users will upload a high number of files. On other days, users will upload a few files or no files.  
Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Configure Amazon EMR to read text files from Amazon S3. Run processing scripts to transform the data. Store the resulting JSON file in an Amazon Aurora DB cluster.  
B. Configure Amazon S3 to send an event notification to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use Amazon EC2 instances to read from the queue and process the data. Store the resulting JSON file in Amazon DynamoDB.  
C. Configure Amazon S3 to send an event notification to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use an AWS Lambda function to read from the queue and process the data. Store the resulting JSON file in Amazon DynamoDB.  
D. Configure Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) to send an event to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams when a new file is uploaded. Use an AWS Lambda function to consume the event from the stream and process the data. Store the resulting JSON file in an Amazon Aurora DB cluster.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The files are small, processing is simple and one-time, and demand is spiky. An S3 notification places an event on an SQS queue, a Lambda function reads the queue and processes the file, and the resulting JSON is stored in DynamoDB. Everything is serverless: it scales itself, costs nothing when idle, and requires almost no operational work. The queue also provides retries on failure.  
Why A is not selected: An EMR cluster is billed for node uptime and requires configuration — disproportionate for processing small files one at a time.  
Why B is not selected: EC2 instances reading the queue need to be scaled, patched, and monitored: more operational overhead than a function.  
Why D is not selected: EventBridge and Kinesis add an extra layer where an S3 notification is already enough, and Aurora is overkill for storing individual JSON documents.

---

95\. An application allows users at a company's headquarters to access product data. The product data is stored in an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance. The operations team has isolated an application performance slowdown and wants to separate read traffic from write traffic. A solutions architect needs to optimize the application's performance quickly.  
What should the solutions architect recommend?  
A. Change the existing database to a Multi-AZ deployment. Serve the read requests from the primary Availability Zone.  
B. Change the existing database to a Multi-AZ deployment. Serve the read requests from the secondary Availability Zone.  
C. Create read replicas for the database. Configure the read replicas with half of the compute and storage resources as the source database.  
D. Create read replicas for the database. Configure the read replicas with the same compute and storage resources as the source database.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: Read and write traffic need to be split quickly, without sacrificing performance. Read replicas take on the SELECT queries while the primary instance remains responsible for writes. Important detail: the replica must have the same compute and storage resources as the source, otherwise it will start to lag and become a bottleneck itself.  
Why A is not selected: A Multi-AZ configuration doesn't split load: reads against the primary instance continue at the same volume.  
Why B is not selected: The Multi-AZ standby instance doesn't accept requests at all — reading from it isn't possible.  
Why C is not selected: A replica with half the source's resources can't keep up with the stream of changes; replication lag will grow, and the data will end up stale.

---

96\. An Amazon EC2 administrator created the following policy associated with an IAM group containing several users:  
What is the effect of this policy?  
![Exhibit for question 96](images/exhibits/q96.png)  
A. Users can terminate an EC2 instance in any AWS Region except us-east-1.  
B. Users can terminate an EC2 instance with the IP address 10.100.100.1 in the us-east-1 Region.  
C. Users can terminate an EC2 instance in the us-east-1 Region when the user's source IP is 10.100.100.254.  
D. Users cannot terminate an EC2 instance in the us-east-1 Region when the user's source IP is 10.100.100.254.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The policy has two statements, and they must be read together. The first allows ec2:TerminateInstances, but only if the request comes from an IP address within the 10.100.100.0/24 range. The second denies all EC2 actions if the Region is not us-east-1, and an explicit Deny overrides any Allow. The intersection of these conditions gives the answer: instances can only be terminated in us-east-1, and only from an address in that subnet; 10.100.100.254 falls within it. General IAM rule: an explicit deny is evaluated first, then whether an allow exists, and everything else is denied by default.  
Why A is not selected: The second statement denies EC2 actions in every Region except us-east-1. That is exactly the opposite of what the option states.  
Why B is not selected: The IpAddress condition checks the source IP of the request (aws:SourceIp), not the IP address of the instance itself. It's about where the API call came from.  
Why D is not selected: 10.100.100.254 falls within 10.100.100.0/24, so the allow applies — it isn't blocked.

---

97\. A company has a large Microsoft SharePoint deployment running on-premises that requires Microsoft Windows shared file storage. The company wants to migrate this workload to the AWS Cloud and is considering various storage options. The storage solution must be highly available and integrated with Active Directory for access control.  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements?  
A. Configure Amazon EFS storage and set the Active Directory domain for authentication.  
B. Create an SMB file share on an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway in two Availability Zones.  
C. Create an Amazon S3 bucket and configure Microsoft Windows Server to mount it as a volume.  
D. Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system on AWS and set the Active Directory domain for authentication.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: SharePoint requires a Windows shared resource over the SMB protocol with Active Directory authentication — that is exactly the profile of Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. The file system joins the AD domain, supports Windows access control lists and shadow copies, and deploys in a Multi-AZ configuration for high availability.  
Why A is not selected: EFS is an NFS file system for Linux; it doesn't work with SMB and doesn't integrate with an Active Directory domain in the required way.  
Why B is not selected: A file gateway is a hybrid gateway for accessing S3 from an on-premises network, not a full-fledged shared storage solution for a workload that has moved entirely into AWS.  
Why C is not selected: There's no built-in way to mount an S3 bucket as a Windows volume, and it wouldn't provide the file-system semantics with locking that SharePoint needs.

---

98\. An image-processing company has a web application that users use to upload images. The application uploads the images into an Amazon S3 bucket. The company has set up S3 event notifications to publish the object creation events to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue. The SQS queue serves as the event source for an AWS Lambda function that processes the images and sends the results to users through email.  
Users report that they are receiving multiple email messages for every uploaded image. A solutions architect determines that SQS messages are invoking the Lambda function more than once, resulting in multiple email messages.  
What should the solutions architect do to resolve this issue with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Set up long polling in the SQS queue by increasing the ReceiveMessage wait time to 30 seconds.  
B. Change the SQS standard queue to an SQS FIFO queue. Use the message deduplication ID to discard duplicate messages.  
C. Increase the visibility timeout in the SQS queue to a value that is greater than the total of the function timeout and the batch window timeout.  
D. Modify the Lambda function to delete each message from the SQS queue immediately after the message is read before processing.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: Repeated emails mean a message is becoming visible in the queue again before the function finishes processing it. The visibility timeout needs to be set higher than the sum of the function's timeout and the batch window timeout — then the message won't be handed to a second instance of the function.  
Why A is not selected: Long polling reduces the number of empty responses and their cost, but it has no effect on message redelivery.  
Why B is not selected: A FIFO queue would solve the problem, but switching to it changes the queue type, limits throughput, and requires changes — while the problem can be fixed with a single setting.  
Why D is not selected: Deleting the message before processing it leads to data loss on any function failure.

---

99\. A company is implementing a shared storage solution for a gaming application that is hosted in an on-premises data center. The company needs the ability to use Lustre clients to access data. The solution must be fully managed.  
Which solution meets these requirements?  
A. Create an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway. Create a file share that uses the required client protocol. Connect the application server to the file share.  
B. Create an Amazon EC2 Windows instance. Install and configure a Windows file share role on the instance. Connect the application server to the file share.  
C. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system, and configure it to support Lustre. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.  
D. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: The key phrase is Lustre clients. The only fully managed AWS service with that protocol is Amazon FSx for Lustre: it delivers very high throughput and low latency, is reachable from an on-premises network over Direct Connect or VPN, and is fully managed by AWS.  
Why A is not selected: Storage Gateway serves shares over NFS and SMB; it has no Lustre protocol.  
Why B is not selected: A self-managed Windows server is neither Lustre nor a managed service: it would have to be maintained in-house.  
Why C is not selected: EFS has no Lustre support mode: it's an NFS file system. That configuration doesn't exist.

---

100\. A company's containerized application runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. The application needs to download security certificates before it can communicate with other business applications. The company wants a highly secure solution to encrypt and decrypt the certificates in near real time. The solution also needs to store data in highly available storage after the data is encrypted.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Create AWS Secrets Manager secrets for encrypted certificates. Manually update the certificates as needed. Control access to the data by using fine-grained IAM access.  
B. Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the Python cryptography library to receive and perform encryption operations. Store the function in an Amazon S3 bucket.  
C. Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Allow the EC2 role to use the KMS key for encryption operations. Store the encrypted data on Amazon S3.  
D. Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Allow the EC2 role to use the KMS key for encryption operations. Store the encrypted data on Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The requirement is to encrypt and decrypt certificates in near real time, store the result in highly available storage, and avoid operational overhead. KMS turns cryptography into a managed service: the EC2 role is granted permission to use the key, the application encrypts the data (in practice via envelope encryption using GenerateDataKey) and puts the ciphertext in S3, which stores objects across three Availability Zones. No custom libraries and no key servers to run.  
Why A is not selected: Secrets Manager is designed for secrets, not arbitrary certificate files, and the option explicitly calls for manual updates — which is exactly the operational overhead the requirement asks to avoid.  
Why B is not selected: A custom function with a cryptography library means you're responsible for the algorithms, the keys, and their storage yourself. "Store the function in an S3 bucket" also isn't a way to run it.  
Why D is not selected: Encrypting via KMS is the right choice, but an EBS volume is tied to a single Availability Zone and a single instance. The requirement for highly available storage is met by S3, not EBS.

---

101\. A solutions architect is designing a VPC with public and private subnets. The VPC and subnets use IPv4 CIDR blocks. There is one public subnet and one private subnet in each of three Availability Zones (AZs) for high availability. An internet gateway is used to provide internet access for the public subnets. The private subnets require access to the internet to allow Amazon EC2 instances to download software updates.  
What should the solutions architect do to enable Internet access for the private subnets?  
A. Create three NAT gateways, one for each public subnet in each AZ. Create a private route table for each AZ that forwards non-VPC traffic to the NAT gateway in its AZ.  
B. Create three NAT instances, one for each private subnet in each AZ. Create a private route table for each AZ that forwards non-VPC traffic to the NAT instance in its AZ.  
C. Create a second internet gateway on one of the private subnets. Update the route table for the private subnets that forward non-VPC traffic to the private internet gateway.  
D. Create an egress-only internet gateway on one of the public subnets. Update the route table for the private subnets that forward non-VPC traffic to the egress-only Internet gateway.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The private subnets need outbound internet access, and the solution has to be fault tolerant. A NAT gateway is a zonal resource, so one is created in the public subnet of each Availability Zone, and each zone's private route table sends all non-VPC-bound traffic to its "own" gateway. A zone failure doesn't affect the others, and no cross-zone data transfer charges apply.  
Why B is not selected: NAT instances need to sit in the public subnets, not the private ones, and they require manual maintenance and scaling.  
Why C is not selected: A VPC can have only one internet gateway, and a subnet with a route to it is, by definition, public.  
Why D is not selected: An egress-only internet gateway works only with IPv6, while the scenario uses IPv4 blocks.

---

102\. A company wants to migrate an on-premises data center to AWS. The data center hosts an SFTP server that stores its data on an NFS-based file system. The server holds 200 GB of data that needs to be transferred. The server must be hosted on an Amazon EC2 instance that uses an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system.  
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to automate this task? (Choose two.)  
A. Launch the EC2 instance into the same Availability Zone as the EFS file system.  
B. Install an AWS DataSync agent in the on-premises data center.  
C. Create a secondary Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume on the EC2 instance for the data.  
D. Manually use an operating system copy command to push the data to the EC2 instance.  
E. Use AWS DataSync to create a suitable location configuration for the on-premises SFTP server.  
Answer: BE  
Explanation: The task is to automate moving the data from the on-premises server into EFS. AWS DataSync does this natively: an agent is installed in the company's data center (B) and gets access to the SFTP server's NFS file system, after which a location is configured in DataSync pointing at that source (E). The transfer task then runs on a schedule, verifies integrity, and works incrementally.  
Why A is not selected: The EFS file system is reachable from every Availability Zone through its mount targets, so there's no need to co-locate the zone with the instance, and it has nothing to do with automating the transfer.  
Why C is not selected: An extra EBS volume contradicts the requirement: the data has to end up in EFS.  
Why D is not selected: Manually copying with an operating-system command is the exact opposite of the automation being asked for.

---

103\. A company has an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job that runs every day at the same time. The job processes XML data that is in an Amazon S3 bucket. New data is added to the S3 bucket every day. A solutions architect notices that AWS Glue is processing all the data during each run.  
What should the solutions architect do to prevent AWS Glue from reprocessing old data?  
A. Edit the job to use job bookmarks.  
B. Edit the job to delete data after the data is processed.  
C. Edit the job by setting the NumberOfWorkers field to 1.  
D. Use a FindMatches machine learning (ML) transform.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: AWS Glue keeps a marker of where the previous successful run left off — this is a job bookmark. With bookmarks enabled, the next run picks up only the S3 objects that appeared after the last run and leaves already-processed objects alone. Nothing needs to be deleted or rewritten; the service tracks the state itself. It's also worth remembering the flip side: if the job needs to reprocess all the data from scratch, the bookmark can be reset (job bookmark reset).  
Why B is not selected: Deleting the source data after processing solves the symptom at the cost of losing raw data that is usually needed for reprocessing and auditing. This is not an incremental-processing mechanism, it's destruction of the source.  
Why C is not selected: NumberOfWorkers sets the number of workers, which controls run speed and cost. It does not change the volume of data read.  
Why D is not selected: FindMatches is an ML transform for finding duplicate records. It has nothing to do with choosing to read only new files.

---

104\. A solutions architect must design a highly available infrastructure for a website. The website is powered by Windows web servers that run on Amazon EC2 instances. The solutions architect must implement a solution that can mitigate a large-scale DDoS attack that originates from thousands of IP addresses. Downtime is not acceptable for the website.  
Which actions should the solutions architect take to protect the website from such an attack? (Choose two.)  
A. Use AWS Shield Advanced to stop the DDoS attack.  
B. Configure Amazon GuardDuty to automatically block the attackers.  
C. Configure the website to use Amazon CloudFront for both static and dynamic content.  
D. Use an AWS Lambda function to automatically add attacker IP addresses to VPC network ACLs.  
E. Use EC2 Spot Instances in an Auto Scaling group with a target tracking scaling policy that is set to 80% CPU utilization.  
Answer: AC  
Explanation: Two complementary measures address a distributed attack from thousands of addresses. Shield Advanced (A) provides protection against large-scale attacks, automatic mitigations, access to the DDoS response team, and cost protection against scaling triggered by the attack. CloudFront (C) moves the entry point onto a global network of edge locations that absorbs volumetric attacks and stops them far from your instances, with all content — including dynamic content — passing through it. Together this is the standard combination for a requirement where "downtime is not acceptable."  
Why B is not selected: GuardDuty detects and reports threats but does not automatically block traffic.  
Why D is not selected: A custom solution that adds addresses to network ACLs does not scale: ACLs have a hard limit on the number of rules, while an attack involves thousands of addresses that keep changing.  
Why E is not selected: Scaling based on CPU utilization only pays for the attack with more compute capacity, and Spot Instances can also be reclaimed at any moment.

---

105\. A company is preparing to deploy a new serverless workload. A solutions architect must use the principle of least privilege to configure permissions that will be used to run an AWS Lambda function. An Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule will invoke the function.  
Which solution meets these requirements?  
A. Add an execution role to the function with lambda:InvokeFunction as the action and * as the principal.  
B. Add an execution role to the function with lambda:InvokeFunction as the action and Service: lambda.amazonaws.com as the principal.  
C. Add a resource-based policy to the function with lambda:* as the action and Service: events.amazonaws.com as the principal.  
D. Add a resource-based policy to the function with lambda:InvokeFunction as the action and Service: events.amazonaws.com as the principal.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: Permission for an external service to invoke the function is granted through a resource-based policy on the function itself, not through the execution role: the execution role describes what the function is allowed to do, not who is allowed to invoke it. Least privilege here means the action lambda:InvokeFunction and the principal events.amazonaws.com — only the EventBridge service, and only permission to invoke.  
Why A is not selected: The execution role grants permissions to the function itself, and a wildcard as the principal opens up invocation to anyone.  
Why B is not selected: This is again an execution role instead of a resource-based policy, and the principal is wrong: it should be the EventBridge service invoking the function, not the Lambda service itself.  
Why C is not selected: The resource-based policy is the right choice, but the action lambda:* grants far more than a single invocation — the least privilege principle is violated.

---

106\. A company is preparing to store confidential data in Amazon S3. For compliance reasons, the data must be encrypted at rest. Encryption key usage must be logged for auditing purposes. Keys must be rotated every year.  
Which solution meets these requirements and is the MOST operationally efficient?  
A. Server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C)  
B. Server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3)  
C. Server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) with manual rotation  
D. Server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) with automatic rotation  
Answer: D  
Explanation: The three requirements are addressed one by one. Encryption at rest is provided by every option. "Encryption key usage must be logged for auditing" rules out SSE-S3 and SSE-C: key access is visible in CloudTrail only for KMS keys, where every Decrypt and GenerateDataKey call is logged along with who accessed which object. "Keys must be rotated every year" combined with "MOST operationally efficient" rules out manual rotation: a KMS key has built-in automatic rotation once every 365 days, turned on with a single setting. That leaves SSE-KMS with automatic rotation.  
Why A is not selected: With SSE-C, the key is held by you and sent with every request. AWS neither logs nor rotates it, and all management falls on the application — the opposite of operational efficiency.  
Why B is not selected: SSE-S3 provides neither a log of key access nor control over the rotation schedule: the service manages the keys, and these operations are not visible in CloudTrail.  
Why C is not selected: Manual rotation satisfies the requirement but requires a human action every year and oversight to make sure it isn't forgotten. Automatic rotation does the same thing without intervention.

---

107\. A bicycle sharing company is developing a multi-tier architecture to track the location of its bicycles during peak operating hours. The company wants to use these data points in its existing analytics platform. A solutions architect must determine the most viable multi-tier option to support this architecture. The data points must be accessible from the REST API.  
Which action meets these requirements for storing and retrieving location data?  
A. Use Amazon Athena with Amazon S3.  
B. Use Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda.  
C. Use Amazon QuickSight with Amazon Redshift.  
D. Use Amazon API Gateway with Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: Location data points must be ingested and served through a REST API with minimal infrastructure. API Gateway provides the REST interface itself, while Lambda functions store and return the data. The combination is serverless, scales to handle peak operating hours, and integrates easily with the existing analytics platform.  
Why A is not selected: Athena runs queries against data in S3, but it is not a REST interface for an application.  
Why C is not selected: QuickSight and Redshift are a dashboard and an analytical data warehouse, not a way to ingest and serve data points through an API.  
Why D is not selected: Kinesis Data Analytics processes streams with queries but does not serve data to an application through a REST interface.

---

108\. A company has an automobile sales website that stores its listings in a database on Amazon RDS. When an automobile is sold, the listing needs to be removed from the website and the data must be sent to multiple target systems.  
Which design should a solutions architect recommend?  
A. Create an AWS Lambda function triggered when the database on Amazon RDS is updated to send the information to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue for the targets to consume.  
B. Create an AWS Lambda function triggered when the database on Amazon RDS is updated to send the information to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue for the targets to consume.  
C. Subscribe to an RDS event notification and send an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue fanned out to multiple Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topics. Use AWS Lambda functions to update the targets.  
D. Subscribe to an RDS event notification and send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic fanned out to multiple Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues. Use AWS Lambda functions to update the targets.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: The sale event needs to reach several independent systems. RDS publishes an event notification to an SNS topic, and several SQS queues are subscribed to that topic — one per receiving system. Each system then gets its own copy, can process it at its own pace, and survives temporary unavailability. Lambda functions read the queues and update the target systems.  
Why A is not selected: A Lambda function is not invoked by a row change in an RDS database — no such trigger exists.  
Why B is not selected: Same nonexistent-trigger problem, and a FIFO queue does not solve fan-out to multiple recipients.  
Why C is not selected: The direction is reversed: fan-out to multiple recipients is done by a topic, while a queue is a single-consumer destination.

---

109\. A company needs to store data in Amazon S3 and must prevent the data from being changed. The company wants new objects that are uploaded to Amazon S3 to remain unchangeable for a nonspecific amount of time until the company decides to modify the objects. Only specific users in the company's AWS account can have the ability 10 delete the objects.  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?  
A. Create an S3 Glacier vault. Apply a write-once, read-many (WORM) vault lock policy to the objects.  
B. Create an S3 bucket with S3 Object Lock enabled. Enable versioning. Set a retention period of 100 years. Use governance mode as the S3 bucket’s default retention mode for new objects.  
C. Create an S3 bucket. Use AWS CloudTrail to track any S3 API events that modify the objects. Upon notification, restore the modified objects from any backup versions that the company has.  
D. Create an S3 bucket with S3 Object Lock enabled. Enable versioning. Add a legal hold to the objects. Add the s3:PutObjectLegalHold permission to the IAM policies of users who need to delete the objects.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: Pay attention to the wording: objects must remain unchangeable for a nonspecific amount of time, meaning the duration is not known in advance and the company will remove the protection manually. A retention period does not describe this — it is always defined by a date or a number of days. This scenario matches a legal hold: it holds indefinitely until removed by someone with the s3:PutObjectLegalHold permission. That's also where the second half of the answer comes from: this is exactly the permission granted to the few people allowed to remove the hold and delete the objects.  
Why A is not selected: Vault Lock in S3 Glacier is a mechanism of the older archival service, applied to an entire vault and immutable once locked. It does not support flexibly lifting protection at the company's discretion.  
Why B is not selected: A 100-year period is a fixed duration, not "until the company decides." Governance mode can also be bypassed by anyone with the s3:BypassGovernanceRetention permission.  
Why C is not selected: CloudTrail and restoring from backups are an after-the-fact reaction. The requirement is that the object cannot be changed in the first place.

---

110\. A social media company allows users to upload images to its website. The website runs on Amazon EC2 instances.  
During upload requests, the website resizes the images to a standard size and stores the resized images in Amazon S3. Users are experiencing slow upload requests to the website.  
The company needs to reduce coupling within the application and improve website performance. A solutions architect must design the most operationally efficient process for image uploads.  
Which combination of actions should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)  
A. Configure the application to upload images to S3 Glacier.  
B. Configure the web server to upload the original images to Amazon S3.  
C. Configure the application to upload images directly from each user's browser to Amazon S3 through the use of a presigned URL  
D. Configure S3 Event Notifications to invoke an AWS Lambda function when an image is uploaded. Use the function to resize the image.  
E. Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function on a schedule to resize uploaded images.  
Answer: CD  
Review status: Corrected key (source: BD; reviewed: CD)  
Correction note: examtopics t1 q110 community consensus  
Explanation: Two separate bottlenecks are resolved individually. Uploads are slow because the bytes travel through the web server: a presigned URL gives the browser the ability to put the file directly into the bucket (C), removing EC2 as the middleman. Resizing is decoupled through an event: an S3 Event Notification invokes Lambda after the object has already been written (D), so the user doesn't wait for processing.  
Why A is not selected: S3 Glacier is an archival storage class: uploading there does not speed up the request, and reads take minutes to hours. It has nothing to do with decoupling components.  
Why B is not selected: The web server still receives the file and forwards it to S3 — the bytes still flow through the instance, so the slow upload remains.  
Why E is not selected: A schedule in EventBridge means batch resizing every N minutes: the image appears with a delay, and the upload event itself is ignored. An event-driven model here is both simpler and faster.

---

111\. A company recently migrated a message processing system to AWS. The system receives messages into an ActiveMQ queue running on an Amazon EC2 instance. Messages are processed by a consumer application running on Amazon EC2. The consumer application processes the messages and writes results to a MySQL database running on Amazon EC2. The company wants this application to be highly available with low operational complexity.  
Which architecture offers the HIGHEST availability?  
A. Add a second ActiveMQ server to another Availability Zone. Add an additional consumer EC2 instance in another Availability Zone. Replicate the MySQL database to another Availability Zone.  
B. Use Amazon MQ with active/standby brokers configured across two Availability Zones. Add an additional consumer EC2 instance in another Availability Zone. Replicate the MySQL database to another Availability Zone.  
C. Use Amazon MQ with active/standby brokers configured across two Availability Zones. Add an additional consumer EC2 instance in another Availability Zone. Use Amazon RDS for MySQL with Multi-AZ enabled.  
D. Use Amazon MQ with active/standby brokers configured across two Availability Zones. Add an Auto Scaling group for the consumer EC2 instances across two Availability Zones. Use Amazon RDS for MySQL with Multi- AZ enabled.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: The question is about the highest availability with the least operational complexity, so every tier needs to move to a managed, cross-AZ redundant service: Amazon MQ in active/standby mode instead of self-managed ActiveMQ, Amazon RDS for MySQL with Multi-AZ instead of a database on an instance, and — the key difference from option C — an Auto Scaling group for the consumers across two Availability Zones, which replaces a failed instance automatically.  
Why A is not selected: All three tiers remain self-managed on EC2: nobody recovers a failed instance, and MySQL replication has to be maintained manually.  
Why B is not selected: The queue and consumers are made redundant, but the database is still on EC2 with manual replication — the weakest link.  
Why C is not selected: The right combination of managed services, but the second consumer is added statically: if that instance fails, nothing replaces it. The Auto Scaling group in option D does this automatically.

---

112\. A company hosts a containerized web application on a fleet of on-premises servers that process incoming requests. The number of requests is growing quickly. The on-premises servers cannot handle the increased number of requests. The company wants to move the application to AWS with minimum code changes and minimum development effort.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Use AWS Fargate on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to run the containerized web application with Service Auto Scaling. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute the incoming requests.  
B. Use two Amazon EC2 instances to host the containerized web application. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute the incoming requests.  
C. Use AWS Lambda with a new code that uses one of the supported languages. Create multiple Lambda functions to support the load. Use Amazon API Gateway as an entry point to the Lambda functions.  
D. Use a high performance computing (HPC) solution such as AWS ParallelCluster to establish an HPC cluster that can process the incoming requests at the appropriate scale.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The application is already containerized, the code cannot change, and operations must be minimized. ECS on Fargate runs the existing images without managing a single server, service Auto Scaling grows the number of tasks with load, and an Application Load Balancer distributes incoming requests.  
Why B is not selected: Two machines is fixed capacity with no automatic growth, plus the burden of maintaining the instances.  
Why C is not selected: Rewriting for Lambda contradicts the requirement of minimal code changes.  
Why D is not selected: ParallelCluster is designed for high-performance computing workloads, not for handling web requests.

---

113\. A company uses 50 TB of data for reporting. The company wants to move this data from on premises to AWS. A custom application in the company’s data center runs a weekly data transformation job. The company plans to pause the application until the data transfer is complete and needs to begin the transfer process as soon as possible.  
The data center does not have any available network bandwidth for additional workloads. A solutions architect must transfer the data and must configure the transformation job to continue to run in the AWS Cloud.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Use AWS DataSync to move the data. Create a custom transformation job by using AWS Glue.  
B. Order an AWS Snowcone device to move the data. Deploy the transformation application to the device.  
C. Order an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device. Copy the data to the device. Create a custom transformation job by using AWS Glue.  
D. Order an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device that includes Amazon EC2 compute. Copy the data to the device. Create a new EC2 instance on AWS to run the transformation application.  
Answer: C  
Review status: Disputed key (alternative: D); Low-confidence audit  
Dispute note: Option C rewrites the custom application as a Glue job, while option D migrates the existing application to EC2. "Least operational overhead" cuts both ways here: Glue requires no administration but demands a full rewrite, whereas D keeps the application as-is. Snowcone (8/14 TB) can't hold 50 TB, and DataSync needs bandwidth that isn't available  
Explanation: There is no available bandwidth for transfer at all, so any network-based transfer is off the table and an offline device is required. 50 TB fits only on a Snowball Edge (about 80 TB of usable capacity); Snowcone provides 8 TB on HDD or 14 TB on SSD. The second requirement is that the transformation job must keep running once it's in the cloud. The key picks Glue: it's a managed service with no infrastructure underneath it, and that's usually how the exam interprets "least operational overhead." The disputed part is that option D keeps the existing application as-is and doesn't require rewriting it for Glue, but it hands you EC2 administration in return. Practical rule: when a question says "least operational overhead" and pits a managed service against your own server, the exam picks the managed service.  
Why A is not selected: DataSync transfers data over the network, and the scenario states plainly that there is no free bandwidth in the data center. The first half of the answer alone is impossible.  
Why B is not selected: Snowcone holds 8 TB (HDD) or 14 TB (SSD) — 50 TB physically will not fit. Also, an application running on the device does not move the transformation job into the cloud, which is exactly what's required.  
Why D is not selected: A strong alternative: the application moves over without a rewrite. But you end up with an EC2 instance that you must patch, monitor, and scale yourself — more operational overhead than a serverless Glue job.

---

114\. A company has created an image analysis application in which users can upload photos and add photo frames to their images. The users upload images and metadata to indicate which photo frames they want to add to their images. The application uses a single Amazon EC2 instance and Amazon DynamoDB to store the metadata.  
The application is becoming more popular, and the number of users is increasing. The company expects the number of concurrent users to vary significantly depending on the time of day and day of week. The company must ensure that the application can scale to meet the needs of the growing user base.  
Which solution meats these requirements?  
A. Use AWS Lambda to process the photos. Store the photos and metadata in DynamoDB.  
B. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to process the photos and to store the photos and metadata.  
C. Use AWS Lambda to process the photos. Store the photos in Amazon S3. Retain DynamoDB to store the metadata.  
D. Increase the number of EC2 instances to three. Use Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes to store the photos and metadata.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The number of users fluctuates sharply throughout the day, so an architecture that scales itself is needed. Lambda handles image processing, invoked on each upload, the images themselves are stored in S3 (object storage that grows without limits and is cheap), and the metadata stays in DynamoDB. There isn't a single instance that has to be scaled manually.  
Why A is not selected: Images cannot be stored in DynamoDB: the item size limit is 400 KB, and photos are noticeably larger.  
Why B is not selected: Firehose delivers streaming records into storage destinations, but it does not process images and is not suitable as image storage.  
Why D is not selected: Three instances is fixed capacity that does not adapt to daily fluctuations, and EBS volumes provide neither shared access nor scaling for a growing volume of photos.

---

115\. A medical records company is hosting an application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application processes customer data files that are stored on Amazon S3. The EC2 instances are hosted in public subnets. The EC2 instances access Amazon S3 over the internet, but they do not require any other network access.  
A new requirement mandates that the network traffic for file transfers take a private route and not be sent over the internet.  
Which change to the network architecture should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?  
A. Create a NAT gateway. Configure the route table for the public subnets to send traffic to Amazon S3 through the NAT gateway.  
B. Configure the security group for the EC2 instances to restrict outbound traffic so that only traffic to the S3 prefix list is permitted.  
C. Move the EC2 instances to private subnets. Create a VPC endpoint for Amazon S3, and link the endpoint to the route table for the private subnets.  
D. Remove the internet gateway from the VPC. Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection, and route traffic to Amazon S3 over the Direct Connect connection.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The requirement is that traffic to S3 must not go over the internet. The instances are moved to private subnets, and a gateway endpoint is created for S3, with a route to it added in the route table of those subnets. Traffic stays inside the AWS network, there's no charge for the endpoint, and the instances need no other network access, which matches the stated condition exactly.  
Why A is not selected: A NAT gateway is a path out to the internet: this directly violates the requirement, and it also adds a charge for processed traffic.  
Why B is not selected: A prefix list in the security group restricts where traffic can go, but the route itself stays the same — through the internet gateway.  
Why D is not selected: Direct Connect links the company's own premises to AWS. The instances are already inside AWS, so building a dedicated connection for them makes no sense.

---

116\. A company uses a popular content management system (CMS) for its corporate website. However, the required patching and maintenance are burdensome. The company is redesigning its website and wants anew solution. The website will be updated four times a year and does not need to have any dynamic content available. The solution must provide high scalability and enhanced security.  
Which combination of changes will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)  
A. Configure Amazon CloudFront in front of the website to use HTTPS functionality.  
B. Deploy an AWS WAF web ACL in front of the website to provide HTTPS functionality.  
C. Create and deploy an AWS Lambda function to manage and serve the website content.  
D. Create the new website and an Amazon S3 bucket. Deploy the website on the S3 bucket with static website hosting enabled.  
E. Create the new website. Deploy the website by using an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer.  
Answer: AD  
Explanation: The site is updated four times a year and has no dynamic content, so there's no reason to run servers at all. A static site in an S3 bucket (D) eliminates patching and maintenance, scales automatically, and costs pennies. CloudFront in front of it (A) adds HTTPS with a custom domain (certificate from ACM), caching close to the user, and the ability to attach WAF, while the bucket is locked down from direct access via an OAC. That's the least operational overhead with high scalability.  
Why B is not selected: AWS WAF filters requests, but it does not provide HTTPS and is not a TLS termination point. The option is factually wrong.  
Why C is not selected: A Lambda function for serving static content is extra code and extra invocations where S3 can serve the files directly.  
Why E is not selected: A fleet of instances behind a load balancer brings back exactly the operational burden the company is trying to escape: patching, scaling, updates.

---

117\. A company stores its application logs in an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. A new policy requires the company to store all application logs in Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service) in near-real time.  
Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Configure a CloudWatch Logs subscription to stream the logs to Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service).  
B. Create an AWS Lambda function. Use the log group to invoke the function to write the logs to Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service).  
C. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Configure the log group as the delivery streams sources. Configure Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service) as the delivery stream's destination.  
D. Install and configure Amazon Kinesis Agent on each application server to deliver the logs to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Configure Kinesis Data Streams to deliver the logs to Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service).  
Answer: A  
Explanation: CloudWatch Logs has a built-in subscription for delivering log data to OpenSearch Service: it's configured in the console and streams records in near-real time without any custom code or intermediate services.  
Why B is not selected: A custom Lambda function means delivery code, error handling, and retries that you have to maintain.  
Why C is not selected: A log group cannot be a source for a Firehose delivery stream directly: a subscription is still required, making the stream an unnecessary extra layer.  
Why D is not selected: Installing agents on every application server is the most labor-intensive path, especially since the logs are already collected in CloudWatch Logs.

---

118\. A company is building a web-based application running on Amazon EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones.  
The web application will provide access to a repository of text documents totaling about 900 TB in size. The company anticipates that the web application will experience periods of high demand. A solutions architect must ensure that the storage component for the text documents can scale to meet the demand of the application at all times. The company is concerned about the overall cost of the solution.  
Which storage solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)  
B. Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)  
C. Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service)  
D. Amazon S3  
Answer: D  
Explanation: 900 TB of text documents, accessed from a web application, with spikes in demand and an explicit cost requirement. S3 scales without any configuration, costs noticeably less per gigabyte than file or block storage, handles any number of concurrent requests, and requires no capacity planning. The application retrieves documents by key — file semantics aren't needed here.
