AWS WAF (C) filters everything that arrives, whether it carries a key or not: rules based on IP address, geography, rate-based rules against botnets, and managed rule groups. Both options stop traffic before the function is invoked, so the Lambda bill doesn't grow either.  
Why B is not selected: Filtering inside the function means you've already paid for a Lambda invocation and consumed its concurrency for every fraudulent request. Filtering needs to happen at the entry point.  
Why D is not selected: A private API is reachable only from inside a VPC — the public application would stop working for legitimate users.  
Why E is not selected: An IAM role for every visitor to a public application isn't feasible: visitors don't have AWS accounts.

---

160\. An ecommerce company hosts its analytics application in the AWS Cloud. The application generates about 300 MB of data each month. The data is stored in JSON format. The company is evaluating a disaster recovery solution to back up the data. The data must be accessible in milliseconds if it is needed, and the data must be kept for 30 days.  
Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service)  
B. Amazon S3 Glacier  
C. Amazon S3 Standard  
D. Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The volume is tiny — 300 MB a month — the data must be kept for 30 days, and access must be in milliseconds. The S3 Standard storage class gives instant access and costs only cents at this volume, while the minimum storage durations and retrieval fees of the archival classes make them uneconomical over a one-month horizon.  
Why A is not selected: OpenSearch is a search cluster billed for continuously running nodes: disproportionately expensive for a backup.  
Why B is not selected: Glacier is cheaper to store in, but retrieval takes minutes to hours, while the requirement is milliseconds.  
Why D is not selected: An RDS for PostgreSQL database is billed hourly and is designed for queries, not for storing JSON file backups.

---

161\. A company has a small Python application that processes JSON documents and outputs the results to an on- premises SQL database. The application runs thousands of times each day. The company wants to move the application to the AWS Cloud. The company needs a highly available solution that maximizes scalability and minimizes operational overhead.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Place the JSON documents in an Amazon S3 bucket. Run the Python code on multiple Amazon EC2 instances to process the documents. Store the results in an Amazon Aurora DB cluster.  
B. Place the JSON documents in an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function that runs the Python code to process the documents as they arrive in the S3 bucket. Store the results in an Amazon Aurora DB cluster.  
C. Place the JSON documents in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Use the EBS Multi- Attach feature to attach the volume to multiple Amazon EC2 instances. Run the Python code on the EC2 instances to process the documents. Store the results on an Amazon RDS DB instance.  
D. Place the JSON documents in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as messages. Deploy the Python code as a container on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that is configured with the Amazon EC2 launch type. Use the container to process the SQS messages. Store the results on an Amazon RDS DB instance.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The application is small, runs thousands of times a day, and is triggered by each document's arrival. A Lambda function invoked by an S3 event notification delivers high availability, scalability, and near-zero operational overhead all at once: you pay only for actual execution time. The results are written into a managed Aurora DB cluster.  
Why A is not selected: A fleet of instances is billed around the clock, has to be patched and scaled, and is a poor fit for thousands of short invocations a day.  
Why C is not selected: EBS Multi-Attach is limited to a single Availability Zone and requires a cluster-aware file system: this is the most complex and least scalable of the options.  
Why D is not selected: An ECS cluster on the EC2 launch type still means managing compute nodes, while the workload is a perfect fit for serverless, event-driven execution.

---

162\. A company wants to use high performance computing (HPC) infrastructure on AWS for financial risk modeling. The company’s HPC workloads run on Linux. Each HPC workflow runs on hundreds of Amazon EC2 Spot Instances, is short-lived, and generates thousands of output files that are ultimately stored in persistent storage for analytics and long-term future use.  
The company seeks a cloud storage solution that permits the copying of on-premises data to long-term persistent storage to make data available for processing by all EC2 instances. The solution should also be a high performance file system that is integrated with persistent storage to read and write datasets and output files.  
Which combination of AWS services meets these requirements?  
A. Amazon FSx for Lustre integrated with Amazon S3  
B. Amazon FSx for Windows File Server integrated with Amazon S3  
C. Amazon S3 Glacier integrated with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)  
D. Amazon S3 bucket with a VPC endpoint integrated with an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) General Purpose SSD (gp2) volume  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Two related things are needed: a high-performance file system for hundreds of instances, and persistent storage where the results land long-term. Amazon FSx for Lustre integrates directly with S3: a bucket is linked to the file system, its objects appear as files, and job output is exported back to S3. This is the standard pattern for HPC workloads on interruptible instances — the file system lives independently of the ephemeral fleet.  
Why B is not selected: FSx for Windows File Server uses the SMB protocol and is built for Windows workloads, while the computations run on Linux and need Lustre-level performance.  
Why C is not selected: Glacier is an archive with retrieval measured in minutes to hours, so it can't serve as working storage for computations, and EBS volumes can't be shared across hundreds of instances.  
Why D is not selected: S3 by itself isn't a file system, and a gp2 EBS volume attaches to a single instance: hundreds of machines can't work with it at the same time.

---

163\. A company is building a containerized application on premises and decides to move the application to AWS. The application will have thousands of users soon after it is deployed. The company is unsure how to manage the deployment of containers at scale. The company needs to deploy the containerized application in a highly available architecture that minimizes operational overhead.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Store container images in an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Use an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with the AWS Fargate launch type to run the containers. Use target tracking to scale automatically based on demand.  
B. Store container images in an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Use an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with the Amazon EC2 launch type to run the containers. Use target tracking to scale automatically based on demand.  
C. Store container images in a repository that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. Run the containers on EC2 instances that are spread across multiple Availability Zones. Monitor the average CPU utilization in Amazon CloudWatch. Launch new EC2 instances as needed.  
D. Create an Amazon EC2 Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that contains the container image. Launch EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Use an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to scale out EC2 instances when the average CPU utilization threshold is breached.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: What's needed is image storage, orchestration without managing nodes, and automatic scaling. Container images are stored in Amazon ECR, an ECS cluster with the AWS Fargate launch type runs the containers without a single instance to manage, and a target tracking policy scales automatically with demand. High availability comes from spreading tasks across multiple Availability Zones.  
Why B is not selected: The Amazon EC2 launch type brings node management back: patching, scaling, and monitoring fall on the team.  
Why C is not selected: A self-hosted registry on an EC2 instance and manually launching new instances as needed is maximum operational effort and risk.  
Why D is not selected: Packing the container image into an AMI and scaling EC2 instances manually means giving up container orchestration entirely.

---

164\. A company has two applications: a sender application that sends messages with payloads to be processed and a processing application intended to receive the messages with payloads. The company wants to implement an AWS service to handle messages between the two applications. The sender application can send about 1,000 messages each hour. The messages may take up to 2 days to be processed: If the messages fail to process, they must be retained so that they do not impact the processing of any remaining messages.  
Which solution meets these requirements and is the MOST operationally efficient?  
A. Set up an Amazon EC2 instance running a Redis database. Configure both applications to use the instance. Store, process, and delete the messages, respectively.  
B. Use an Amazon Kinesis data stream to receive the messages from the sender application. Integrate the processing application with the Kinesis Client Library (KCL).  
C. Integrate the sender and processor applications with an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure a dead-letter queue to collect the messages that failed to process.  
D. Subscribe the processing application to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to receive notifications to process. Integrate the sender application to write to the SNS topic.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: About a thousand messages an hour, processing that can take up to two days, and a requirement to keep failed messages from affecting the rest — this is the classic use case for an Amazon SQS queue. Its message retention period goes up to 14 days, comfortably covering the two-day processing window, and a dead-letter queue collects the messages that failed to process without blocking the remaining messages.  
Why A is not selected: A self-managed Redis instance is a machine you have to operate, plus store/process/delete logic you'd have to build yourself.  
Why B is not selected: Kinesis is built for streaming processing in sequence; it has no built-in way to isolate and separately retain individual failed records, and integrating the KCL requires writing your own consumer code.  
Why D is not selected: SNS delivers a notification immediately and doesn't hold it for two days: if the subscriber is unavailable, the message is lost.

---

165\. A solutions architect must design a solution that uses Amazon CloudFront with an Amazon S3 origin to store a static website. The company’s security policy requires that all website traffic be inspected by AWS WAF.  
How should the solutions architect comply with these requirements?  
A. Configure an S3 bucket policy to accept requests coming from the AWS WAF Amazon Resource Name (ARN) only.  
B. Configure Amazon CloudFront to forward all incoming requests to AWS WAF before requesting content from the S3 origin.  
C. Configure a security group that allows Amazon CloudFront IP addresses to access Amazon S3 only. Associate AWS WAF to CloudFront.  
D. Configure Amazon CloudFront and Amazon S3 to use an origin access identity (OAI) to restrict access to the S3 bucket. Enable AWS WAF on the distribution.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: For all website traffic to actually pass through WAF inspection, two conditions must hold. First, WAF is enabled on the CloudFront distribution itself (a web ACL) — this way every request is inspected at the edge location. Second, direct access to the bucket must be blocked, otherwise requests could bypass CloudFront and WAF entirely; this is done with an origin access identity (today, origin access control), with the bucket policy allowing reads only from it.  
Why A is not selected: AWS WAF has no ARN principal that can be referenced in a bucket policy: it never talks to the origin. It's CloudFront that makes the requests to S3.  
Why B is not selected: CloudFront doesn't "forward requests to WAF": a web ACL is associated with the distribution and inspects requests on the spot, before the origin is contacted.  
Why C is not selected: Security groups don't apply to Amazon S3 — it's a service with a public API. Restricting access to CloudFront's IP addresses isn't built that way.

---

166\. Organizers for a global event want to put daily reports online as static HTML pages. The pages are expected to generate millions of views from users around the world. The files are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. A solutions architect has been asked to design an efficient and effective solution.  
Which action should the solutions architect take to accomplish this?  
A. Generate presigned URLs for the files.  
B. Use cross-Region replication to all Regions.  
C. Use the geoproximity feature of Amazon Route 53.  
D. Use Amazon CloudFront with the S3 bucket as its origin.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: Millions of views of the same static pages is the classic use case for a CDN. CloudFront with the S3 bucket as its origin caches the pages at edge locations, so the vast majority of requests never reach the bucket: latency drops, outbound data transfer cost drops, and load on the origin drops. The bucket is also locked down from direct access via origin access control.  
Why A is not selected: A presigned URL is a mechanism for temporary access to private objects. It doesn't speed up delivery and doesn't fit public pages.  
Why B is not selected: Cross-Region replication to every Region means paying for many copies of storage and manually managing routing, while a CDN cache achieves the same result more cheaply.  
Why C is not selected: The geoproximity feature of Route 53 distributes users across multiple origins, but here there's only one origin, and this routing policy provides no caching.

---

167\. A company runs a production application on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The application reads the data from an Amazon SQS queue and processes the messages in parallel. The message volume is unpredictable and often has intermittent traffic. This application should continually process messages without any downtime.  
Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Use Spot Instances exclusively to handle the maximum capacity required.  
B. Use Reserved Instances exclusively to handle the maximum capacity required.  
C. Use Reserved Instances for the baseline capacity and use Spot Instances to handle additional capacity.  
D. Use Reserved Instances for the baseline capacity and use On-Demand Instances to handle additional capacity.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: The application must keep processing without any downtime, and traffic is unpredictable and often intermittent. The steady baseline is covered by discounted Reserved Instances, and spikes are handled by On-Demand Instances, which can't be reclaimed. Interruptible capacity doesn't fit here: the "no downtime" requirement is incompatible with instances that can be reclaimed at any time.  
Why A is not selected: Spot Instances for the entire maximum capacity risk a simultaneous reclaim that halts processing.  
Why B is not selected: Reserving the entire maximum capacity year-round means overpaying for capacity that's only needed some of the time.  
Why C is not selected: Cheaper, but Spot Instances again conflict with the requirement to process messages continuously without downtime.

---

168\. A security team wants to limit access to specific services or actions in all of the team’s AWS accounts. All accounts belong to a large organization in AWS Organizations. The solution must be scalable and there must be a single point where permissions can be maintained.  
What should a solutions architect do to accomplish this?  
A. Create an ACL to provide access to the services or actions.  
B. Create a security group to allow accounts and attach it to user groups.  
C. Create cross-account roles in each account to deny access to the services or actions.  
D. Create a service control policy in the root organizational unit to deny access to the services or actions.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: The goal is to restrict a set of services and actions across every account in the organization, from a single point, in a way a local administrator can't undo. That's exactly what a service control policy does: an SCP is attached to the organization's root (or an OU) and sets a permissions ceiling for every principal in every member account, including that account's root user. The key mechanic to understand: an SCP never grants anything — it only restricts. Effective permissions are the intersection of the SCP and the IAM policies.  
Why A is not selected: An ACL in AWS refers to network subnet access control lists, plus a legacy S3 access mechanism. Neither can manage service-level permissions across every account.  
Why B is not selected: A security group filters network traffic to instances. It has nothing to do with permissions for API calls.  
Why C is not selected: Cross-account roles would have to be created and maintained in every single account, and they don't stop local administrators from acting directly. There's no single point of control.

---

169\. A company is concerned about the security of its public web application due to recent web attacks. The application uses an Application Load Balancer (ALB). A solutions architect must reduce the risk of DDoS attacks against the application.  
What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement?  
A. Add an Amazon Inspector agent to the ALB.  
B. Configure Amazon Macie to prevent attacks.  
C. Enable AWS Shield Advanced to prevent attacks.  
D. Configure Amazon GuardDuty to monitor the ALB.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The requirement is direct: reduce the risk of DDoS attacks against the application behind the ALB. AWS Shield Advanced is subscribed to the resources you want protected (ALB, CloudFront, Global Accelerator, Route 53, Elastic IP), and it provides automatic mitigations at the network and application layers, access to the DDoS Response Team, and cost protection against a billing spike during an attack. Shield Standard is already active regardless, but without these advanced capabilities.  
Why A is not selected: Amazon Inspector scans instances and images for vulnerabilities; it has no "agent" that attaches to a load balancer and provides no protection against attacks.  
Why B is not selected: Amazon Macie looks for sensitive data in S3. It has nothing to do with DDoS protection.  
Why D is not selected: GuardDuty detects suspicious activity, but it doesn't absorb attack traffic.

---

170\. A company’s web application is running on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The company recently changed its policy, which now requires the application to be accessed from one specific country only.  
Which configuration will meet this requirement?  
A. Configure the security group for the EC2 instances.  
B. Configure the security group on the Application Load Balancer.  
C. Configure AWS WAF on the Application Load Balancer in a VPC.  
D. Configure the network ACL for the subnet that contains the EC2 instances.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: Restricting access to one specific country is an application-layer rule, because the country is determined from the source IP address using a geolocation database. AWS WAF has exactly this capability: a geo match statement blocks or allows requests from selected countries, and the web ACL is attached to the Application Load Balancer. Security groups and network ACLs operate on address ranges and ports and know nothing about countries — manually maintaining the subnet list for an entire country isn't realistic.  
Why A is not selected: The EC2 instances' security group receives traffic from the load balancer, not from clients, and it works with CIDR ranges, not countries.  
Why B is not selected: The load balancer's security group also operates on address ranges: listing every subnet for a country in it is not feasible.  
Why D is not selected: A network ACL is an address-and-port filter at the subnet level with a hard limit on the number of rules. Geo-blocking can't be built with it.

---

171\. A company provides an API to its users that automates inquiries for tax computations based on item prices. The company experiences a larger number of inquiries during the holiday season only that cause slower response times. A solutions architect needs to design a solution that is scalable and elastic.  
What should the solutions architect do to accomplish this?  
A. Provide an API hosted on an Amazon EC2 instance. The EC2 instance performs the required computations when the API request is made.  
B. Design a REST API using Amazon API Gateway that accepts the item names. API Gateway passes item names to AWS Lambda for tax computations.  
C. Create an Application Load Balancer that has two Amazon EC2 instances behind it. The EC2 instances will compute the tax on the received item names.  
D. Design a REST API using Amazon API Gateway that connects with an API hosted on an Amazon EC2 instance. API Gateway accepts and passes the item names to the EC2 instance for tax computations.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: Load spikes sharply during the holiday season and is nearly nonexistent the rest of the time. API Gateway with Lambda functions scales instantly and is billed only for actual invocations: no capacity planning and no idle servers.  
Why A is not selected: A single instance doesn't scale at all and becomes a bottleneck during the season.  
Why C is not selected: Two machines behind a load balancer represent fixed capacity that either can't handle the peak or sits idle the rest of the year.  
Why D is not selected: Putting API Gateway in front of the instance only adds a layer: computation is still bottlenecked on a single machine.

---

172\. A solutions architect is creating a new Amazon CloudFront distribution for an application. Some of the information submitted by users is sensitive. The application uses HTTPS but needs another layer of security. The sensitive information should.be protected throughout the entire application stack, and access to the information should be restricted to certain applications.  
Which action should the solutions architect take?  
A. Configure a CloudFront signed URL.  
B. Configure a CloudFront signed cookie.  
C. Configure a CloudFront field-level encryption profile.  
D. Configure CloudFront and set the Origin Protocol Policy setting to HTTPS Only for the Viewer Protocol Policy.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: HTTPS only protects data in transit: at the load balancer and onward through the stack, it's decrypted again. CloudFront field-level encryption encrypts specific form fields with a public key right at the edge location, so sensitive values stay encrypted throughout the entire path, and only the application holding the matching private key can decrypt them.  
Why A is not selected: A signed URL restricts access to the distribution's content but does nothing to protect the data the user submits.  
Why B is not selected: Signed cookies solve the same content-access-restriction problem and have nothing to do with field-level encryption.  
Why D is not selected: Protocol settings only provide encryption in transit — the same layer that's already present in the scenario and already deemed insufficient.

---

173\. A gaming company hosts a browser-based application on AWS. The users of the application consume a large number of videos and images that are stored in Amazon S3. This content is the same for all users.  
The application has increased in popularity, and millions of users worldwide accessing these media files. The company wants to provide the files to the users while reducing the load on the origin.  
Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Deploy an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator in front of the web servers.  
B. Deploy an Amazon CloudFront web distribution in front of the S3 bucket.  
C. Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis instance in front of the web servers.  
D. Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached instance in front of the web servers.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The files are the same for every user, the audience is global, load on the origin must be reduced, and cost matters. CloudFront in front of the bucket caches objects at edge locations, so the vast majority of requests never reach S3: both the load and the outbound-traffic cost drop, since traffic served from CloudFront is cheaper than traffic served directly from S3.  
Why A is not selected: Global Accelerator optimizes the network path but doesn't cache objects: the load on the origin stays the same.  
Why C is not selected: Redis caches data in memory within a single Region and isn't built to serve large media files to a global audience.  
Why D is not selected: Memcached has the same drawback: it's a regional in-memory cache, not a content delivery network.

---

174\. A company has a multi-tier application that runs six front-end web servers in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group in a single Availability Zone behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). A solutions architect needs to modify the infrastructure to be highly available without modifying the application.  
Which architecture should the solutions architect choose that provides high availability?  
A. Create an Auto Scaling group that uses three instances across each of two Regions.  
B. Modify the Auto Scaling group to use three instances across each of two Availability Zones.  
C. Create an Auto Scaling template that can be used to quickly create more instances in another Region.  
D. Change the ALB in front of the Amazon EC2 instances in a round-robin configuration to balance traffic to the web tier.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The single weakness is that all six machines sit in one Availability Zone. It's enough to spread the Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones, three instances in each: the load balancer already works across multiple zones, the application doesn't need to change, and a zone failure leaves half the capacity running.  
Why A is not selected: Multiple Regions solve a different problem and require rebuilding routing and data replication — more than what's needed, and it touches the application.  
Why C is not selected: A template for quickly creating instances in another Region is a recovery plan, not high availability.  
Why D is not selected: The Application Load Balancer already distributes requests; the distribution algorithm doesn't help when the single zone fails.

---

175\. An ecommerce company has an order-processing application that uses Amazon API Gateway and an AWS Lambda function. The application stores data in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database. During a recent sales event, a sudden surge in customer orders occurred. Some customers experienced timeouts, and the application did not process the orders of those customers.  
A solutions architect determined that the CPU utilization and memory utilization were high on the database because of a large number of open connections. The solutions architect needs to prevent the timeout errors while making the least possible changes to the application.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Configure provisioned concurrency for the Lambda function. Modify the database to be a global database in multiple AWS Regions.  
B. Use Amazon RDS Proxy to create a proxy for the database. Modify the Lambda function to use the RDS Proxy endpoint instead of the database endpoint.  
C. Create a read replica for the database in a different AWS Region. Use query string parameters in API Gateway to route traffic to the read replica.  
D. Migrate the data from Aurora PostgreSQL to Amazon DynamoDB by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Modify the Lambda function to use the DynamoDB table.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The diagnosis is given right in the scenario: too many open connections to the database. During a spike, Lambda spins up hundreds of concurrent instances, each opening its own connection, and Aurora chokes. RDS Proxy maintains a pool of persistent connections and reuses them across function invocations — the change amounts to swapping the endpoint address used by the function.  
Why A is not selected: Provisioned concurrency speeds up cold starts but doesn't reduce the number of connections, and a global database solves an entirely different problem — cross-Region disaster recovery.  
Why C is not selected: A read replica won't help: the problem is connections, including for writes, and routing by query string parameters in API Gateway means reworking the application.  
Why D is not selected: Moving to DynamoDB means rewriting the data model and every query, which directly conflicts with the requirement for minimal changes.

---

176\. An application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets. The application needs to access an Amazon DynamoDB table.  
What is the MOST secure way to access the table while ensuring that the traffic does not leave the AWS network?  
A. Use a VPC endpoint for DynamoDB.  
B. Use a NAT gateway in a public subnet.  
C. Use a NAT instance in a private subnet.  
D. Use the internet gateway attached to the VPC.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Private access to DynamoDB comes from a gateway endpoint: a route to the service prefix is added to the private subnets' route table, traffic never leaves the AWS network, and the endpoint policy restricts access to the required tables. There's no charge for the endpoint itself.  
Why B is not selected: A NAT gateway sends traffic out to the internet — that violates the requirement to stay within the AWS network, and it adds a charge for processed data.  
Why C is not selected: A NAT instance sits in a public subnet and still routes traffic out to the internet; it doesn't even work from a private subnet.  
Why D is not selected: An internet gateway is a direct path to the internet — the opposite of the requirement.

---

177\. An entertainment company is using Amazon DynamoDB to store media metadata. The application is read intensive and experiencing delays. The company does not have staff to handle additional operational overhead and needs to improve the performance efficiency of DynamoDB without reconfiguring the application.  
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?  
A. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.  
B. Use Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX).  
C. Replicate data by using DynamoDB global tables.  
D. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached with Auto Discovery enabled.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The application can't be rewritten, the workload is read-heavy, and latency needs to go away without adding operational overhead. DynamoDB Accelerator is a cache built directly into the service: it's API-compatible with DynamoDB, so pointing to the cluster endpoint is enough, and reads start being served in microseconds.  
Why A is not selected: Redis would require rewriting the data-access logic and managing cache invalidation yourself.  
Why C is not selected: Global tables solve multi-Region operation, not read latency within a single Region.  
Why D is not selected: Memcached also requires application changes and managing the cache yourself.

---

178\. A company’s infrastructure consists of Amazon EC2 instances and an Amazon RDS DB instance in a single AWS Region. The company wants to back up its data in a separate Region.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Use AWS Backup to copy EC2 backups and RDS backups to the separate Region.  
B. Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM) to copy EC2 backups and RDS backups to the separate Region.  
C. Create Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) of the EC2 instances. Copy the AMIs to the separate Region. Create a read replica for the RDS DB instance in the separate Region.  
D. Create Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots. Copy the EBS snapshots to the separate Region. Create RDS snapshots. Export the RDS snapshots to Amazon S3. Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) to the separate Region.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Copies are needed in another Region for two different services with minimal operations. AWS Backup supports both EC2 and RDS, defines a single plan with a cross-Region copy rule, and shows the status of every job in one place. No scripts and no separate mechanism per service.  
Why B is not selected: Amazon DLM manages EBS snapshots and AMIs, but RDS backups are outside its scope.  
Why C is not selected: Manually copying AMIs plus a cross-Region read replica means a database instance running continuously and manual steps — more work and more cost.  
Why D is not selected: Four different mechanisms (snapshots, copying, export, bucket replication) instead of one plan — maximum operational load.

---

179\. A solutions architect needs to securely store a database user name and password that an application uses to access an Amazon RDS DB instance. The application that accesses the database runs on an Amazon EC2 instance.  
The solutions architect wants to create a secure parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store.  
What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement?  
A. Create an IAM role that has read access to the Parameter Store parameter. Allow Decrypt access to an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key that is used to encrypt the parameter. Assign this IAM role to the EC2 instance.  
B. Create an IAM policy that allows read access to the Parameter Store parameter. Allow Decrypt access to an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key that is used to encrypt the parameter. Assign this IAM policy to the EC2 instance.  
C. Create an IAM trust relationship between the Parameter Store parameter and the EC2 instance. Specify Amazon RDS as a principal in the trust policy.  
D. Create an IAM trust relationship between the DB instance and the EC2 instance. Specify Systems Manager as a principal in the trust policy.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: This tests understanding of how a compute resource gets permissions. An instance is assigned an IAM role (through the instance profile), and a policy is attached to that role — a policy can't be assigned directly to an instance. The second nuance: a SecureString parameter is encrypted with a KMS key, so ssm:GetParameter alone isn't enough — the role also needs kms:Decrypt on that key, otherwise the read fails with an access error. That exact pair of permissions is what the correct option describes.  
Why B is not selected: An IAM policy can't be "assigned to an instance": policies attach to users, groups, and roles, and an instance is granted a role. The wording describes an operation that doesn't exist.  
Why C is not selected: A trust relationship is set up between a role and the principal that assumes it. "Trust between a parameter and an instance," with RDS named as the principal, is a construct that doesn't exist in IAM.  
Why D is not selected: Same mistake: a role's trust policy doesn't link a database instance to an application instance, and Systems Manager isn't a principal that assumes a role here.

---

180\. A company is designing a cloud communications platform that is driven by APIs. The application is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB). The company uses Amazon API Gateway to provide external users with access to the application through APIs. The company wants to protect the platform against web exploits like SQL injection and also wants to detect and mitigate large, sophisticated DDoS attacks.  
Which combination of solutions provides the MOST protection? (Choose two.)  
A. Use AWS WAF to protect the NLB.  
B. Use AWS Shield Advanced with the NLB.  
C. Use AWS WAF to protect Amazon API Gateway.  
D. Use Amazon GuardDuty with AWS Shield Standard  
E. Use AWS Shield Standard with Amazon API Gateway.  
Answer: BC  
Explanation: Protection is needed on two different fronts. SQL injection and XSS are HTTP-layer attacks, and AWS WAF filters those — a web ACL can be attached to API Gateway (C), since WAF doesn't attach to a Network Load Balancer. Large, sophisticated DDoS attacks call for Shield Advanced, which does support NLB and Elastic IP addresses (B), providing automatic mitigations and support from the DDoS Response Team. That gives the pair "WAF on API Gateway plus Shield Advanced on the NLB."  
Why A is not selected: AWS WAF doesn't support Network Load Balancer: the list of supported resources is limited to CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, AppSync, Cognito, and a few others.  
Why D is not selected: GuardDuty only detects, and Shield Standard is enabled by default and doesn't provide the protection against sophisticated attacks that the scenario requires.  
Why E is not selected: Shield Standard operates automatically and isn't a separately configurable solution, and it provides no protection against injection attacks at all.

---

181\. A company has a legacy data processing application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. Data is processed sequentially, but the order of results does not matter. The application uses a monolithic architecture. The only way that the company can scale the application to meet increased demand is to increase the size of the instances.  
The company’s developers have decided to rewrite the application to use a microservices architecture on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS).  
What should a solutions architect recommend for communication between the microservices?  
A. Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Add code to the data producers, and send data to the queue. Add code to the data consumers to process data from the queue.  
B. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Add code to the data producers, and publish notifications to the topic. Add code to the data consumers to subscribe to the topic.  
C. Create an AWS Lambda function to pass messages. Add code to the data producers to call the Lambda function with a data object. Add code to the data consumers to receive a data object that is passed from the Lambda function.  
D. Create an Amazon DynamoDB table. Enable DynamoDB Streams. Add code to the data producers to insert data into the table. Add code to the data consumers to use the DynamoDB Streams API to detect new table entries and retrieve the data.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Data is processed sequentially, but the order of results doesn't matter, and there will be many consumers. An SQS queue fits exactly this: producers place messages, consumers pull them independently and scale with the queue length, each message is processed once, and a failure puts it back on the queue.  
Why B is not selected: SNS delivers a copy of the message to every subscriber: that doesn't work for distributing work across consumers, and there's no buffering.  
Why C is not selected: A function acting as a go-between for services adds a synchronous dependency and a point of failure instead of decoupling.  
Why D is not selected: DynamoDB Streams could be adapted, but that means an extra table, extra cost, and noticeably more complex logic than a queue.

---

182\. A company wants to migrate its MySQL database from on premises to AWS. The company recently experienced a database outage that significantly impacted the business. To ensure this does not happen again, the company wants a reliable database solution on AWS that minimizes data loss and stores every transaction on at least two nodes.  
Which solution meets these requirements?  
A. Create an Amazon RDS DB instance with synchronous replication to three nodes in three Availability Zones.  
B. Create an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance with Multi-AZ functionality enabled to synchronously replicate the data.  
C. Create an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance and then create a read replica in a separate AWS Region that synchronously replicates the data.  
D. Create an Amazon EC2 instance with a MySQL engine installed that triggers an AWS Lambda function to synchronously replicate the data to an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The requirement that "every transaction is stored on at least two nodes" means synchronous replication. RDS for MySQL's Multi-AZ configuration synchronously writes every transaction to a standby instance in another Availability Zone and fails over automatically.  
Why A is not selected: RDS has no synchronous three-node, three-zone replication mode for MySQL: that configuration doesn't exist.  
Why C is not selected: Cross-Region read replicas replicate asynchronously: the word "synchronously" in this option is wrong.  
Why D is not selected: Homegrown replication through a Lambda function is never synchronous and adds both complexity and points of failure.

---

183\. A company is building a new dynamic ordering website. The company wants to minimize server maintenance and patching. The website must be highly available and must scale read and write capacity as quickly as possible to meet changes in user demand.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Host static content in Amazon S3. Host dynamic content by using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. Use Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity for the database. Configure Amazon CloudFront to deliver the website content.  
B. Host static content in Amazon S3. Host dynamic content by using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. Use Amazon Aurora with Aurora Auto Scaling for the database. Configure Amazon CloudFront to deliver the website content.  
C. Host all the website content on Amazon EC2 instances. Create an Auto Scaling group to scale the EC2 instances. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic. Use Amazon DynamoDB with provisioned write capacity for the database.  
D. Host all the website content on Amazon EC2 instances. Create an Auto Scaling group to scale the EC2 instances. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic. Use Amazon Aurora with Aurora Auto Scaling for the database.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Minimal server maintenance is required, along with the fastest possible scaling of both read and write capacity. This is a fully serverless stack: static content in S3, dynamic content through API Gateway and Lambda, data in DynamoDB in on-demand mode, delivery through CloudFront. On-demand mode adjusts both writes and reads instantly, with no capacity planning.  
Why B is not selected: Aurora Auto Scaling adds read replicas, but writes remain on a single primary instance and don't scale up quickly.  
Why C is not selected: EC2 instances require maintenance and patching, and DynamoDB provisioned write capacity doesn't adjust instantly.  
Why D is not selected: This has both servers to maintain and Aurora's write-scaling limitation.

---

184\. A company has an AWS account used for software engineering. The AWS account has access to the company’s on- premises data center through a pair of AWS Direct Connect connections. All non-VPC traffic routes to the virtual private gateway.  
A development team recently created an AWS Lambda function through the console. The development team needs to allow the function to access a database that runs in a private subnet in the company’s data center.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Configure the Lambda function to run in the VPC with the appropriate security group.  
B. Set up a VPN connection from AWS to the data center. Route the traffic from the Lambda function through the VPN.  
C. Update the route tables in the VPC to allow the Lambda function to access the on-premises data center through Direct Connect.  
D. Create an Elastic IP address. Configure the Lambda function to send traffic through the Elastic IP address without an elastic network interface.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: By default, a Lambda function has no access to private networks — it runs inside the AWS-managed service network. To reach the database in the data center, the function must be connected to the VPC: subnets and a security group are specified, and a network interface is then created in those subnets. From there, the existing routing takes over — all traffic leaving the VPC goes to the virtual private gateway and through Direct Connect to the data center.  
Why B is not selected: The Direct Connect links already exist, and a function outside the VPC couldn't use a new VPN either: the problem isn't a missing link, it's that the function isn't connected to the network.  
Why C is not selected: The VPC route tables already send all non-VPC traffic to the virtual private gateway. As long as the function isn't in the VPC, those routes don't apply to it.  
Why D is not selected: An Elastic IP address is a public address, and the phrase "without a network interface" describes a capability that doesn't exist: Lambda's access to a private network comes specifically from an interface in the VPC.

---

185\. A company runs an application using Amazon ECS. The application creates resized versions of an original image and then makes Amazon S3 API calls to store the resized images in Amazon S3.  
How can a solutions architect ensure that the application has permission to access Amazon S3?  
A. Update the S3 role in AWS IAM to allow read/write access from Amazon ECS, and then relaunch the container.  
B. Create an IAM role with S3 permissions, and then specify that role as the taskRoleArn in the task definition.  
C. Create a security group that allows access from Amazon ECS to Amazon S3, and update the launch configuration used by the ECS cluster.  
D. Create an IAM user with S3 permissions, and then relaunch the Amazon EC2 instances for the ECS cluster while logged in as this account.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: An ECS task has two distinct roles, and this question checks that you can tell them apart. The task execution role is used by the agent: to pull the image from ECR and write logs to CloudWatch. The task role is the role of the application itself running in the container, and it's the one specified as taskRoleArn in the task definition; the container obtains temporary credentials through it and calls S3. Keys never end up in the image, and rotation happens automatically.  
Why A is not selected: "Update the S3 role to allow access from Amazon ECS" describes a construct that doesn't exist: the service doesn't call the bucket on its own behalf — permissions belong to the task role.  
Why C is not selected: A security group controls network traffic, not permissions for S3 API calls. Access would still be denied on permissions grounds.  
Why D is not selected: An IAM user and launching instances "under that account" isn't the right mechanism: the container gets its permissions from the task role, and long-lived keys aren't needed in this model.

---

186\. A company has a Windows-based application that must be migrated to AWS. The application requires the use of a shared Windows file system attached to multiple Amazon EC2 Windows instances that are deployed across multiple Availability Zone:  
What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?  
A. Configure AWS Storage Gateway in volume gateway mode. Mount the volume to each Windows instance.  
B. Configure Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. Mount the Amazon FSx file system to each Windows instance.  
C. Configure a file system by using Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Mount the EFS file system to each Windows instance.  
D. Configure an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume with the required size. Attach each EC2 instance to the volume. Mount the file system within the volume to each Windows instance.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: A shared Windows file share for instances across multiple Availability Zones is Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. It speaks the SMB protocol, supports Windows ACLs and Active Directory integration, deploys in a Multi-AZ configuration, and mounts on every instance as an ordinary network drive.  
Why A is not selected: Volume Gateway serves block volumes over iSCSI and is meant for hybrid scenarios, not shared file access for multiple instances in the cloud.  
Why C is not selected: EFS speaks NFS: that's not the native access method for Windows applications and instances, and it has no support for Windows ACLs.  
Why D is not selected: An EBS volume generally attaches to a single instance, and a file system on it isn't designed for simultaneous writes from multiple machines, let alone from different Availability Zones.

---

187\. A company is developing an ecommerce application that will consist of a load-balanced front end, a container- based application, and a relational database. A solutions architect needs to create a highly available solution that operates with as little manual intervention as possible.  
Which solutions meet these requirements? (Choose two.)  
A. Create an Amazon RDS DB instance in Multi-AZ mode.  
B. Create an Amazon RDS DB instance and one or more replicas in another Availability Zone.  
C. Create an Amazon EC2 instance-based Docker cluster to handle the dynamic application load.  
D. Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with a Fargate launch type to handle the dynamic application load.  
E. Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with an Amazon EC2 launch type to handle the dynamic application load.  
Answer: AD  
Explanation: Both tiers need to be highly available with as little manual intervention as possible. The database — RDS in Multi-AZ configuration, with synchronous replication and automatic failover (A). The containers — an ECS cluster with the Fargate launch type, where there are no nodes to maintain and tasks are spread across Availability Zones (D).  
Why B is not selected: Read replicas don't fail over automatically and are meant to offload reads, not to provide fault tolerance.  
Why C is not selected: A self-managed Docker cluster on instances means nodes that have to be maintained and scaled manually.  
Why E is not selected: The EC2 launch type works, but it requires managing nodes, while the scenario calls for minimal manual intervention.

---

188\. A company uses Amazon S3 as its data lake. The company has a new partner that must use SFTP to upload data files. A solutions architect needs to implement a highly available SFTP solution that minimizes operational overhead.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Use AWS Transfer Family to configure an SFTP-enabled server with a publicly accessible endpoint. Choose the S3 data lake as the destination.  
B. Use Amazon S3 File Gateway as an SFTP server. Expose the S3 File Gateway endpoint URL to the new partner. Share the S3 File Gateway endpoint with the new partner.  
C. Launch an Amazon EC2 instance in a private subnet in a VPInstruct the new partner to upload files to the EC2 instance by using a VPN. Run a cron job script, on the EC2 instance to upload files to the S3 data lake.  
D. Launch Amazon EC2 instances in a private subnet in a VPC. Place a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in front of the EC2 instances. Create an SFTP listener port for the NLB. Share the NLB hostname with the new partner. Run a cron job script on the EC2 instances to upload files to the S3 data lake.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The partner needs the SFTP protocol, and the solution must be highly available with minimal operations. AWS Transfer Family is a managed service: it stands up an SFTP endpoint, provides availability across multiple zones on its own, and drops files straight into the data lake bucket. No servers, no scripts.  
Why B is not selected: S3 File Gateway isn't an SFTP server: it serves resources over NFS and SMB and is meant for local-network use.  
Why C is not selected: A single instance is a single point of failure, plus a self-managed SFTP server, a VPN, and a scheduled script that has to be maintained.  
Why D is not selected: A fleet of instances behind a load balancer adds availability, but all the operational burden of the SFTP servers and the upload scripts still falls on the company.

---

189\. A company needs to store contract documents. A contract lasts for 5 years. During the 5-year period, the company must ensure that the documents cannot be overwritten or deleted. The company needs to encrypt the documents at rest and rotate the encryption keys automatically every year.  
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)  
A. Store the documents in Amazon S3. Use S3 Object Lock in governance mode.  
B. Store the documents in Amazon S3. Use S3 Object Lock in compliance mode.  
C. Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3). Configure key rotation.  
D. Use server-side encryption with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed keys. Configure key rotation.  
E. Use server-side encryption with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer provided (imported) keys. Configure key rotation.  
Answer: BD  
Explanation: There are two requirements here, and they're met by two different mechanisms. Five-year immutability comes from S3 Object Lock in compliance mode (B): in this mode, no one — including the root user — can delete or overwrite an object version before the retention period ends. Encryption with automatic yearly key rotation comes from a customer managed key in KMS with automatic rotation enabled (D): AWS generates new cryptographic material once a year on its own, while retaining the old material so previously written objects can still be decrypted. That's exactly why rotation doesn't break access to older documents.  
Why A is not selected: Governance mode can be bypassed by anyone holding the s3:BypassGovernanceRetention permission. That's not enough for a legal requirement that documents "cannot be overwritten or deleted."  
Why C is not selected: With SSE-S3, rotation is managed entirely by the service — the customer can't configure or confirm a yearly period. The requirement to "rotate automatically every year" isn't verifiably met.  
Why E is not selected: Automatic rotation isn't supported for keys with imported material: new material has to be imported manually. That's both not automatic and the highest possible operational cost.

---

190\. A company has a web application that is based on Java and PHP. The company plans to move the application from on premises to AWS. The company needs the ability to test new site features frequently. The company also needs a highly available and managed solution that requires minimum operational overhead.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Enable static web hosting on the S3 bucket. Upload the static content to the S3 bucket. Use AWS Lambda to process all dynamic content.  
B. Deploy the web application to an AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment. Use URL swapping to switch between multiple Elastic Beanstalk environments for feature testing.  
C. Deploy the web application to Amazon EC2 instances that are configured with Java and PHP. Use Auto Scaling groups and an Application Load Balancer to manage the website’s availability.  
D. Containerize the web application. Deploy the web application to Amazon EC2 instances. Use the AWS Load Balancer Controller to dynamically route traffic between containers that contain the new site features for testing.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The Java-and-PHP application moves over as-is, frequent testing of new features is needed, and operations must stay minimal. AWS Elastic Beanstalk deploys applications like this on a managed platform with a load balancer and Auto Scaling, and swapping URLs between two environments gives instant switching between the current and the tested version, with an equally instant rollback.  
Why A is not selected: PHP is a server-side language, S3 static hosting can't execute it, and moving all the logic to Lambda means a rewrite.  
Why C is not selected: Self-managed instances configured with Java and PHP still need patching and updates — that's not a managed solution.  
Why D is not selected: Containers on EC2 instances again leave nodes to maintain, and the AWS Load Balancer Controller belongs to Kubernetes, not to instances running containers directly.

---

191\. A company has an ordering application that stores customer information in Amazon RDS for MySQL. During regular business hours, employees run one-time queries for reporting purposes. Timeouts are occurring during order processing because the reporting queries are taking a long time to run. The company needs to eliminate the timeouts without preventing employees from performing queries.  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?  
A. Create a read replica. Move reporting queries to the read replica.  
B. Create a read replica. Distribute the ordering application to the primary DB instance and the read replica.  
C. Migrate the ordering application to Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity.  
D. Schedule the reporting queries for non-peak hours.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The reporting queries are interfering with order processing. A read replica takes on those queries, freeing the primary instance for transactions. Employees keep running their queries, and the timeouts during order placement go away.  
Why B is not selected: Routing the ordering application to the replica too doesn't work: writes to a replica aren't possible, and reads from it may return stale data.  
Why C is not selected: Moving to DynamoDB means rewriting the application, and ad hoc reporting queries are awkward there.  
Why D is not selected: Moving the queries to off-peak hours takes away employees' ability to work with reports during the day, which the scenario doesn't allow.

---

192\. A hospital wants to create digital copies for its large collection of historical written records. The hospital will continue to add hundreds of new documents each day. The hospital’s data team will scan the documents and will upload the documents to the AWS Cloud.  
A solutions architect must implement a solution to analyze the documents, extract the medical information, and store the documents so that an application can run SQL queries on the data. The solution must maximize scalability and operational efficiency.  
Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)  
A. Write the document information to an Amazon EC2 instance that runs a MySQL database.  
B. Write the document information to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to query the data.  
C. Create an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to run a custom application that processes the scanned files and extracts the medical information.  
D. Create an AWS Lambda function that runs when new documents are uploaded. Use Amazon Rekognition to convert the documents to raw text. Use Amazon Transcribe Medical to detect and extract relevant medical information from the text.  
E. Create an AWS Lambda function that runs when new documents are uploaded. Use Amazon Textract to convert the documents to raw text. Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to detect and extract relevant medical information from the text.  
Answer: BE  
Explanation: The documents are scanned, so the text needs to be recognized. A Lambda function triggered on upload calls Amazon Textract to extract the text and Amazon Comprehend Medical to find the medical information (E). The result lands in S3, and SQL queries against it run through Amazon Athena (B) — no servers, and pay only for data scanned.  
Why A is not selected: A MySQL database on an EC2 instance requires maintenance and scales poorly with hundreds of documents a day.  
Why C is not selected: A custom application on a fleet of instances is maximum development and operational effort where ready-made services already exist.  
Why D is not selected: Rekognition doesn't parse multi-page documents, and Transcribe Medical works with speech, not text.

---

193\. A company is running a batch application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application consists of a backend with multiple Amazon RDS databases. The application is causing a high number of reads on the databases. A solutions architect must reduce the number of database reads while ensuring high availability.  
What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement?  
A. Add Amazon RDS read replicas.  
B. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.  
C. Use Amazon Route 53 DNS caching  
D. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: There are two requirements: cut database read load and preserve high availability, without rewriting the application. RDS read replicas solve both: SELECT queries route to the replica, the primary instance is offloaded, and the replica can be promoted to primary if needed. A cache also offloads reads, but it requires application changes (cache-aside logic and invalidation) and by itself adds nothing to the database's availability.  
Why B is not selected: ElastiCache for Redis does offload reads, but it requires rewriting the data-access code and doesn't improve the database's own availability.  
Why C is not selected: DNS caching relates to name resolution and has no effect at all on the number of database queries.  
Why D is not selected: Memcached doesn't support replication or data persistence, so it's even weaker on availability, and the application would still need to change.

---

194\. A company needs to run a critical application on AWS. The company needs to use Amazon EC2 for the application’s database. The database must be highly available and must fail over automatically if a disruptive event occurs.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Launch two EC2 instances, each in a different Availability Zone in the same AWS Region. Install the database on both EC2 instances. Configure the EC2 instances as a cluster. Set up database replication.  
B. Launch an EC2 instance in an Availability Zone. Install the database on the EC2 instance. Use an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) to back up the data. Use AWS CloudFormation to automate provisioning of the EC2 instance if a disruptive event occurs.  
C. Launch two EC2 instances, each in a different AWS Region. Install the database on both EC2 instances. Set up database replication. Fail over the database to a second Region.  
D. Launch an EC2 instance in an Availability Zone. Install the database on the EC2 instance. Use an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) to back up the data. Use EC2 automatic recovery to recover the instance if a disruptive event occurs.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The scenario specifically requires using EC2 for the database, so managed services are off the table. Fault tolerance has to be built by hand: two instances in different Availability Zones within the same Region, the database installed on both, a cluster and replication configured — when one zone fails, the role transfers to the second node automatically.  
Why B is not selected: Recovering from an image after a disaster is a manual or delayed action with noticeable downtime, not an automatic failover.  
Why C is not selected: Two Regions complicate replication and add latency; two zones within one Region are enough for fault tolerance.  
Why D is not selected: EC2 automatic recovery restarts the same machine and doesn't help if the entire Availability Zone fails.

---

195\. A company’s order system sends requests from clients to Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances process the orders and then store the orders in a database on Amazon RDS. Users report that they must reprocess orders when the system fails. The company wants a resilient solution that can process orders automatically if a system outage occurs.  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?  
A. Move the EC2 instances into an Auto Scaling group. Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule to target an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task.  
B. Move the EC2 instances into an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Update the order system to send messages to the ALB endpoint.  
C. Move the EC2 instances into an Auto Scaling group. Configure the order system to send messages to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure the EC2 instances to consume messages from the queue.  
D. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Create an AWS Lambda function, and subscribe the function to the SNS topic. Configure the order system to send messages to the SNS topic. Send a command to the EC2 instances to process the messages by using AWS Systems Manager Run Command.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: Orders get lost because the request is handled by the same instance that can fail. An SQS queue holds the order until processing is confirmed: if the instance goes down, the message becomes visible again and another instance picks it up. Meanwhile, the instances sit in an Auto Scaling group and scale with the queue length.  
Why A is not selected: EventBridge routes events but doesn't store them and doesn't guarantee reprocessing after a failure.  
Why B is not selected: A load balancer distributes requests, but if an instance fails partway through processing, the order is still lost.  
Why D is not selected: SNS doesn't store messages, and dispatching commands through Run Command is an awkward and fragile way to process orders.

---

196\. A company runs an application on a large fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The application reads and writes entries into an Amazon DynamoDB table. The size of the DynamoDB table continuously grows, but the application needs only data from the last 30 days. The company needs a solution that minimizes cost and development effort.  
Which solution meets these requirements?  
A. Use an AWS CloudFormation template to deploy the complete solution. Redeploy the CloudFormation stack every 30 days, and delete the original stack.  
B. Use an EC2 instance that runs a monitoring application from AWS Marketplace. Configure the monitoring application to use Amazon DynamoDB Streams to store the timestamp when a new item is created in the table. Use a script that runs on the EC2 instance to delete items that have a timestamp that is older than 30 days.  
C. Configure Amazon DynamoDB Streams to invoke an AWS Lambda function when a new item is created in the table. Configure the Lambda function to delete items in the table that are older than 30 days.  
D. Extend the application to add an attribute that has a value of the current timestamp plus 30 days to each new item that is created in the table. Configure DynamoDB to use the attribute as the TTL attribute.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: DynamoDB has a built-in item-expiration mechanism: an attribute holding a timestamp up to which the item is valid is added to each item, and the table is configured to use that attribute as the TTL attribute. The service deletes expired items on its own, with no write-capacity cost and no cleanup code at all.  
Why A is not selected: Recreating the stack every 30 days means losing all the data at once, including the recent data.  
Why B is not selected: An instance running a third-party application plus a deletion script is maximum cost and maintenance.  
Why C is not selected: A function that deletes old items consumes write capacity and requires code, whereas TTL does the same thing for free.

---

197\. A company has a Microsoft .NET application that runs on an on-premises Windows Server. The application stores data by using an Oracle Database Standard Edition server. The company is planning a migration to AWS and wants to minimize development changes while moving the application. The AWS application environment should be highly available.  
Which combination of actions should the company take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)  
A. Refactor the application as serverless with AWS Lambda functions running .NET Core.  
B. Rehost the application in AWS Elastic Beanstalk with the .NET platform in a Multi-AZ deployment.  
C. Replatform the application to run on Amazon EC2 with the Amazon Linux Amazon Machine Image (AMI).  
D. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate from the Oracle database to Amazon DynamoDB in a Multi-AZ deployment.  
E. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate from the Oracle database to Oracle on Amazon RDS in a Multi-AZ deployment.  
Answer: BE  
Explanation: The requirement is minimal code changes and high availability. The .NET-on-Windows application moves over as-is into Elastic Beanstalk on the .NET platform in a Multi-AZ deployment (B), and the Oracle database migrates through AWS DMS into Oracle on Amazon RDS in a Multi-AZ deployment (E). The database engine stays the same, so the queries and schema don't change.  
Why A is not selected: Rewriting for Lambda is exactly the kind of major application rework the scenario asks to avoid.  
Why C is not selected: Moving the Windows .NET application to the Amazon Linux AMI requires code changes and compatibility testing.  
Why D is not selected: DynamoDB is a non-relational store: every SQL query would have to be rewritten.

---

198\. A company runs a containerized application on a Kubernetes cluster in an on-premises data center. The company is using a MongoDB database for data storage. The company wants to migrate some of these environments to AWS, but no code changes or deployment method changes are possible at this time. The company needs a solution that minimizes operational overhead.  
Which solution meets these requirements?  
A. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with Amazon EC2 worker nodes for compute and MongoDB on EC2 for data storage.  
B. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate for compute and Amazon DynamoDB for data storage  
C. Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with Amazon EC2 worker nodes for compute and Amazon DynamoDB for data storage.  
D. Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with AWS Fargate for compute and Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) for data storage.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: Neither the code nor the deployment method can change, which means keeping Kubernetes and MongoDB. So EKS preserves the familiar manifests and tooling, the Fargate mode removes node management, and Amazon DocumentDB is MongoDB-compatible, so the application's drivers and queries stay the same.  
Why A is not selected: ECS is a different orchestration system: the Kubernetes manifests would need to be rewritten, and MongoDB on instances still needs maintenance.  
Why B is not selected: Both the orchestration is different and DynamoDB is incompatible with MongoDB: the code would have to change.  
Why C is not selected: Kubernetes is preserved, but the EC2 worker nodes still need maintenance, and moving to DynamoDB requires code changes.

---

199\. A telemarketing company is designing its customer call center functionality on AWS. The company needs a solution that provides multiple speaker recognition and generates transcript files. The company wants to query the transcript files to analyze the business patterns. The transcript files must be stored for 7 years for auditing purposes.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Use Amazon Rekognition for multiple speaker recognition. Store the transcript files in Amazon S3. Use machine learning models for transcript file analysis.  
B. Use Amazon Transcribe for multiple speaker recognition. Use Amazon Athena for transcript file analysis.  
C. Use Amazon Translate for multiple speaker recognition. Store the transcript files in Amazon Redshift. Use SQL queries for transcript file analysis.  
D. Use Amazon Rekognition for multiple speaker recognition. Store the transcript files in Amazon S3. Use Amazon Textract for transcript file analysis.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: Recognizing multiple speakers and transcribing calls is Amazon Transcribe with speaker diarization enabled. The finished transcripts land in S3, where they can be kept for as long as seven years, and Amazon Athena runs queries against them using plain SQL, billed by data scanned.  
Why A is not selected: Rekognition analyzes images and video, not speech.  
Why C is not selected: Translate translates text between languages and doesn't distinguish speakers.  
Why D is not selected: Again, Rekognition isn't for speech, and Textract extracts text from documents rather than analyzing finished transcripts.

---

200\. A company hosts its application on AWS. The company uses Amazon Cognito to manage users. When users log in to the application, the application fetches required data from Amazon DynamoDB by using a REST API that is hosted in Amazon API Gateway. The company wants an AWS managed solution that will control access to the REST API to reduce development efforts.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Configure an AWS Lambda function to be an authorizer in API Gateway to validate which user made the request.  
B. For each user, create and assign an API key that must be sent with each request. Validate the key by using an AWS Lambda function.  
C. Send the user’s email address in the header with every request. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to validate that the user with that email address has proper access.  
D. Configure an Amazon Cognito user pool authorizer in API Gateway to allow Amazon Cognito to validate each request.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: The users already live in a Cognito user pool, so their token should be validated by a built-in mechanism, not by custom code. API Gateway lets you configure a Cognito user pool authorizer: the client sends a JWT in the Authorization header, and the gateway itself validates the signature, the expiration, and, if desired, groups and scopes. Zero development. A custom Lambda authorizer is only needed when the authorization logic is more complex than checking a token.  
Why A is not selected: A Lambda authorizer is code that has to be written and maintained. With a Cognito user pool already in place, the built-in authorizer does the same thing for free.  
Why B is not selected: API keys are meant for usage plans and throttling, not for authenticating users. Plus, again, a custom validation function.  
Why C is not selected: Sending the email address in a header just takes the client's word for it: forging such a header is trivial.

---

201\. A company is developing a marketing communications service that targets mobile app users. The company needs to send confirmation messages with Short Message Service (SMS) to its users. The users must be able to reply to the SMS messages. The company must store the responses for a year for analysis.  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?  
A. Create an Amazon Connect contact flow to send the SMS messages. Use AWS Lambda to process the responses.  
B. Build an Amazon Pinpoint journey. Configure Amazon Pinpoint to send events to an Amazon Kinesis data stream for analysis and archiving.  
C. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to distribute the SMS messages. Use AWS Lambda to process the responses.  
D. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) FIFO topic. Subscribe an Amazon Kinesis data stream to the SNS topic for analysis and archiving.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: Two-way SMS messaging is needed, with responses stored and later analyzed. Amazon Pinpoint supports two-way SMS and messaging journeys, and events — including incoming replies — are sent to a Kinesis data stream for archiving and analysis.  
Why A is not selected: Amazon Connect is built for contact centers and voice scenarios, not bulk SMS messaging with response analysis.  
Why C is not selected: SQS is an internal message queue; it can't send SMS messages to users.  
Why D is not selected: SNS can send SMS, but it doesn't support receiving replies from users, and FIFO topics can't be used with SMS.

---

202\. A company is planning to move its data to an Amazon S3 bucket. The data must be encrypted when it is stored in the S3 bucket. Additionally, the encryption key must be automatically rotated every year.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Move the data to the S3 bucket. Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE- S3). Use the built-in key rotation behavior of SSE-S3 encryption keys.  
B. Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Enable automatic key rotation. Set the S3 bucket’s default encryption behavior to use the customer managed KMS key. Move the data to the S3 bucket.  
C. Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Set the S3 bucket’s default encryption behavior to use the customer managed KMS key. Move the data to the S3 bucket. Manually rotate the KMS key every year.  
D. Encrypt the data with customer key material before moving the data to the S3 bucket. Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key without key material. Import the customer key material into the KMS key. Enable automatic key rotation.  
Answer: B  
Review status: Disputed key (alternative: A)  
Dispute note: Contradiction within the bank: question {{q:825}} is phrased identically, but there the key is A (SSE-S3). KMS with automatic rotation gives a documented annual cycle, while SSE-S3 requires fewer steps — both keys can't be correct at the same time  
Explanation: This question is worded the same way as {{q:825}}, but the two carry different answer keys — a contradiction within the dump itself, which is why the question is flagged as disputed. Resolving it comes down to weighing two phrases in the scenario. "Automatically rotated every year" is precisely and documentably satisfied only by a customer managed key in KMS: automatic rotation happens every 365 days, and the fact of rotation is visible in the console and in CloudTrail. "LEAST operational overhead" points toward SSE-S3, where the service fully manages the keys and there's nothing to configure. Practical takeaway: if the scenario stresses a verifiable yearly period, go with KMS and automatic rotation; if the emphasis is only on "we don't care how, as long as it happens on its own," go with SSE-S3.
