Why A is not selected: A strong alternative, and the answer key for {{q:825}}: SSE-S3 really does rotate keys through the service and requires no configuration at all. Its weak point is that the rotation period isn't documented as yearly and can't be confirmed to an auditor.  
Why C is not selected: Manual rotation once a year satisfies the requirement in substance, but it requires a human action every year. With an "automatic rotation" option available, that's unnecessary operational cost.  
Why D is not selected: Importing your own key material is the most labor-intensive path, and automatic rotation in KMS isn't supported for imported material. The option contradicts itself.

---

203\. The customers of a finance company request appointments with financial advisors by sending text messages. A web application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances accepts the appointment requests. The text messages are published to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue through the web application. Another application that runs on EC2 instances then sends meeting invitations and meeting confirmation email messages to the customers. After successful scheduling, this application stores the meeting information in an Amazon DynamoDB database.  
As the company expands, customers report that their meeting invitations are taking longer to arrive.  
What should a solutions architect recommend to resolve this issue?  
A. Add a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster in front of the DynamoDB database.  
B. Add an Amazon API Gateway API in front of the web application that accepts the appointment requests.  
C. Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Set the origin as the web application that accepts the appointment requests.  
D. Add an Auto Scaling group for the application that sends meeting invitations. Configure the Auto Scaling group to scale based on the depth of the SQS queue.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: The invitations are arriving late because the instances reading the queue can't keep up with the growing number of messages. The right fix is to put those instances into an Auto Scaling group and scale it based on the depth of the SQS queue: the more messages pile up, the more processing instances get launched.  
Why A is not selected: DAX speeds up reads from DynamoDB, but the bottleneck is in sending invitations, not in reading data.  
Why B is not selected: Putting API Gateway in front of intake doesn't affect how fast requests get processed afterward: requests are already being accepted successfully.  
Why C is not selected: CloudFront caches content for readers and does nothing to speed up background processing of messages from the queue.

---

204\. An online retail company has more than 50 million active customers and receives more than 25,000 orders each day. The company collects purchase data for customers and stores this data in Amazon S3. Additional customer data is stored in Amazon RDS.  
The company wants to make all the data available to various teams so that the teams can perform analytics. The solution must provide the ability to manage fine-grained permissions for the data and must minimize operational overhead.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Migrate the purchase data to write directly to Amazon RDS. Use RDS access controls to limit access.  
B. Schedule an AWS Lambda function to periodically copy data from Amazon RDS to Amazon S3. Create an AWS Glue crawler. Use Amazon Athena to query the data. Use S3 policies to limit access.  
C. Create a data lake by using AWS Lake Formation. Create an AWS Glue JDBC connection to Amazon RDS. Register the S3 bucket in Lake Formation. Use Lake Formation access controls to limit access.  
D. Create an Amazon Redshift cluster. Schedule an AWS Lambda function to periodically copy data from Amazon S3 and Amazon RDS to Amazon Redshift. Use Amazon Redshift access controls to limit access.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: Data lives in two places — S3 and RDS — and access needs fine-grained control with minimal operations. AWS Lake Formation builds a data lake on top of S3, connects to RDS through a JDBC connection in AWS Glue, and lets you grant permissions at the database, table, column, and row level from a single place.  
Why A is not selected: Moving all the purchase data into a relational database means both higher cost and lost scalability, and it doesn't give RDS fine-grained column-level control.  
Why B is not selected: Custom copy functions and bucket policies only provide coarse, object-level access control and require ongoing maintenance.  
Why D is not selected: A Redshift cluster is billed continuously, and copying data with Lambda functions is unnecessary extra development.

---

205\. A company hosts a marketing website in an on-premises data center. The website consists of static documents and runs on a single server. An administrator updates the website content infrequently and uses an SFTP client to upload new documents.  
The company decides to host its website on AWS and to use Amazon CloudFront. The company’s solutions architect creates a CloudFront distribution. The solutions architect must design the most cost-effective and resilient architecture for website hosting to serve as the CloudFront origin.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Create a virtual server by using Amazon Lightsail. Configure the web server in the Lightsail instance. Upload website content by using an SFTP client.  
B. Create an AWS Auto Scaling group for Amazon EC2 instances. Use an Application Load Balancer. Upload website content by using an SFTP client.  
C. Create a private Amazon S3 bucket. Use an S3 bucket policy to allow access from a CloudFront origin access identity (OAI). Upload website content by using the AWS CLI.  
D. Create a public Amazon S3 bucket. Configure AWS Transfer for SFTP. Configure the S3 bucket for website hosting. Upload website content by using the SFTP client.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The site is static, updates infrequently, and needs a cost-effective and resilient origin for CloudFront. A private S3 bucket satisfies both conditions: you pay only for storage and requests, durability is eleven nines, and there are no servers at all. Access to the bucket is opened only to the distribution through an origin access identity, and content is uploaded with the AWS CLI.  
Why A is not selected: The Lightsail instance is billed around the clock and remains a single point of failure that has to be maintained.  
Why B is not selected: An Auto Scaling group behind a load balancer is the most expensive setup for a static site that's updated about once a month.  
Why D is not selected: A public bucket plus an always-on AWS Transfer Family endpoint means both unnecessary cost and open access to the content that bypasses CloudFront.

---

206\. A company wants to manage Amazon Machine Images (AMIs). The company currently copies AMIs to the same AWS Region where the AMIs were created. The company needs to design an application that captures AWS API calls and sends alerts whenever the Amazon EC2 CreateImage API operation is called within the company’s account.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Create an AWS Lambda function to query AWS CloudTrail logs and to send an alert when a CreateImage API call is detected.  
B. Configure AWS CloudTrail with an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification that occurs when updated logs are sent to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to create a new table and to query on CreateImage when an API call is detected.  
C. Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule for the CreateImage API call. Configure the target as an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send an alert when a CreateImage API call is detected.  
D. Configure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue as a target for AWS CloudTrail logs. Create an AWS Lambda function to send an alert to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when a CreateImage API call is detected.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: EventBridge receives API call events from CloudTrail directly: you create a rule that matches the CreateImage event and set an SNS topic as the target. No code, no querying logs — the alert arrives right after the call is made.  
Why A is not selected: Periodically parsing logs with a function means both delay and code that has to be maintained.  
Why B is not selected: A notification when new log files arrive, plus queries in Athena, means a delay of minutes and requires manual work.  
Why D is not selected: CloudTrail does not send logs to an SQS queue as a destination — no such integration exists.

---

207\. A company owns an asynchronous API that is used to ingest user requests and, based on the request type, dispatch requests to the appropriate microservice for processing. The company is using Amazon API Gateway to deploy the API front end, and an AWS Lambda function that invokes Amazon DynamoDB to store user requests before dispatching them to the processing microservices.  
The company provisioned as much DynamoDB throughput as its budget allows, but the company is still experiencing availability issues and is losing user requests.  
What should a solutions architect do to address this issue without impacting existing users?  
A. Add throttling on the API Gateway with server-side throttling limits.  
B. Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) and Lambda to buffer writes to DynamoDB.  
C. Create a secondary index in DynamoDB for the table with the user requests.  
D. Use the Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue and Lambda to buffer writes to DynamoDB.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: The table's throughput has already been provisioned to the budget's maximum, and requests are still being lost. That calls for a buffer: one function places the request on an SQS queue, and another function reads the queue and writes to DynamoDB at a controlled rate. Spikes are smoothed out, nothing is lost, and existing users notice no change.  
Why A is not selected: Rate limiting in API Gateway drops some requests — that is, it turns data loss into policy and affects users.  
Why B is not selected: DAX speeds up reads and does not buffer writes: the write problem remains.  
Why C is not selected: A secondary index adds another consumer of write throughput and will only make things worse.

---

208\. A company needs to move data from an Amazon EC2 instance to an Amazon S3 bucket. The company must ensure that no API calls and no data are routed through public internet routes. Only the EC2 instance can have access to upload data to the S3 bucket.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Create an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the subnet where the EC2 instance is located. Attach a resource policy to the S3 bucket to only allow the EC2 instance’s IAM role for access.  
B. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the Availability Zone where the EC2 instance is located. Attach appropriate security groups to the endpoint. Attach a resource policy to the S3 bucket to only allow the EC2 instance’s IAM role for access.  
C. Run the nslookup tool from inside the EC2 instance to obtain the private IP address of the S3 bucket’s service API endpoint. Create a route in the VPC route table to provide the EC2 instance with access to the S3 bucket. Attach a resource policy to the S3 bucket to only allow the EC2 instance’s IAM role for access.  
D. Use the AWS provided, publicly available ip-ranges.json file to obtain the private IP address of the S3 bucket’s service API endpoint. Create a route in the VPC route table to provide the EC2 instance with access to the S3 bucket. Attach a resource policy to the S3 bucket to only allow the EC2 instance’s IAM role for access.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Neither API calls nor data may travel public routes, and only this instance is allowed to upload. The first requirement is met by a VPC endpoint, the second by a bucket policy that allows access only to the instance's role (and, if desired, only through that endpoint). Here the key selects the interface endpoint: it is created in a specific subnet, gets a private IP address, and is protected by a security group. The difference from a gateway endpoint matters: a gateway endpoint works through routes in the route table, has neither an IP address nor security groups, and is not reachable from on premises — compare with {{q:667,471}}.  
Why B is not selected: The description doesn't match the mechanism: a gateway endpoint isn't placed in an Availability Zone and doesn't support security groups — it's a route in the VPC route table.  
Why C is not selected: S3 has no "private bucket IP address" that can be looked up with nslookup and set as a route. A private address only appears together with an interface endpoint.  
Why D is not selected: The ip-ranges.json file contains AWS's public IP ranges. A route to them does nothing to make the traffic private.

---

209\. A solutions architect is designing the architecture of a new application being deployed to the AWS Cloud. The application will run on Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances and will automatically scale across multiple Availability Zones. The EC2 instances will scale up and down frequently throughout the day. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) will handle the load distribution. The architecture needs to support distributed session data management.  
The company is willing to make changes to code if needed.  
What should the solutions architect do to ensure that the architecture supports distributed session data management?  
A. Use Amazon ElastiCache to manage and store session data.  
B. Use session affinity (sticky sessions) of the ALB to manage session data.  
C. Use Session Manager from AWS Systems Manager to manage the session.  
D. Use the GetSessionToken API operation in AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to manage the session.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Instances are frequently added and removed, so session state can't be kept on them. ElastiCache moves sessions out to an external in-memory store: any instance reads and writes the same data, response time is measured in fractions of a millisecond, and code changes are allowed under the stated condition.  
Why B is not selected: Session affinity keeps a user pinned to a specific instance, and when that instance is removed from the group the session is lost.  
Why C is not selected: Session Manager from Systems Manager is administrator access to an instance's shell — it has nothing to do with application user sessions.  
Why D is not selected: GetSessionToken issues temporary AWS credentials — it doesn't store web application sessions.

---

210\. A company offers a food delivery service that is growing rapidly. Because of the growth, the company’s order processing system is experiencing scaling problems during peak traffic hours. The current architecture includes the following:  
• A group of Amazon EC2 instances that run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to collect orders from the application  
• Another group of EC2 instances that run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to fulfill orders The order collection process occurs quickly, but the order fulfillment process can take longer. Data must not be lost because of a scaling event.  
A solutions architect must ensure that the order collection process and the order fulfillment process can both scale properly during peak traffic hours. The solution must optimize utilization of the company’s AWS resources.  
Which solution meets these requirements?  
A. Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to monitor the CPU of each instance in the Auto Scaling groups. Configure each Auto Scaling group’s minimum capacity according to peak workload values.  
B. Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to monitor the CPU of each instance in the Auto Scaling groups. Configure a CloudWatch alarm to invoke an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic that creates additional Auto Scaling groups on demand.  
C. Provision two Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues: one for order collection and another for order fulfillment. Configure the EC2 instances to poll their respective queue. Scale the Auto Scaling groups based on notifications that the queues send.  
D. Provision two Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues: one for order collection and another for order fulfillment. Configure the EC2 instances to poll their respective queue. Create a metric based on a backlog per instance calculation. Scale the Auto Scaling groups based on this metric.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: Order collection is fast, fulfillment is slow — so the stages need to be decoupled with two queues and each scaled to its own load. The right metric for a queue is backlog per instance: the number of messages in the queue divided by the number of consumers, with the Auto Scaling group holding that value steady. That way capacity tracks the actual volume of work, and no data is lost during scaling.  
Why A is not selected: Permanently keeping peak minimum capacity is overpaying, and CPU utilization is a poor reflection of the volume of accumulated orders.  
Why B is not selected: Creating new Auto Scaling groups on a signal is an unworkable, unmanageable design.  
Why C is not selected: The queues are chosen correctly, but SQS doesn't send notifications you can scale on — you need a metric based on message count.

---

211\. A company hosts multiple production applications. One of the applications consists of resources from Amazon EC2, AWS Lambda, Amazon RDS, Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS), and Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) across multiple AWS Regions. All company resources are tagged with a tag name of “application” and a value that corresponds to each application. A solutions architect must provide the quickest solution for identifying all of the tagged components.  
Which solution meets these requirements?  
A. Use AWS CloudTrail to generate a list of resources with the application tag.  
B. Use the AWS CLI to query each service across all Regions to report the tagged components.  
C. Run a query in Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights to report on the components with the application tag.  
D. Run a query with the AWS Resource Groups Tag Editor to report on the resources globally with the application tag.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: Resources are tagged and scattered across multiple Regions and services. Tag Editor in AWS Resource Groups searches by tag across all Regions and resource types at once and produces a ready list — this is the fastest path, with no code required.  
Why A is not selected: CloudTrail shows API calls, not a current inventory of resources with a given tag.  
Why B is not selected: Polling every service in every Region via the CLI is slow and labor-intensive.  
Why C is not selected: CloudWatch Logs Insights works with logs, not with resource inventory.

---

212\. A company needs to export its database once a day to Amazon S3 for other teams to access. The exported object size varies between 2 GB and 5 GB. The S3 access pattern for the data is variable and changes rapidly. The data must be immediately available and must remain accessible for up to 3 months. The company needs the most cost- effective solution that will not increase retrieval time.  
Which S3 storage class should the company use to meet these requirements?  
A. S3 Intelligent-Tiering  
B. S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval  
C. S3 Standard  
D. S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The key phrases are "variable and changes rapidly" and "must not increase retrieval time." The first means the access class can't be guessed manually; the second rules out anything that doesn't return the object instantly or that charges for retrieval. Intelligent-Tiering satisfies both: objects move between the frequent and infrequent tiers automatically, there's no retrieval fee, and access time is the same on both tiers. At 2–5 GB, the objects are large enough that the monitoring fee is negligible.  
Why B is not selected: Glacier Instant Retrieval returns the object instantly, but charges a noticeable retrieval fee and requires a minimum 90-day storage duration. The data lives up to three months and is read unpredictably often — both conditions work against it.  
Why C is not selected: S3 Standard doesn't optimize anything: during periods when nobody reads the export, you pay the full rate.  
Why D is not selected: Standard-IA is designed for infrequent access. With a rapidly changing pattern, the retrieval fee and the 30-day minimum storage duration make it more expensive than Intelligent-Tiering.

---

213\. A company is developing a new mobile app. The company must implement proper traffic filtering to protect its Application Load Balancer (ALB) against common application-level attacks, such as cross-site scripting or SQL injection. The company has minimal infrastructure and operational staff. The company needs to reduce its share of the responsibility in managing, updating, and securing servers for its AWS environment.  
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?  
A. Configure AWS WAF rules and associate them with the ALB.  
B. Deploy the application using Amazon S3 with public hosting enabled.  
C. Deploy AWS Shield Advanced and add the ALB as a protected resource.  
D. Create a new ALB that directs traffic to an Amazon EC2 instance running a third-party firewall, which then passes the traffic to the current ALB.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Cross-site scripting and SQL injection are application-layer attacks, and AWS WAF is what filters them: a web ACL is attached to the load balancer, AWS managed rule groups are enabled (including the Core rule set and the SQL database rule set), and traffic is inspected before it reaches the application. AWS itself updates the managed rules, so a team with no dedicated administrators doesn't maintain signatures by hand — this directly answers the requirement to reduce its share of the responsibility.  
Why B is not selected: Public hosting of static content in S3 has nothing to do with filtering attacks and doesn't fit an application sitting behind a load balancer.  
Why C is not selected: Shield Advanced protects against DDoS but doesn't inspect the content of HTTP requests for injection attempts.  
Why D is not selected: A third-party firewall on an instance is a server that has to be patched and maintained — the opposite of the requirement.

---

214\. A company’s reporting system delivers hundreds of .csv files to an Amazon S3 bucket each day. The company must convert these files to Apache Parquet format and must store the files in a transformed data bucket.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?  
A. Create an Amazon EMR cluster with Apache Spark installed. Write a Spark application to transform the data. Use EMR File System (EMRFS) to write files to the transformed data bucket.  
B. Create an AWS Glue crawler to discover the data. Create an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to transform the data. Specify the transformed data bucket in the output step.  
C. Use AWS Batch to create a job definition with Bash syntax to transform the data and output the data to the transformed data bucket. Use the job definition to submit a job. Specify an array job as the job type.  
D. Create an AWS Lambda function to transform the data and output the data to the transformed data bucket. Configure an event notification for the S3 bucket. Specify the Lambda function as the destination for the event notification.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: Converting formats with minimal development is what AWS Glue is for. A crawler determines the structure of the CSV files and creates a table in the data catalog, and an ETL job with built-in transforms writes the result in Parquet format to the target bucket. There's almost no code and no infrastructure to manage.  
Why A is not selected: An EMR cluster and a Spark application mean both development work and cluster management.  
Why C is not selected: A Bash script to convert to Parquet would have to be written from scratch, and AWS Batch adds environment configuration on top.  
Why D is not selected: A Lambda function would need its own conversion code, and large files might not fit within its time and memory limits.

---

215\. A company has 700 TB of backup data stored in network attached storage (NAS) in its data center. This backup data need to be accessible for infrequent regulatory requests and must be retained 7 years. The company has decided to migrate this backup data from its data center to AWS. The migration must be complete within 1 month.  
The company has 500 Mbps of dedicated bandwidth on its public internet connection available for data transfer.  
What should a solutions architect do to migrate and store the data at the LOWEST cost?  
A. Order AWS Snowball devices to transfer the data. Use a lifecycle policy to transition the files to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.  
B. Deploy a VPN connection between the data center and Amazon VPC. Use the AWS CLI to copy the data from on premises to Amazon S3 Glacier.  
C. Provision a 500 Mbps AWS Direct Connect connection and transfer the data to Amazon S3. Use a lifecycle policy to transition the files to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.  
D. Use AWS DataSync to transfer the data and deploy a DataSync agent on premises. Use the DataSync task to copy files from the on-premises NAS storage to Amazon S3 Glacier.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Start by checking the timing: 700 TB at 500 Mbps takes roughly four months of continuous transfer, while the deadline is one month. That rules out the network link, so the data travels physically, on Snowball devices. Storing rarely requested copies for seven years is cheapest in S3 Glacier Deep Archive, which a lifecycle rule transitions the objects into.  
Why B is not selected: A VPN runs over the same internet connection: the deadline can't be met.  
Why C is not selected: A 500 Mbps Direct Connect connection gives the same speed as the existing internet link, plus the lead time to physically provision it — usually weeks. That won't fit in a month.  
Why D is not selected: DataSync is a good tool, but it's limited by the same bandwidth, and it can't upload directly into the Glacier storage class: data lands in S3 first.

---

216\. A company has a serverless website with millions of objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company uses the S3 bucket as the origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution. The company did not set encryption on the S3 bucket before the objects were loaded. A solutions architect needs to enable encryption for all existing objects and for all objects that are added to the S3 bucket in the future.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of effort?  
A. Create a new S3 bucket. Turn on the default encryption settings for the new S3 bucket. Download all existing objects to temporary local storage. Upload the objects to the new S3 bucket.  
B. Turn on the default encryption settings for the S3 bucket. Use the S3 Inventory feature to create a .csv file that lists the unencrypted objects. Run an S3 Batch Operations job that uses the copy command to encrypt those objects.  
C. Create a new encryption key by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Change the settings on the S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS managed encryption keys (SSE-KMS). Turn on versioning for the S3 bucket.  
D. Navigate to Amazon S3 in the AWS Management Console. Browse the S3 bucket’s objects. Sort by the encryption field. Select each unencrypted object. Use the Modify button to apply default encryption settings to every unencrypted object in the S3 bucket.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The task splits in two: new objects and the millions already sitting there. For new objects, it's enough to turn on default encryption on the bucket — after that S3 encrypts everything that arrives. The existing objects need a bulk rewrite: S3 Inventory builds a report listing the objects and their encryption status, and S3 Batch Operations runs a copy operation against that report, which rewrites each object already encrypted. All of this is managed tooling — no downloading, no custom code.  
Why A is not selected: Downloading and re-uploading millions of objects through local storage means traffic in both directions, time, and a high risk of error — exactly what the "LEAST amount of effort" wording asks you to avoid.  
Why C is not selected: Turning on default encryption only affects new objects, and versioning has nothing to do with encryption. The millions of objects already uploaded stay unencrypted.  
Why D is not selected: There's no console operation for bulk-applying encryption to selected objects, and going through millions of objects by hand is physically impossible.

---

217\. A company runs a global web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The application stores data in Amazon Aurora. The company needs to create a disaster recovery solution and can tolerate up to 30 minutes of downtime and potential data loss. The solution does not need to handle the load when the primary infrastructure is healthy.  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?  
A. Deploy the application with the required infrastructure elements in place. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-passive failover. Create an Aurora Replica in a second AWS Region.  
B. Host a scaled-down deployment of the application in a second AWS Region. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-active failover. Create an Aurora Replica in the second Region.  
C. Replicate the primary infrastructure in a second AWS Region. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active- active failover. Create an Aurora database that is restored from the latest snapshot.  
D. Back up data with AWS Backup. Use the backup to create the required infrastructure in a second AWS Region. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-passive failover. Create an Aurora second primary instance in the second Region.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Up to 30 minutes of downtime and some data loss are acceptable, and the standby site doesn't need to handle the load — this describes a pilot light or warm standby design with active-passive failover. A minimal-size infrastructure is deployed in the standby Region, data is kept current with a cross-Region Aurora replica (which can be promoted to primary), and Route 53 with health checks fails traffic over when the primary site goes down. The design is cheaper than active-active and fits within the stated RTO and RPO.  
Why B is not selected: An active-active configuration means the standby site is constantly serving part of the traffic, and the requirement explicitly says that's not needed. That's unnecessary cost.  
Why C is not selected: A full copy of the infrastructure running active-active costs even more, and restoring the database from the latest snapshot gives a worse RPO than a replica.  
Why D is not selected: Provisioning infrastructure from backups only after a disaster won't fit in 30 minutes, and a "second Aurora primary instance" in another Region describes a global database, not what's asked for here.

---

218\. A company has a web server running on an Amazon EC2 instance in a public subnet with an Elastic IP address. The default security group is assigned to the EC2 instance. The default network ACL has been modified to block all traffic. A solutions architect needs to make the web server accessible from everywhere on port 443.  
Which combination of steps will accomplish this task? (Choose two.)  
A. Create a security group with a rule to allow TCP port 443 from source 0.0.0.0/0.  
B. Create a security group with a rule to allow TCP port 443 to destination 0.0.0.0/0.  
C. Update the network ACL to allow TCP port 443 from source 0.0.0.0/0.  
D. Update the network ACL to allow inbound/outbound TCP port 443 from source 0.0.0.0/0 and to destination 0.0.0.0/0.  
E. Update the network ACL to allow inbound TCP port 443 from source 0.0.0.0/0 and outbound TCP port 32768- 65535 to destination 0.0.0.0/0.  
Answer: AE  
Explanation: Two layers of filtering are involved. A security group is stateful, so a single inbound rule for port 443 from any source is enough (A). A network ACL is stateless, so it needs two rules: inbound on port 443 and outbound to the ephemeral port range 32768–65535, where responses to the client go out (E).  
Why B is not selected: An outbound security group rule isn't needed for inbound connections: the response leaves automatically.  
Why C is not selected: An inbound-only rule in the network ACL isn't enough: responses would be blocked on the way out.  
Why D is not selected: Allowing port 443 outbound makes no sense: the web server's responses leave from ephemeral ports, not from port 443.

---

219\. A company’s application is having performance issues. The application is stateful and needs to complete in- memory tasks on Amazon EC2 instances. The company used AWS CloudFormation to deploy infrastructure and used the M5 EC2 instance family. As traffic increased, the application performance degraded. Users are reporting delays when the users attempt to access the application.  
Which solution will resolve these issues in the MOST operationally efficient way?  
A. Replace the EC2 instances with T3 EC2 instances that run in an Auto Scaling group. Make the changes by using the AWS Management Console.  
B. Modify the CloudFormation templates to run the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Increase the desired capacity and the maximum capacity of the Auto Scaling group manually when an increase is necessary.  
C. Modify the CloudFormation templates. Replace the EC2 instances with R5 EC2 instances. Use Amazon CloudWatch built-in EC2 memory metrics to track the application performance for future capacity planning.  
D. Modify the CloudFormation templates. Replace the EC2 instances with R5 EC2 instances. Deploy the Amazon CloudWatch agent on the EC2 instances to generate custom application latency metrics for future capacity planning.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: The application performs in-memory tasks, so the bottleneck is RAM, and the general-purpose M5 family doesn't fit that profile. The instances are swapped for R5, which is memory-optimized, and the change is made in the CloudFormation template that deploys the infrastructure. For future capacity planning, the CloudWatch agent is installed to collect custom application latency metrics — EC2 has no built-in memory or latency metrics.  
Why A is not selected: T3 instances are burstable with a limited performance budget: they're worse for sustained memory-heavy work, and changes made outside the template would cause configuration drift.  
Why B is not selected: Manually resizing capacity isn't operational efficiency, and the instance type is still wrong for the workload.  
Why C is not selected: The instance type is chosen correctly, but EC2 has no built-in memory metrics — only the agent provides them.

---

220\. A solutions architect is designing a new API using Amazon API Gateway that will receive requests from users. The volume of requests is highly variable; several hours can pass without receiving a single request. The data processing will take place asynchronously, but should be completed within a few seconds after a request is made.  
Which compute service should the solutions architect have the API invoke to deliver the requirements at the lowest cost?  
A. An AWS Glue job  
B. An AWS Lambda function  
C. A containerized service hosted in Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)  
D. A containerized service hosted in Amazon ECS with Amazon EC2  
Answer: B  
Explanation: Requests arrive rarely and unevenly, and processing takes seconds. A Lambda function is billed only for actual execution time, so nothing is paid for during idle hours, and it scales instantly. This is the cheapest way to serve this traffic profile.  
Why A is not selected: An AWS Glue job is built for batch data processing, starts with noticeable delay, and is billed in minimum-duration increments.  
Why C is not selected: An EKS cluster is billed continuously, including a control plane fee, even when there are no requests.  
Why D is not selected: EC2 instances behind ECS run and are billed around the clock regardless of request volume.

---

221\. A company runs an application on a group of Amazon Linux EC2 instances. For compliance reasons, the company must retain all application log files for 7 years. The log files will be analyzed by a reporting tool that must be able to access all the files concurrently.  
Which storage solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)  
B. Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)  
C. Amazon EC2 instance store  
D. Amazon S3  
Answer: D  
Explanation: Logs must be kept for seven years and read concurrently by a reporting tool. S3 is cheaper per gigabyte than any block or file storage, allows any number of simultaneous reads, and lifecycle rules let you move older logs into even cheaper storage classes. The instances simply upload the files to the bucket.  
Why A is not selected: An EBS volume is tied to an Availability Zone and to an instance, costs more per gigabyte, and doesn't give the reporting tool concurrent access.  
Why B is not selected: EFS does provide concurrent access, but it's significantly more expensive per gigabyte of storage than S3, and for a seven-year archive that's the deciding factor.  
Why C is not selected: Instance store data disappears along with the instance: a seven-year retention requirement is impossible to meet with it in the first place.

---

222\. A company has hired an external vendor to perform work in the company’s AWS account. The vendor uses an automated tool that is hosted in an AWS account that the vendor owns. The vendor does not have IAM access to the company’s AWS account.  
How should a solutions architect grant this access to the vendor?  
A. Create an IAM role in the company’s account to delegate access to the vendor’s IAM role. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the role for the permissions that the vendor requires.  
B. Create an IAM user in the company’s account with a password that meets the password complexity requirements. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the user for the permissions that the vendor requires.  
C. Create an IAM group in the company’s account. Add the tool’s IAM user from the vendor account to the group. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the group for the permissions that the vendor requires.  
D. Create a new identity provider by choosing “AWS account” as the provider type in the IAM console. Supply the vendor’s AWS account ID and user name. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the new provider for the permissions that the vendor requires.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: An external vendor doesn't need credentials in your account — it needs the ability to act as your role. You create a role in your account with the required policies, and its trust policy allows a principal from the vendor's account to assume it. The vendor's tool calls AssumeRole and receives temporary credentials. A good practice on top of this is an external ID in the trust policy condition: it protects against the confused deputy problem, when the vendor serves many clients.  
Why B is not selected: An IAM user with a password is long-lived credentials inside your account handed out externally — and you'd have to revoke them manually.  
Why C is not selected: A user from a different account can't be added to an IAM group: groups only work within their own account.  
Why D is not selected: There's no "AWS account" identity provider type in IAM: what's configured there is SAML and OIDC. Cross-account access is done with a role and a trust policy.

---

223\. A company has deployed a Java Spring Boot application as a pod that runs on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) in private subnets. The application needs to write data to an Amazon DynamoDB table. A solutions architect must ensure that the application can interact with the DynamoDB table without exposing traffic to the internet.  
Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to accomplish this goal? (Choose two.)  
A. Attach an IAM role that has sufficient privileges to the EKS pod.  
B. Attach an IAM user that has sufficient privileges to the EKS pod.  
C. Allow outbound connectivity to the DynamoDB table through the private subnets’ network ACLs.  
D. Create a VPC endpoint for DynamoDB.  
E. Embed the access keys in the Java Spring Boot code.  
Answer: AD  
Explanation: There are two separate requirements — permissions and routing. Permissions: the EKS pod is given a role through IRSA (the role is linked to a service account via the cluster's OIDC provider), after which the application runs on temporary credentials (A). Routing: to keep calls to DynamoDB from going out to the internet, a VPC endpoint is created — for DynamoDB that's a free gateway endpoint (D). No keys in code, no NAT gateway anywhere in the design.  
Why B is not selected: An IAM user isn't "attached" to a pod: that's long-lived credentials, whereas pods get permissions through a role.  
Why C is not selected: A network ACL allows or denies traffic, but without an endpoint the path to DynamoDB would still go out through an internet gateway or a NAT gateway.  
Why E is not selected: Access keys in code are a direct anti-pattern: the secret ends up in the image and the repository and never gets rotated.

---

224\. A company recently migrated its web application to AWS by rehosting the application on Amazon EC2 instances in a single AWS Region. The company wants to redesign its application architecture to be highly available and fault tolerant. Traffic must reach all running EC2 instances randomly.  
Which combination of steps should the company take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)  
A. Create an Amazon Route 53 failover routing policy.  
B. Create an Amazon Route 53 weighted routing policy.  
C. Create an Amazon Route 53 multivalue answer routing policy.  
D. Launch three EC2 instances: two instances in one Availability Zone and one instance in another Availability Zone.  
E. Launch four EC2 instances: two instances in one Availability Zone and two instances in another Availability Zone.  
Answer: CE  
Explanation: There are two separate requirements here. Fault tolerance across zones: instances are split evenly between two Availability Zones, so the loss of one zone doesn't cut capacity unevenly in half — hence four instances, two in each zone (E). Random distribution of requests across all running instances: the multivalue answer policy in Route 53 returns up to eight records with associated health checks, the client picks one of them, and unhealthy addresses are excluded from the answer (C).  
Why A is not selected: Failover sends traffic to a standby resource only when the primary fails — that's not random distribution across all instances.  
Why B is not selected: Weighted routing distributes traffic in set proportions, while the requirement is random distribution across all healthy targets.  
Why D is not selected: Three instances split two plus one is uneven: if the zone with two instances fails, only a third of capacity remains.

---

225\. A media company collects and analyzes user activity data on premises. The company wants to migrate this capability to AWS. The user activity data store will continue to grow and will be petabytes in size. The company needs to build a highly available data ingestion solution that facilitates on-demand analytics of existing data and new data with SQL.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Send activity data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Configure the stream to deliver the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.  
B. Send activity data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Configure the stream to deliver the data to an Amazon Redshift cluster.  
C. Place activity data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure Amazon S3 to run an AWS Lambda function on the data as the data arrives in the S3 bucket.  
D. Create an ingestion service on Amazon EC2 instances that are spread across multiple Availability Zones. Configure the service to forward data to an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ database.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: High availability, growing volume, and on-demand SQL queries are all required with minimal operational overhead. Kinesis Data Firehose ingests the stream without shard management and delivers the data straight to a Redshift cluster, where SQL queries can run immediately, including against historical data.  
Why A is not selected: Data sitting in an S3 bucket doesn't give you SQL queries by itself: you'd still need a catalog and a query engine, and a Kinesis data stream requires shard management.  
Why C is not selected: Custom processing functions triggered on file arrival mean code and maintenance, and the design contains no query engine at all.  
Why D is not selected: A custom ingestion service on instances plus a relational RDS database scale poorly to petabytes and require full operational management.

---

226\. A company collects data from thousands of remote devices by using a RESTful web services application that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. The EC2 instance receives the raw data, transforms the raw data, and stores all the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The number of remote devices will increase into the millions soon. The company needs a highly scalable solution that minimizes operational overhead.  
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)  
A. Use AWS Glue to process the raw data in Amazon S3.  
B. Use Amazon Route 53 to route traffic to different EC2 instances.  
C. Add more EC2 instances to accommodate the increasing amount of incoming data.  
D. Send the raw data to Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS). Use EC2 instances to process the data.  
E. Use Amazon API Gateway to send the raw data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Configure Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to use the data stream as a source to deliver the data to Amazon S3.  
Answer: AE  
Explanation: Millions of devices, a raw data stream, and a requirement for minimal operations mean ingestion has to be serverless and elastic. API Gateway accepts the devices' HTTP requests and puts records onto a Kinesis Data Streams stream, and Firehose buffers them and drops them into S3 with no servers involved (E). The transformation the instance used to do is handled by managed ETL — AWS Glue, working directly on the data already in S3 (A). No instances remain in the design at all.  
Why B is not selected: Route 53 distributes requests across instances, but the instances don't go anywhere: the operational burden remains.  
Why C is not selected: Adding more instances is exactly the manual scaling the requirement asks you to avoid.  
Why D is not selected: An SQS queue with processing on instances flattens spikes but still leaves a fleet of machines to operate, and Kinesis is the more natural fit for streaming data.

---

227\. A company needs to retain its AWS CloudTrail logs for 3 years. The company is enforcing CloudTrail across a set of AWS accounts by using AWS Organizations from the parent account. The CloudTrail target S3 bucket is configured with S3 Versioning enabled. An S3 Lifecycle policy is in place to delete current objects after 3 years.  
After the fourth year of use of the S3 bucket, the S3 bucket metrics show that the number of objects has continued to rise. However, the number of new CloudTrail logs that are delivered to the S3 bucket has remained consistent.  
Which solution will delete objects that are older than 3 years in the MOST cost-effective manner?  
A. Configure the organization’s centralized CloudTrail trail to expire objects after 3 years.  
B. Configure the S3 Lifecycle policy to delete previous versions as well as current versions.  
C. Create an AWS Lambda function to enumerate and delete objects from Amazon S3 that are older than 3 years.  
D. Configure the parent account as the owner of all objects that are delivered to the S3 bucket.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The symptom is described precisely: no new logs have been added, yet the object count keeps rising — meaning stale versions are piling up. On a versioned bucket, a lifecycle rule with an Expiration action only removes the current version, turning it into a delete marker, while the earlier versions remain and keep being billed. The fix is to add NoncurrentVersionExpiration to the rule (and clean up expired delete markers while at it). This is a configuration change, not code, which is why it's also the cheapest.  
Why A is not selected: The CloudTrail trail itself has no setting for how long objects are retained in the bucket: object lifecycle is managed by S3.  
Why C is not selected: A function that enumerates objects and versions means code, and paying for invocations plus LIST and DELETE requests. A lifecycle rule does the same thing for free.  
Why D is not selected: Object ownership affects access permissions to the objects, not how many versions are kept or what that costs.

---

228\. A company has an API that receives real-time data from a fleet of monitoring devices. The API stores this data in an Amazon RDS DB instance for later analysis. The amount of data that the monitoring devices send to the API fluctuates. During periods of heavy traffic, the API often returns timeout errors.  
After an inspection of the logs, the company determines that the database is not capable of processing the volume of write traffic that comes from the API. A solutions architect must minimize the number of connections to the database and must ensure that data is not lost during periods of heavy traffic.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Increase the size of the DB instance to an instance type that has more available memory.  
B. Modify the DB instance to be a Multi-AZ DB instance. Configure the application to write to all active RDS DB instances.  
C. Modify the API to write incoming data to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use an AWS Lambda function that Amazon SQS invokes to write data from the queue to the database.  
D. Modify the API to write incoming data to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Use an AWS Lambda function that Amazon SNS invokes to write data from the topic to the database.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: Two requirements: reduce the number of connections to the database and don't lose data during traffic spikes. An SQS queue accepts records instantly and holds onto them, and a Lambda function reads the queue in batches and writes to the database with limited concurrency — so there are few connections, and a spike just makes the queue longer.  
Why A is not selected: More memory doesn't increase the number of allowed connections and won't prevent data loss during a spike.  
Why B is not selected: The standby instance in a Multi-AZ configuration doesn't accept writes: writing "to all active instances" isn't possible.  
Why D is not selected: SNS delivers messages immediately and doesn't buffer them: if the subscriber is unavailable, the data is lost.

---

229\. A company manages its own Amazon EC2 instances that run MySQL databases. The company is manually managing replication and scaling as demand increases or decreases. The company needs a new solution that simplifies the process of adding or removing compute capacity to or from its database tier as needed. The solution also must offer improved performance, scaling, and durability with minimal effort from operations.  
Which solution meets these requirements?  
A. Migrate the databases to Amazon Aurora Serverless for Aurora MySQL.  
B. Migrate the databases to Amazon Aurora Serverless for Aurora PostgreSQL.  
C. Combine the databases into one larger MySQL database. Run the larger database on larger EC2 instances.  
D. Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group for the database tier. Migrate the existing databases to the new environment.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The company is manually handling replication and scaling for MySQL on instances. Aurora Serverless for Aurora MySQL removes that entirely: the engine is MySQL-compatible, so the application doesn't need to change, capacity adjusts automatically, storage grows on its own, and data is stored in six copies across three Availability Zones.  
Why B is not selected: The PostgreSQL option requires switching engines and rewriting queries, whereas the company runs MySQL.  
Why C is not selected: Combining the databases onto larger instances is manual vertical scaling — exactly the work they want to move away from.  
Why D is not selected: A relational database can't be scaled with an EC2 Auto Scaling group: new instances won't share the same data.

---

230\. A company is concerned that two NAT instances in use will no longer be able to support the traffic needed for the company’s application. A solutions architect wants to implement a solution that is highly available, fault tolerant, and automatically scalable.  
What should the solutions architect recommend?  
A. Remove the two NAT instances and replace them with two NAT gateways in the same Availability Zone.  
B. Use Auto Scaling groups with Network Load Balancers for the NAT instances in different Availability Zones.  
C. Remove the two NAT instances and replace them with two NAT gateways in different Availability Zones.  
D. Replace the two NAT instances with Spot Instances in different Availability Zones and deploy a Network Load Balancer.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: High availability, fault tolerance, and automatic scaling are all required. A NAT gateway is a managed service that scales on its own up to tens of gigabits and is maintained by AWS. Placing one gateway in each Availability Zone keeps the zones independent if one of them fails.  
Why A is not selected: Both gateways in the same Availability Zone means that zone's failure knocks internet access out for every subnet.  
Why B is not selected: NAT instances in an Auto Scaling group behind a load balancer is a homegrown design: a default route can't point at a load balancer.  
Why D is not selected: Spot Instances can be reclaimed at any time, and routing outbound traffic through a load balancer doesn't work.

---

231\. An application runs on an Amazon EC2 instance that has an Elastic IP address in VPC A. The application requires access to a database in VPC B. Both VPCs are in the same AWS account.  
Which solution will provide the required access MOST securely?  
A. Create a DB instance security group that allows all traffic from the public IP address of the application server in VPC A.  
B. Configure a VPC peering connection between VPC A and VPC B.  
C. Make the DB instance publicly accessible. Assign a public IP address to the DB instance.  
D. Launch an EC2 instance with an Elastic IP address into VPC B. Proxy all requests through the new EC2 instance.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: Both networks belong to the same account and are inside AWS, so they should be connected privately. VPC peering creates a direct route between the networks over AWS's internal infrastructure: traffic never goes out to the internet, the database stays without a public address, and access is further narrowed with security groups.  
Why A is not selected: Allowing by public IP address means the traffic travels over the internet, and the rule itself is easily bypassed if the address changes.  
Why C is not selected: Public access to the database is a blunt violation of basic security practice: it becomes visible to the entire internet.  
Why D is not selected: A proxy on a separate instance adds a point of failure, cost, and maintenance where ordinary peering would be enough.

---

232\. A company runs demonstration environments for its customers on Amazon EC2 instances. Each environment is isolated in its own VPC. The company’s operations team needs to be notified when RDP or SSH access to an environment has been established.  
A. Configure Amazon CloudWatch Application Insights to create AWS Systems Manager OpsItems when RDP or SSH access is detected.  
B. Configure the EC2 instances with an IAM instance profile that has an IAM role with the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy attached.  
C. Publish VPC flow logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Create required metric filters. Create an Amazon CloudWatch metric alarm with a notification action for when the alarm is in the ALARM state.  
D. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to listen for events of type EC2 Instance State-change Notification. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as a target. Subscribe the operations team to the topic.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: A signal is needed the moment someone connects to an environment over RDP or SSH. The standard way to see the connection itself is VPC flow logs: they record accepted connections with destination ports 3389 and 22, are sent to CloudWatch Logs, a metric filter there turns them into a metric, and an alarm sends the notification. Everything is built from managed components and works the same way across all the isolated VPCs.  
Why A is not selected: CloudWatch Application Insights monitors application health and metrics, not the fact of an SSH or RDP login.  
Why B is not selected: A role with the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy lets you manage the instance through Systems Manager, but on its own it doesn't notify anyone of anything.  
Why D is not selected: EC2 Instance State-change events report an instance starting, stopping, and terminating. A user connecting isn't one of those events.

---

233\. A solutions architect has created a new AWS account and must secure AWS account root user access.  
Which combination of actions will accomplish this? (Choose two.)  
A. Ensure the root user uses a strong password.  
B. Enable multi-factor authentication to the root user.  
C. Store root user access keys in an encrypted Amazon S3 bucket.  
D. Add the root user to a group containing administrative permissions.  
E. Apply the required permissions to the root user with an inline policy document.  
Answer: AB  
Explanation: The root user account can't be restricted with IAM policies — it always has full permissions in the account. So protecting root comes down to making sign-in harder: a strong, unique password (A) and multi-factor authentication (B), ideally on a hardware or virtual device kept separately. On top of that, AWS recommends never creating access keys for root at all, and doing day-to-day work under IAM roles instead.  
Why C is not selected: Root shouldn't have access keys to begin with — then there's nothing to store. An encrypted bucket doesn't change the fact that leaking such a key means full control of the account.  
Why D is not selected: Root isn't subject to IAM policies: adding it to a group with administrative permissions does nothing and restricts nothing.  
Why E is not selected: You can't attach an inline policy to the root user. Its actions can only be limited by an SCP policy from the AWS Organizations management account, and even then not completely.

---

234\. A company is building a new web-based customer relationship management application. The application will use several Amazon EC2 instances that are backed by Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The application will also use an Amazon Aurora database. All data for the application must be encrypted at rest and in transit.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) certificates on the ALB to encrypt data in transit. Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to encrypt the EBS volumes and Aurora database storage at rest.  
B. Use the AWS root account to log in to the AWS Management Console. Upload the company’s encryption certificates. While in the root account, select the option to turn on encryption for all data at rest and in transit for the account.  
C. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to encrypt the EBS volumes and Aurora database storage at rest. Attach an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate to the ALB to encrypt data in transit.  
D. Use BitLocker to encrypt all data at rest. Import the company’s TLS certificate keys to AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) Attach the KMS keys to the ALB to encrypt data in transit.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: This question tests which service is responsible for what. Encryption at rest in AWS is KMS: EBS volumes and the Aurora cluster's storage have encryption turned on with a specified KMS key. Encryption in transit to the user is a TLS certificate on the load balancer, and certificates are issued and managed by ACM, free of charge and with automatic renewal. That exact pair — KMS for data on disk, ACM for traffic — is what the correct option describes.  
Why A is not selected: The services' roles are swapped: KMS doesn't issue TLS certificates for a load balancer, and ACM doesn't encrypt EBS volumes or database storage.  
Why B is not selected: There's no global "turn on encryption for everything in the account" switch, and doing everyday work under the root account contradicts basic security guidance.  
Why D is not selected: BitLocker is a Windows mechanism you maintain yourself, instead of managed volume encryption. And you can't attach a KMS key to a load balancer in place of an ACM certificate.

---

235\. A company is moving its on-premises Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. The database has several applications that write to the same tables. The applications need to be migrated one by one with a month in between each migration. Management has expressed concerns that the database has a high number of reads and writes. The data must be kept in sync across both databases throughout the migration.  
What should a solutions architect recommend?  
A. Use AWS DataSync for the initial migration. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create a change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select all tables.  
B. Use AWS DataSync for the initial migration. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create a full load plus change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select all tables.  
C. Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool with AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) using a memory optimized replication instance. Create a full load plus change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select all tables.  
D. Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool with AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) using a compute optimized replication instance. Create a full load plus change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select the largest tables.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: Moving from Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL is an engine change, so the AWS Schema Conversion Tool converts the schema and stored code. DMS then runs a full load plus change data capture task across all tables: it migrates the data first, then continuously applies changes, so the databases stay in sync throughout the months of staged application migration. Given the high volume of reads and writes, a memory-optimized replication instance is used — DMS keeps its change cache in memory.  
Why A is not selected: DataSync moves files, not database contents, and a CDC-only task with no initial load would leave the target database empty.  
Why B is not selected: The same mistake, with DataSync cast as the tool for the initial database migration.  
Why D is not selected: A compute-optimized instance is worse suited to CDC with a high volume of changes, and selecting only the largest tables would leave the rest out of sync.

---

236\. A company has a three-tier application for image sharing. The application uses an Amazon EC2 instance for the front-end layer, another EC2 instance for the application layer, and a third EC2 instance for a MySQL database. A solutions architect must design a scalable and highly available solution that requires the least amount of change to the application.  
Which solution meets these requirements?  
A. Use Amazon S3 to host the front-end layer. Use AWS Lambda functions for the application layer. Move the database to an Amazon DynamoDB table. Use Amazon S3 to store and serve users’ images.  
B. Use load-balanced Multi-AZ AWS Elastic Beanstalk environments for the front-end layer and the application layer. Move the database to an Amazon RDS DB instance with multiple read replicas to serve users’ images.  
C. Use Amazon S3 to host the front-end layer. Use a fleet of EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group for the application layer. Move the database to a memory optimized instance type to store and serve users’ images.  
D. Use load-balanced Multi-AZ AWS Elastic Beanstalk environments for the front-end layer and the application layer. Move the database to an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance. Use Amazon S3 to store and serve users’ images.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: Scalability and high availability are required with the least change to the application. Elastic Beanstalk takes the existing code as-is and deploys it into environments with a load balancer and multiple Availability Zones, the database moves to RDS in a Multi-AZ configuration, and user images are moved out to S3, taking the load off the instances.  
Why A is not selected: Moving to Lambda and DynamoDB means rewriting the application, which the requirement asks to avoid.  
Why B is not selected: Read replicas don't provide automatic failover, and storing images in a relational database is inefficient.  
Why C is not selected: A larger database instance solves neither the availability requirement nor image storage.

---

237\. An application running on an Amazon EC2 instance in VPC-A needs to access files in another EC2 instance in VPC- B. Both VPCs are in separate AWS accounts. The network administrator needs to design a solution to configure secure access to EC2 instance in VPC-B from VPC-A. The connectivity should not have a single point of failure or bandwidth concerns.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Set up a VPC peering connection between VPC-A and VPC-B.  
B. Set up VPC gateway endpoints for the EC2 instance running in VPC-B.  
C. Attach a virtual private gateway to VPC-B and set up routing from VPC-A.  
D. Create a private virtual interface (VIF) for the EC2 instance running in VPC-B and add appropriate routes from VPC-A.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Private connectivity is needed between networks in different accounts, with no single point of failure and no bandwidth limits. VPC peering satisfies all of this: it's a managed capability of the AWS network itself, has no intermediate devices that could fail, and has none of the bandwidth limits typical of tunnels.  
Why B is not selected: A gateway endpoint gives access to services like S3 and DynamoDB, not to instances in someone else's VPC.  
Why C is not selected: A virtual private gateway is the attachment point for a VPN or Direct Connect connection to your own site — it isn't used to connect two VPCs.  
Why D is not selected: A private virtual interface belongs to Direct Connect and is created for a connection from a data center, not between two VPCs.

---

238\. A company wants to experiment with individual AWS accounts for its engineer team. The company wants to be notified as soon as the Amazon EC2 instance usage for a given month exceeds a specific threshold for each account.  
What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Use Cost Explorer to create a daily report of costs by service. Filter the report by EC2 instances. Configure Cost Explorer to send an Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) notification when a threshold is exceeded.  
B. Use Cost Explorer to create a monthly report of costs by service. Filter the report by EC2 instances. Configure Cost Explorer to send an Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) notification when a threshold is exceeded.  
C. Use AWS Budgets to create a cost budget for each account. Set the period to monthly. Set the scope to EC2 instances. Set an alert threshold for the budget. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to receive a notification when a threshold is exceeded.  
D. Use AWS Cost and Usage Reports to create a report with hourly granularity. Integrate the report data with Amazon Athena. Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule an Athena query. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to receive a notification when a threshold is exceeded.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: A notification is needed when EC2 usage for a given month crosses a threshold, and as cheaply as possible. AWS Budgets is built exactly for this: a budget with a monthly period, filtered to the EC2 service, with an alert threshold, sends its notification to an SNS topic. The first two budgets in an account are free, and beyond that it costs cents per day. Cost Explorer and CUR are analysis tools — they don't send threshold notifications.  
Why A is not selected: Cost Explorer builds reports but can't send notifications when a threshold is exceeded — that's what Budgets is for.  
Why B is not selected: Same mistake: a Cost Explorer report isn't a notification mechanism.  
Why D is not selected: The combination of CUR, Athena, and scheduled queries works, but it's several services, custom queries, and paying for scans where a budget alone would do.

---

239\. A solutions architect needs to design a new microservice for a company’s application. Clients must be able to call an HTTPS endpoint to reach the microservice. The microservice also must use AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) to authenticate calls. The solutions architect will write the logic for this microservice by using a single AWS Lambda function that is written in Go 1.x.  
Which solution will deploy the function in the MOST operationally efficient way?  
A. Create an Amazon API Gateway REST API. Configure the method to use the Lambda function. Enable IAM authentication on the API.  
B. Create a Lambda function URL for the function. Specify AWS_IAM as the authentication type.  
C. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Deploy the function to [email protected] Integrate IAM authentication logic into the [email protected] function.  
D. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Deploy the function to CloudFront Functions. Specify AWS_IAM as the authentication type.  
Answer: B  
Review status: Corrected key (source: A; reviewed: B)  
Correction note: examtopics t1 q239 — Lambda function URL with AWS_IAM is the single-function microservice path; API Gateway adds a service that is not required  
Explanation: A single HTTPS endpoint for a single function with IAM authentication is needed. That is exactly what a Lambda function URL with the AWS_IAM authentication type (B) provides: no additional service, and the endpoint is created together with the function.  
Why A is not selected: IAM authorization on API Gateway technically works, but it adds a service that must be configured, versioned, and paid for. The requirements do not call for routing, API keys, or throttling — so this is an unnecessary layer.  
Why C is not selected: Lambda@Edge requires a CloudFront distribution, and the authentication logic would have to be written by hand — the most work of all the options.  
Why D is not selected: CloudFront Functions fail on two counts: they are lightweight JavaScript functions for editing headers with no network access, and they have no AWS_IAM authentication type.

240\. A company previously migrated its data warehouse solution to AWS. The company also has an AWS Direct Connect connection. Corporate office users query the data warehouse using a visualization tool. The average size of a query returned by the data warehouse is 50 MB and each webpage sent by the visualization tool is approximately 500 KB. Result sets returned by the data warehouse are not cached.  
Which solution provides the LOWEST data transfer egress cost for the company?  
A. Host the visualization tool on premises and query the data warehouse directly over the internet.  
B. Host the visualization tool in the same AWS Region as the data warehouse. Access it over the internet.  
C. Host the visualization tool on premises and query the data warehouse directly over a Direct Connect connection at a location in the same AWS Region.  
D. Host the visualization tool in the same AWS Region as the data warehouse and access it over a Direct Connect connection at a location in the same Region.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: Charges apply only to traffic leaving AWS. If the visualization tool runs in the same Region as the data warehouse, the 50 MB query results never leave AWS at all — only the 500 KB web pages go out, a hundred times less data. On top of that, this egress traffic is routed over Direct Connect, where the per-gigabyte rate is noticeably lower than the internet rate.  
Why A is not selected: The on-premises tool pulls the full 50 MB result of every query out of AWS, and at the most expensive internet rate on top of that. The worst option.  
Why B is not selected: The location is right and the outbound volume is small, but internet traffic costs more than traffic over Direct Connect.  
Why C is not selected: The connection is cheaper than the internet, but the full query results still go out — a hundred times more data than the pages.

---

241\. An online learning company is migrating to the AWS Cloud. The company maintains its student records in a PostgreSQL database. The company needs a solution in which its data is available and online across multiple AWS Regions at all times.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?  
A. Migrate the PostgreSQL database to a PostgreSQL cluster on Amazon EC2 instances.  
B. Migrate the PostgreSQL database to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance with the Multi-AZ feature turned on.  
C. Migrate the PostgreSQL database to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. Create a read replica in another Region.  
D. Migrate the PostgreSQL database to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. Set up DB snapshots to be copied to another Region.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The data must remain available online across multiple Regions at all times, with minimal operational overhead. An RDS read replica in another Region is created with a single operation, continuously receives changes, is available for queries, and can be promoted to a standalone database if needed.  
Why A is not selected: A self-managed PostgreSQL cluster on instances is the heaviest amount of maintenance.  
Why B is not selected: Multi-AZ operates within a single Region: there will be no data in other Regions.  
Why D is not selected: Copying snapshots to another Region does not provide online access: a database still has to be restored from them first.

---

242\. A company hosts its web application on AWS using seven Amazon EC2 instances. The company requires that the IP addresses of all healthy EC2 instances be returned in response to DNS queries.  
Which policy should be used to meet this requirement?  
A. Simple routing policy  
B. Latency routing policy  
C. Multivalue routing policy  
D. Geolocation routing policy  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The requirement is to return the addresses of all healthy instances in the DNS response. That's what the multivalue answer routing policy does: Route 53 returns up to eight records, each tied to its own health check, and unhealthy ones are excluded from the response.  
Why A is not selected: The simple routing policy returns records as-is and does not support health checks.  
Why B is not selected: The latency routing policy picks a single Region with the lowest latency, rather than returning the whole list.  
Why D is not selected: Geolocation picks a response based on the client's location and does not return a list of all healthy addresses.

---

243\. A medical research lab produces data that is related to a new study. The lab wants to make the data available with minimum latency to clinics across the country for their on-premises, file-based applications. The data files are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket that has read-only permissions for each clinic.  
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?  
A. Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway as a virtual machine (VM) on premises at each clinic  
B. Migrate the files to each clinic’s on-premises applications by using AWS DataSync for processing.  
C. Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway as a virtual machine (VM) on premises at each clinic.  
D. Attach an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system to each clinic’s on-premises servers.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The clinics need file-based access to data stored in S3, with minimum latency locally. A file gateway is deployed as a virtual machine at each clinic: it presents local applications with a familiar NFS or SMB share backed by the S3 bucket, and caches frequently read files locally. Applications don't change, and latency is governed by the local cache.  
Why B is not selected: DataSync is a tool for one-time or periodic transfers, not ongoing file access. Copying the entire dataset to every clinic is wasteful and doesn't provide a single source of truth.  
Why C is not selected: A volume gateway presents block volumes over iSCSI, while the clinics' applications work with files.  
Why D is not selected: An EFS file system cannot be mounted on arbitrary on-premises servers over the internet: that requires private connectivity to the VPC, and latency in that case would be governed by the link, not by a local cache.

---

244\. A company is using a content management system that runs on a single Amazon EC2 instance. The EC2 instance contains both the web server and the database software. The company must make its website platform highly available and must enable the website to scale to meet user demand.  
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?  
A. Move the database to Amazon RDS, and enable automatic backups. Manually launch another EC2 instance in the same Availability Zone. Configure an Application Load Balancer in the Availability Zone, and set the two instances as targets.  
B. Migrate the database to an Amazon Aurora instance with a read replica in the same Availability Zone as the existing EC2 instance. Manually launch another EC2 instance in the same Availability Zone. Configure an Application Load Balancer, and set the two EC2 instances as targets.
