Explanation: Deployments succeed and the files in the bucket are updated, but users still see the old version — meaning CloudFront is serving from cache. Objects are held at edge locations until their TTL expires, so an invalidation is needed after each deployment, and it's best to build that into the same delivery pipeline.  
Why A is not selected: A load balancer distributes traffic across instances, but the site is static and lives in a bucket — that has nothing to do with a stale cache.  
Why B is not selected: A cache in front of the database speeds up queries, but it isn't what's serving the stale files — the content delivery network is.  
Why D is not selected: Certificate validation is about TLS and has no bearing on content freshness.

---

287\. A company wants to migrate a Windows-based application from on premises to the AWS Cloud. The application has three tiers: an application tier, a business tier, and a database tier with Microsoft SQL Server. The company wants to use specific features of SQL Server such as native backups and Data Quality Services. The company also needs to share files for processing between the tiers.  
How should a solutions architect design the architecture to meet these requirements?  
A. Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx File Gateway for file sharing between the tiers.  
B. Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server for file sharing between the tiers.  
C. Host the application tier and the business tier on Amazon EC2 instances. Host the database tier on Amazon RDS. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) for file sharing between the tiers.  
D. Host the application tier and the business tier on Amazon EC2 instances. Host the database tier on Amazon RDS. Use a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume for file sharing between the tiers.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The scenario names SQL Server features that a managed service doesn't offer: native engine backups and Data Quality Services. So the database has to stay on an EC2 instance. Shared file exchange between tiers in a Windows environment is provided by Amazon FSx for Windows File Server — an SMB share with Windows ACLs, accessible from all three tiers.  
Why A is not selected: FSx File Gateway is meant for accessing FSx file systems from an on-premises network, but all the tiers are already in AWS — it would just be an unnecessary intermediary.  
Why C is not selected: RDS for SQL Server supports neither native backups the way the company uses them nor Data Quality Services — a direct violation of the requirements.  
Why D is not selected: Same problem with RDS, plus an EBS volume isn't a shared file resource that multiple instances can use.

---

288\. A company is migrating a Linux-based web server group to AWS. The web servers must access files in a shared file store for some content. The company must not make any changes to the application.  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?  
A. Create an Amazon S3 Standard bucket with access to the web servers.  
B. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an Amazon S3 bucket as the origin.  
C. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system on all web servers.  
D. Configure a General Purpose SSD (gp3) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Mount the EBS volume to all web servers.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: Shared file access for a group of Linux servers with no application changes is Amazon EFS. The file system is mounted over NFS on all the web servers across all Availability Zones, the application keeps working with ordinary paths and files, and the storage scales itself.  
Why A is not selected: S3 is object storage, accessed through an API. To use it, the application would have to be rewritten, which the requirements rule out.  
Why B is not selected: CloudFront in front of S3 speeds up delivery of static content, but it still doesn't give the servers a shared file system.  
Why D is not selected: An EBS volume attaches within a single Availability Zone, and a regular file system on it isn't designed for simultaneous writes from multiple servers.

---

289\. A company has an AWS Lambda function that needs read access to an Amazon S3 bucket that is located in the same AWS account.  
Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure manner?  
A. Apply an S3 bucket policy that grants read access to the S3 bucket.  
B. Apply an IAM role to the Lambda function. Apply an IAM policy to the role to grant read access to the S3 bucket.  
C. Embed an access key and a secret key in the Lambda function’s code to grant the required IAM permissions for read access to the S3 bucket.  
D. Apply an IAM role to the Lambda function. Apply an IAM policy to the role to grant read access to all S3 buckets in the account.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The correct way to grant permissions to any compute resource in AWS is a role. The Lambda function gets an execution role, and an IAM policy attached to that role grants s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on the specific bucket and, if needed, a specific prefix. The credentials involved are temporary: they're issued by STS, refresh automatically, and are never stored anywhere. The key phrase in the question is 'MOST secure manner' — between a role scoped to one bucket and a role scoped to all buckets, the former is chosen because least privilege applies even within a single account.  
Why A is not selected: A bucket policy describes who is allowed to access the resource, but the function still needs its own identity and permissions. Within a single account this is normally handled with a role, not by opening up the bucket.  
Why C is not selected: An access key embedded in the function's code is a long-lived secret sitting in the repository and the deployment package, and it can't be rotated automatically. The worst option offered.  
Why D is not selected: The role is the right approach, but the permissions are granted on every bucket in the account. That violates least privilege, and the question asks for the most secure option.

---

290\. A company hosts a web application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group that scales in response to user demand. The company wants to optimize cost savings without making a long- term commitment.  
Which EC2 instance purchasing option should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?  
A. Dedicated Instances only  
B. On-Demand Instances only  
C. A mix of On-Demand Instances and Spot Instances  
D. A mix of On-Demand Instances and Reserved Instances  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The company doesn't want a long-term commitment, so Reserved Instances and Savings Plans are out. That leaves a mixed group: a baseline on On-Demand Instances to guarantee availability, plus additional capacity for spikes on interruptible Spot Instances at up to a 90 percent discount.  
Why A is not selected: Dedicated Instances are the most expensive option and are only needed when there's a hardware-isolation requirement.  
Why B is not selected: On-Demand Instances alone don't provide any savings beyond the base price.  
Why D is not selected: Reserved Instances are exactly the one- or three-year commitment the company wants to avoid.

---

291\. A media company uses Amazon CloudFront for its publicly available streaming video content. The company wants to secure the video content that is hosted in Amazon S3 by controlling who has access. Some of the company’s users are using a custom HTTP client that does not support cookies. Some of the company’s users are unable to change the hardcoded URLs that they are using for access.  
Which services or methods will meet these requirements with the LEAST impact to the users? (Choose two.)  
A. Signed cookies  
B. Signed URLs  
C. AWS AppSync  
D. JSON Web Token (JWT)  
E. AWS Secrets Manager  
Answer: AB  
Explanation: The scenario hides two separate user constraints, and each is solved by its own CloudFront mechanism. A client that doesn't support cookies can't work with signed cookies — for that user, a signed URL fits, since the signature lives in the link itself. Users whose URL is hardcoded and can't be changed can't switch to a signed URL — for them, signed cookies fit instead, because the address stays the same while the signature arrives in the Cookie header. So both mechanisms belong in the answer: each serves its own group with the least impact on users.  
Why C is not selected: AWS AppSync is a managed GraphQL API service. It has nothing to do with restricting access to content in CloudFront.  
Why D is not selected: A JWT by itself isn't an authorization mechanism in CloudFront — validating such a token would require writing a Lambda@Edge function. That's development work, not 'least impact.'  
Why E is not selected: Secrets Manager stores application secrets. It doesn't manage viewer access to video files.

---

292\. A company is preparing a new data platform that will ingest real-time streaming data from multiple sources. The company needs to transform the data before writing the data to Amazon S3. The company needs the ability to use SQL to query the transformed data.  
Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)  
A. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to transform the data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to write the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.  
B. Use Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) to stream the data. Use AWS Glue to transform the data and to write the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.  
C. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to ingest the data. Use Amazon EMR to transform the data and to write the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.  
D. Use Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) to stream the data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to transform the data and to write the data to Amazon S3. Use the Amazon RDS query editor to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.  
E. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the data. Use AWS Glue to transform the data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to write the data to Amazon S3. Use the Amazon RDS query editor to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.  
Answer: AB  
Explanation: Three things are required: ingesting streaming data, transforming it before it's written, and being able to query the result with SQL. Both working combinations end in S3 and Athena. The first: Kinesis Data Streams ingests the stream, Kinesis Data Analytics transforms it on the fly, and Firehose delivers the result to S3 (A). The second: Amazon MSK ingests the stream, and AWS Glue performs the transformation and writes to S3 (B).  
Why C is not selected: DMS migrates data out of databases — it doesn't ingest real-time streams from multiple sources.  
Why D is not selected: Data in S3 cannot be queried through the Amazon RDS query editor — that tool works against the database itself.  
Why E is not selected: The same mistake with the RDS query editor, which cannot reach objects in S3.

---

293\. A company has an on-premises volume backup solution that has reached its end of life. The company wants to use AWS as part of a new backup solution and wants to maintain local access to all the data while it is backed up on AWS. The company wants to ensure that the data backed up on AWS is automatically and securely transferred.  
Which solution meets these requirements?  
A. Use AWS Snowball to migrate data out of the on-premises solution to Amazon S3. Configure on-premises systems to mount the Snowball S3 endpoint to provide local access to the data.  
B. Use AWS Snowball Edge to migrate data out of the on-premises solution to Amazon S3. Use the Snowball Edge file interface to provide on-premises systems with local access to the data.  
C. Use AWS Storage Gateway and configure a cached volume gateway. Run the Storage Gateway software appliance on premises and configure a percentage of data to cache locally. Mount the gateway storage volumes to provide local access to the data.  
D. Use AWS Storage Gateway and configure a stored volume gateway. Run the Storage Gateway software appliance on premises and map the gateway storage volumes to on-premises storage. Mount the gateway storage volumes to provide local access to the data.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: The key requirement is preserving local access to all the data, not just part of it. That's exactly what Storage Gateway does in stored volume mode: the complete dataset stays on local disks, while snapshots go up to S3 asynchronously and encrypted. Backup becomes automatic, and access latency stays local.  
Why A is not selected: Snowball is a one-time transport device — it has no persistent S3 endpoint to mount and doesn't provide automatic, ongoing uploads.  
Why B is not selected: Snowball Edge is also meant for a one-time transfer and isn't a persistent backup solution.  
Why C is not selected: Cached volume mode keeps only a portion of the data locally, but the requirement calls for local access to the entire volume.

---

294\. An application that is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances needs to access an Amazon S3 bucket. Traffic must not traverse the internet.  
How should a solutions architect configure access to meet these requirements?  
A. Create a private hosted zone by using Amazon Route 53.  
B. Set up a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC.  
C. Configure the EC2 instances to use a NAT gateway to access the S3 bucket.  
D. Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the VPC and the S3 bucket.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: There's one requirement: traffic must not cross the internet. For S3, that's a gateway VPC endpoint — a route to the service prefix is added to the VPC's route tables, traffic stays within the AWS network, and there's no charge for the endpoint itself. On top of that, the bucket can be locked down with an aws:SourceVpce condition so it only accepts requests through this endpoint. The same technique is covered in {{q:91,480,710}}.  
Why A is not selected: A Route 53 private hosted zone handles name resolution within the VPC and has no effect on the route to S3.  
Why C is not selected: A NAT gateway is a path out to the internet — it directly violates the requirement, and it also charges for processed traffic.  
Why D is not selected: A Site-to-Site VPN connects a VPC to an external network, not to the S3 service — no such construct exists.

---

295\. An ecommerce company stores terabytes of customer data in the AWS Cloud. The data contains personally identifiable information (PII). The company wants to use the data in three applications. Only one of the applications needs to process the PII. The PII must be removed before the other two applications process the data.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Store the data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Create a proxy application layer to intercept and process the data that each application requests.  
B. Store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Process and transform the data by using S3 Object Lambda before returning the data to the requesting application.  
C. Process the data and store the transformed data in three separate Amazon S3 buckets so that each application has its own custom dataset. Point each application to its respective S3 bucket.  
D. Process the data and store the transformed data in three separate Amazon DynamoDB tables so that each application has its own custom dataset. Point each application to its respective DynamoDB table.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: It's the same data, but different applications need different views of it. S3 Object Lambda lets you attach a function to an access point: it transforms the object on the fly as it's returned, so two applications get a version with the personal data removed while the third gets the original. No extra copies of the data appear, and all the logic fits in a single function.  
Why A is not selected: A custom proxy layer is an application that has to be written, scaled, and maintained.  
Why C is not selected: Three copies of terabytes of data mean triple the storage cost and constant synchronization.  
Why D is not selected: The same idea, but in DynamoDB, where storing terabytes is even more expensive and requires rewriting how the data is accessed.

---

296\. A development team has launched a new application that is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances inside a development VPC. A solutions architect needs to create a new VPC in the same account. The new VPC will be peered with the development VPC. The VPC CIDR block for the development VPC is 192.168.0.0/24. The solutions architect needs to create a CIDR block for the new VPC. The CIDR block must be valid for a VPC peering connection to the development VPC.  
What is the SMALLEST CIDR block that meets these requirements?  
A. 10.0.1.0/32  
B. 192.168.0.0/24  
C. 192.168.1.0/32  
D. 10.0.1.0/24  
Answer: D  
Explanation: Two constraints apply. Peered VPC address ranges must not overlap, so 192.168.0.0/24 and anything within it are out. And the smallest allowed VPC block size is /28, so a /32 mask is never valid at all. Of the options given, only 10.0.1.0/24 is left.  
Why A is not selected: A /32 mask designates a single address — a VPC can't be created with that block; the minimum is /28.  
Why B is not selected: This block matches the existing network's block exactly, and overlapping address ranges make peering impossible.  
Why C is not selected: Again a /32 mask, which is invalid for a VPC, and the address also falls within the neighboring network's range.

---

297\. A company deploys an application on five Amazon EC2 instances. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) distributes traffic to the instances by using a target group. The average CPU usage on each of the instances is below 10% most of the time, with occasional surges to 65%.  
A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to automate the scalability of the application. The solution must optimize the cost of the architecture and must ensure that the application has enough CPU resources when surges occur.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that enters the ALARM state when the CPUUtilization metric is less than 20%. Create an AWS Lambda function that the CloudWatch alarm invokes to terminate one of the EC2 instances in the ALB target group.  
B. Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Select the existing ALB as the load balancer and the existing target group as the target group. Set a target tracking scaling policy that is based on the ASGAverageCPUUtilization metric. Set the minimum instances to 2, the desired capacity to 3, the maximum instances to 6, and the target value to 50%. Add the EC2 instances to the Auto Scaling group.  
C. Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Select the existing ALB as the load balancer and the existing target group as the target group. Set the minimum instances to 2, the desired capacity to 3, and the maximum instances to 6. Add the EC2 instances to the Auto Scaling group.  
D. Create two Amazon CloudWatch alarms. Configure the first CloudWatch alarm to enter the ALARM state when the average CPUUtilization metric is below 20%. Configure the second CloudWatch alarm to enter the ALARM state when the average CPUUtilization matric is above 50%. Configure the alarms to publish to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send an email message. After receiving the message, log in to decrease or increase the number of EC2 instances that are running.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The instances already exist and the load balancer and target group are already configured — what's needed is automatic scaling without overpaying. An Auto Scaling group is created that uses the same load balancer and the same target group, with a target tracking policy based on average CPU utilization: capacity grows during a spike up to 65 percent and shrinks back down to the minimum during quiet periods.  
Why A is not selected: A custom function that terminates instances on a signal can't scale up and bypasses the standard scaling mechanisms.  
Why C is not selected: A group with no scaling policy simply holds a fixed instance count and doesn't react to spikes.  
Why D is not selected: Manually changing the instance count after receiving an email isn't automation — and automation is what's required.

---

298\. A company is running a critical business application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group and access an Amazon RDS DB instance.  
The design did not pass an operational review because the EC2 instances and the DB instance are all located in a single Availability Zone. A solutions architect must update the design to use a second Availability Zone.  
Which solution will make the application highly available?  
A. Provision a subnet in each Availability Zone. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance with connections to each network.  
B. Provision two subnets that extend across both Availability Zones. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance with connections to each network.  
C. Provision a subnet in each Availability Zone. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance for Multi-AZ deployment.  
D. Provision a subnet that extends across both Availability Zones. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance for Multi-AZ deployment.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: A subnet in AWS always belongs to exactly one Availability Zone, so there's no such thing as a subnet that 'spans' multiple zones. The correct approach: one subnet per Availability Zone, the Auto Scaling group spreads the instances across both, and the database is switched to a Multi-AZ deployment with synchronous replication and automatic failover.  
Why A is not selected: The subnets are set up correctly, but the database still stays in a single zone — 'connections to each network' doesn't add fault tolerance to it.  
Why B is not selected: A subnet cannot span two Availability Zones, and the database again remains a single point of failure.  
Why D is not selected: The same spanning-subnet mistake, even though the database is configured correctly.

---

299\. A research laboratory needs to process approximately 8 TB of data. The laboratory requires sub-millisecond latencies and a minimum throughput of 6 GBps for the storage subsystem. Hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances that run Amazon Linux will distribute and process the data.  
Which solution will meet the performance requirements?  
A. Create an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system. Sat each volume’ tiering policy to ALL. Import the raw data into the file system. Mount the fila system on the EC2 instances.  
B. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the raw data. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system that uses persistent SSD storage. Select the option to import data from and export data to Amazon S3. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.  
C. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the raw data. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system that uses persistent HDD storage. Select the option to import data from and export data to Amazon S3. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.  
D. Create an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system. Set each volume’s tiering policy to NONE. Import the raw data into the file system. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: Hard numbers are specified: sub-millisecond latency and at least 6 GBps of throughput while hundreds of Linux instances are working. That profile matches Amazon FSx for Lustre on persistent SSD storage — it's the only option that delivers those numbers. The source data lives in S3 and is linked to the file system through import/export, which is convenient both for loading data and for saving results.  
Why A is not selected: FSx for NetApp ONTAP is a general-purpose file service — it isn't built for gigabyte-per-second throughput to hundreds of clients, and its tiering policy would also push data down to a slower storage tier.  
Why C is not selected: Persistent storage on HDD disks can't deliver sub-millisecond latency: mechanical disks are inherently slower.  
Why D is not selected: Turning off tiering removes one problem, but ONTAP's performance still doesn't reach the required numbers.

---

300\. A company needs to migrate a legacy application from an on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud because of hardware capacity constraints. The application runs 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. The application’s database storage continues to grow over time.  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon S3.  
B. Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon RDS On-Demand Instances.  
C. Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon Aurora Reserved Instances.  
D. Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon RDS Reserved Instances.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The application runs continuously around the clock, and the database storage keeps growing over time. For steady, constant load, Reserved Instances are the cheapest option — a discount of up to three-quarters off the On-Demand price. Aurora also expands its storage automatically, so the growing volume needs no manual intervention, and Aurora Reserved Instances lower the cost of the data layer as well.  
Why A is not selected: AWS can reclaim Spot Instances at any time — unacceptable for an application that must run around the clock — and S3 doesn't replace a relational database.  
Why B is not selected: On-Demand RDS instances are billed at the full rate, even though the load is constant and predictable.  
Why D is not selected: Here it's the opposite: the discount applies to the database, but the largest layer — the application — is billed at the full rate.

---

301\. A university research laboratory needs to migrate 30 TB of data from an on-premises Windows file server to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. The laboratory has a 1 Gbps network link that many other departments in the university share.  
The laboratory wants to implement a data migration service that will maximize the performance of the data transfer. However, the laboratory needs to be able to control the amount of bandwidth that the service uses to minimize the impact on other departments. The data migration must take place within the next 5 days.  
Which AWS solution will meet these requirements?  
A. AWS Snowcone  
B. Amazon FSx File Gateway  
C. AWS DataSync  
D. AWS Transfer Family  
Answer: C  
Explanation: Thirty terabytes over a gigabit link takes roughly three days at full utilization, so hitting the five-day window is possible as long as the link isn't fully occupied by other traffic. The main requirement is controlling the bandwidth used, and that's exactly what AWS DataSync provides: a task can have a bandwidth limit set on it, and it transfers data over parallel streams with integrity checks and can write directly into FSx for Windows File Server.  
Why A is not selected: Snowcone only holds a few terabytes — 30 TB would require multiple devices, and shipping time would eat into the deadline.  
Why B is not selected: FSx File Gateway provides ongoing access to a file system from an on-premises network, but it isn't a one-time migration tool with bandwidth control.  
Why D is not selected: AWS Transfer Family provides SFTP, FTPS, and FTP over S3 and EFS — it offers neither bulk migration with bandwidth limiting nor writes into FSx.

---

302\. A company wants to create a mobile app that allows users to stream slow-motion video clips on their mobile devices. Currently, the app captures video clips and uploads the video clips in raw format into an Amazon S3 bucket. The app retrieves these video clips directly from the S3 bucket. However, the videos are large in their raw format.  
Users are experiencing issues with buffering and playback on mobile devices. The company wants to implement solutions to maximize the performance and scalability of the app while minimizing operational overhead.  
Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)  
A. Deploy Amazon CloudFront for content delivery and caching.  
B. Use AWS DataSync to replicate the video files across AW'S Regions in other S3 buckets.  
C. Use Amazon Elastic Transcoder to convert the video files to more appropriate formats.  
D. Deploy an Auto Sealing group of Amazon EC2 instances in Local Zones for content delivery and caching.  
E. Deploy an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to convert the video files to more appropriate formats.  
Answer: AC  
Explanation: There are two separate problems, each solved on its own. The files are too large in their raw form — they need to be transcoded into formats and bitrates suited to mobile devices, which is what the managed Amazon Elastic Transcoder does (C). Latency and buffering for users around the world are addressed with edge caching, meaning a CloudFront distribution placed in front of the bucket (A).  
Why B is not selected: Copying files to buckets in other Regions increases storage costs and requires its own routing logic, while a CDN cache achieves the same effect more cheaply.  
Why D is not selected: A custom fleet of instances in Local Zones for content delivery is infrastructure that has to be maintained, instead of using a ready-made delivery network.  
Why E is not selected: Transcoding on self-managed instances means managing a fleet and queues instead of using a managed transcoding service.

---

303\. A company is launching a new application deployed on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster and is using the Fargate launch type for ECS tasks. The company is monitoring CPU and memory usage because it is expecting high traffic to the application upon its launch. However, the company wants to reduce costs when utilization decreases.  
What should a solutions architect recommend?  
A. Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to scale at certain periods based on previous traffic patterns.  
B. Use an AWS Lambda function to scale Amazon ECS based on metric breaches that trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.  
C. Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling with simple scaling policies to scale when ECS metric breaches trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.  
D. Use AWS Application Auto Scaling with target tracking policies to scale when ECS metric breaches trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: The tasks run on Fargate, so there are no instances to scale at all. The number of service tasks is controlled by AWS Application Auto Scaling: a target tracking policy holds a set CPU or memory utilization level, adding tasks at the peak and removing them during a lull — automatically cutting costs.  
Why A is not selected: EC2 Auto Scaling manages instances, which don't exist with the Fargate launch type, and scaling based on past patterns doesn't respond to actual load.  
Why B is not selected: A custom function that resizes the service based on signals is code that has to be written and maintained, whereas a built-in policy does the same thing.  
Why C is not selected: Again, scaling EC2 instances, which don't exist in this architecture.

---

304\. A company recently created a disaster recovery site in a different AWS Region. The company needs to transfer large amounts of data back and forth between NFS file systems in the two Regions on a periodic basis.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Use AWS DataSync.  
B. Use AWS Snowball devices.  
C. Set up an SFTP server on Amazon EC2.  
D. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS).  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Periodic, bidirectional transfer of large volumes between NFS file systems in two Regions is a textbook AWS DataSync task. It works between storage locations within AWS, runs on a schedule, transfers only the changes, verifies integrity, and requires no servers or scripts.  
Why B is not selected: Snowball devices are meant for a one-time transfer over a weak link, not for regular synchronization between AWS Regions.  
Why C is not selected: A self-managed SFTP server on an instance is a machine and scripts that would have to be maintained.  
Why D is not selected: DMS migrates database data, not file system contents.

---

305\. A company is designing a shared storage solution for a gaming application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud. The company needs the ability to use SMB clients to access data. The solution must be fully managed.  
Which AWS solution meets these requirements?  
A. Create an AWS DataSync task that shares the data as a mountable file system. Mount the file system to the application server.  
B. Create an Amazon EC2 Windows instance. Install and configure a Windows file share role on the instance. Connect the application server to the file share.  
C. Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.  
D. Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Assign an IAM role to the application to grant access to the S3 bucket. Mount the S3 bucket to the application server.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The requirements are simple and specific: SMB access and a fully managed solution. That's Amazon FSx for Windows File Server — a file system with native SMB, Windows ACL support, and Active Directory integration, all managed by AWS. For the exam: SMB maps to FSx for Windows, NFS maps to EFS, object access via API maps to S3, and a self-managed file server on EC2 violates the 'fully managed' requirement.  
Why A is not selected: DataSync moves data between storage locations and doesn't provide a mountable file system.  
Why B is not selected: A file server on a Windows instance would have to be patched, backed up, and scaled manually. The managed-service requirement is violated.  
Why D is not selected: S3 is object storage and doesn't support SMB. A bucket can only be mounted with third-party tools, and without full file semantics.

---

306\. A company wants to run an in-memory database for a latency-sensitive application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The application processes more than 100,000 transactions each minute and requires high network throughput. A solutions architect needs to provide a cost-effective network design that minimizes data transfer charges.  
Which solution meets these requirements?  
A. Launch all EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone within the same AWS Region. Specify a placement group with cluster strategy when launching EC2 instances.  
B. Launch all EC2 instances in different Availability Zones within the same AWS Region. Specify a placement group with partition strategy when launching EC2 instances.  
C. Deploy an Auto Scaling group to launch EC2 instances in different Availability Zones based on a network utilization target.  
D. Deploy an Auto Scaling group with a step scaling policy to launch EC2 instances in different Availability Zones.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The goal is maximum network throughput, minimum latency, and minimum data transfer charges. All of this comes from placing the instances in a single Availability Zone within a cluster placement group: the machines end up close together on the same network segment, and traffic within a zone between private addresses isn't charged.  
Why B is not selected: Different Availability Zones mean cross-AZ data transfer charges and higher latency, and the partition strategy is designed for spreading instances across racks for fault tolerance.  
Why C is not selected: Spreading across zones again introduces cross-AZ traffic, and scaling based on network utilization doesn't address the latency requirement.  
Why D is not selected: The same cross-AZ charge problem, and step scaling has nothing to do with network performance.

---

307\. A company that primarily runs its application servers on premises has decided to migrate to AWS. The company wants to minimize its need to scale its Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (iSCSI) storage on premises.  
The company wants only its recently accessed data to remain stored locally.  
Which AWS solution should the company use to meet these requirements?  
A. Amazon S3 File Gateway  
B. AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway  
C. AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway stored volumes  
D. AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway cached volumes  
Answer: D  
Explanation: Two words determine the answer. iSCSI means block-level access, so a Volume Gateway is needed: S3 File Gateway serves files over NFS and SMB, and Tape Gateway emulates a tape library. "Only its recently accessed data to remain stored locally" points to the volume mode: in cached volumes, the primary dataset lives in AWS while the on-premises side keeps a cache of the hot blocks, so there's no need to grow local capacity. Stored volumes work the opposite way — the full copy is kept locally, and only snapshots go to AWS.  
Why A is not selected: S3 File Gateway provides file access over NFS and SMB. It does not suit an application that works over iSCSI.  
Why B is not selected: Tape Gateway is a virtual tape library for backups. It is not storage for an application's day-to-day operation.  
Why C is not selected: Stored volumes keep a full copy of the data on premises, so the need for local capacity stays the same. The requirement to "minimize the need to scale local storage" is not met.

---

308\. A company has multiple AWS accounts that use consolidated billing. The company runs several active high performance Amazon RDS for Oracle On-Demand DB instances for 90 days. The company’s finance team has access to AWS Trusted Advisor in the consolidated billing account and all other AWS accounts.  
The finance team needs to use the appropriate AWS account to access the Trusted Advisor check recommendations for RDS. The finance team must review the appropriate Trusted Advisor check to reduce RDS costs.  
Which combination of steps should the finance team take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)  
A. Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations from the account where the RDS instances are running.  
B. Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations from the consolidated billing account to see all RDS instance checks at the same time.  
C. Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon RDS Reserved Instance Optimization.  
D. Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon RDS Idle DB Instances.  
E. Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon Redshift Reserved Node Optimization.  
Answer: BC  
Review status: Corrected key (source: BD; reviewed: BC); Low-confidence audit  
Correction note: The instances are described as active, so running the Idle DB Instances check (D) on them would show nothing — it looks for databases with no connections. Reducing the cost of instances that have been running continuously for 90 days is what the RDS Reserved Instance Optimization check (C) does, and RI recommendations are consolidated in the payer account (B)  
Explanation: The instances run continuously for 90 days, so the savings come from moving to Reserved Instances, which is exactly what the Trusted Advisor "Amazon RDS Reserved Instance Optimization" check flags (C). You need to view it in the consolidated billing account (B): RI recommendations are calculated across the whole organization at once, not per individual account.  
Why A is not selected: Recommendations from the account where the instances run would have to be collected account by account, and purchasing RIs that way wouldn't account for the organization's combined usage.  
Why D is not selected: The "Idle DB Instances" check looks for databases with no connections over the past several days. The question explicitly states the instances are active, so this check won't flag them. This was the error in the dump's answer key.  
Why E is not selected: The Redshift Reserved Node check applies to a different service and has nothing to do with RDS.

---

309\. A solutions architect needs to optimize storage costs. The solutions architect must identify any Amazon S3 buckets that are no longer being accessed or are rarely accessed.  
Which solution will accomplish this goal with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Analyze bucket access patterns by using the S3 Storage Lens dashboard for advanced activity metrics.  
B. Analyze bucket access patterns by using the S3 dashboard in the AWS Management Console.  
C. Turn on the Amazon CloudWatch BucketSizeBytes metric for buckets. Analyze bucket access patterns by using the metrics data with Amazon Athena.  
D. Turn on AWS CloudTrail for S3 object monitoring. Analyze bucket access patterns by using CloudTrail logs that are integrated with Amazon CloudWatch Logs.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: S3 Storage Lens is a built-in storage analytics dashboard: it shows size and object count across all buckets, and — with advanced activity metrics turned on — access frequency as well. Nothing needs to be configured or analyzed manually.  
Why B is not selected: The standard S3 console shows bucket contents, but not summarized access statistics.  
Why C is not selected: The bucket size metric reflects volume, not access frequency, and requires its own analysis.  
Why D is not selected: Enabling object-level event logging in CloudTrail sharply increases log volume and requires writing your own queries — considerably more operational overhead.

---

310\. A company sells datasets to customers who do research in artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML). The datasets are large, formatted files that are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket in the us-east-1 Region. The company hosts a web application that the customers use to purchase access to a given dataset. The web application is deployed on multiple Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. After a purchase is made, customers receive an S3 signed URL that allows access to the files.  
The customers are distributed across North America and Europe. The company wants to reduce the cost that is associated with data transfers and wants to maintain or improve performance.  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?  
A. Configure S3 Transfer Acceleration on the existing S3 bucket. Direct customer requests to the S3 Transfer Acceleration endpoint. Continue to use S3 signed URLs for access control.  
B. Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the existing S3 bucket as the origin. Direct customer requests to the CloudFront URL. Switch to CloudFront signed URLs for access control.  
C. Set up a second S3 bucket in the eu-central-1 Region with S3 Cross-Region Replication between the buckets. Direct customer requests to the closest Region. Continue to use S3 signed URLs for access control.  
D. Modify the web application to enable streaming of the datasets to end users. Configure the web application to read the data from the existing S3 bucket. Implement access control directly in the application.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The cost comes from data transferred out of S3 to customers in North America and Europe. Putting CloudFront in front of the bucket reduces cost (CloudFront's data transfer out rate is lower than S3's direct rate) while also bringing the files closer to users. Access control then shifts to CloudFront signed URLs — S3 signed URLs don't apply once requests go through the distribution.  
Why A is not selected: Transfer Acceleration speeds up uploads into the bucket and is billed as an add-on: costs would increase, not decrease.  
Why C is not selected: A second bucket with Cross-Region Replication doubles the storage cost for these large datasets and adds a charge for the replication itself.  
Why D is not selected: Proxying the data through the company's own application loads the instances, keeps the same amount of outbound traffic, and adds development work.

---

311\. A company is using AWS to design a web application that will process insurance quotes. Users will request quotes from the application. Quotes must be separated by quote type, must be responded to within 24 hours, and must not get lost. The solution must maximize operational efficiency and must minimize maintenance.  
Which solution meets these requirements?  
A. Create multiple Amazon Kinesis data streams based on the quote type. Configure the web application to send messages to the proper data stream. Configure each backend group of application servers to use the Kinesis Client Library (KCL) to pool messages from its own data stream.  
B. Create an AWS Lambda function and an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic for each quote type. Subscribe the Lambda function to its associated SNS topic. Configure the application to publish requests for quotes to the appropriate SNS topic.  
C. Create a single Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues to the SNS topic. Configure SNS message filtering to publish messages to the proper SQS queue based on the quote type. Configure each backend application server to use its own SQS queue.  
D. Create multiple Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery streams based on the quote type to deliver data streams to an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster. Configure the application to send messages to the proper delivery stream. Configure each backend group of application servers to search for the messages from OpenSearch Service and process them accordingly.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: Requests must be separated by type, must never be lost, and must be handled within 24 hours with minimal operational overhead. A single SNS topic with message filtering routes each message to its own SQS queue based on the type attribute, and each group of backend servers reads only its own queue. The queue retains messages for up to 14 days, so nothing gets lost.  
Why A is not selected: Multiple Kinesis streams require managing shards and writing custom code on top of the KCL — more operational overhead.  
Why B is not selected: An SNS topic with a subscriber function doesn't store messages: if processing fails, the request is lost.  
Why D is not selected: Firehose and an OpenSearch cluster form an analytics pipeline, not a task queue; searching an index for messages as a way to process them is highly impractical.

---

312\. A company has an application that runs on several Amazon EC2 instances. Each EC2 instance has multiple Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) data volumes attached to it. The application’s EC2 instance configuration and data need to be backed up nightly. The application also needs to be recoverable in a different AWS Region.  
Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?  
A. Write an AWS Lambda function that schedules nightly snapshots of the application’s EBS volumes and copies the snapshots to a different Region.  
B. Create a backup plan by using AWS Backup to perform nightly backups. Copy the backups to another Region. Add the application’s EC2 instances as resources.  
C. Create a backup plan by using AWS Backup to perform nightly backups. Copy the backups to another Region. Add the application’s EBS volumes as resources.  
D. Write an AWS Lambda function that schedules nightly snapshots of the application's EBS volumes and copies the snapshots to a different Availability Zone.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: Both the instance configuration and the data on every attached volume need to be backed up, and recovery needs to happen in a different Region. AWS Backup can treat an EC2 instance as a single resource: the backup includes the machine image plus all attached volumes. A plan with a nightly schedule and a cross-Region copy rule is configured once.  
Why A is not selected: A custom snapshot function means code, schedules, and error handling that you have to maintain, and it still doesn't preserve the instance configuration.  
Why C is not selected: If only the volumes are added to the plan, the instance configuration isn't backed up: you won't be able to restore the machine as a whole.  
Why D is not selected: Copying to a different Availability Zone doesn't protect against a Region-level failure, and a custom function again means extra operational overhead.

---

313\. A company is building a mobile app on AWS. The company wants to expand its reach to millions of users. The company needs to build a platform so that authorized users can watch the company’s content on their mobile devices.  
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?  
A. Publish content to a public Amazon S3 bucket. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to stream content.  
B. Set up IPsec VPN between the mobile app and the AWS environment to stream content.  
C. Use Amazon CloudFront. Provide signed URLs to stream content.  
D. Set up AWS Client VPN between the mobile app and the AWS environment to stream content.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: Millions of mobile users plus the requirement to allow only authorized users points to CloudFront with signed URLs. After verifying the user's entitlement, the application issues a signed URL with a limited lifetime (optionally tied to an IP address), content is served from the nearest edge location, and the bucket is locked down to direct access using origin access control. Scaling then becomes the CDN's job, not yours.  
Why A is not selected: A public bucket means access for everyone, which contradicts the "authorized users" requirement. KMS keys, moreover, don't "stream" anything — that's an encryption key management service.  
Why B is not selected: An IPsec VPN to a mobile app running on millions of devices is infeasible both technically and organizationally, and it doesn't solve the problem of delivering video.  
Why D is not selected: Client VPN is designed for connecting employees to a corporate network, not for publicly delivering content to millions of viewers. Its cost and complexity are out of proportion to the task.

---

314\. A company has an on-premises MySQL database used by the global sales team with infrequent access patterns.  
The sales team requires the database to have minimal downtime. A database administrator wants to migrate this database to AWS without selecting a particular instance type in anticipation of more users in the future.  
Which service should a solutions architect recommend?  
A. Amazon Aurora MySQL  
B. Amazon Aurora Serverless for MySQL  
C. Amazon Redshift Spectrum  
D. Amazon RDS for MySQL  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The key phrase is "without selecting a particular instance type." That's exactly what Aurora Serverless for MySQL provides: capacity is defined as a range of ACUs and scales automatically, including as new users arrive. Access is infrequent, so you pay little during quiet periods, and MySQL compatibility keeps the application unchanged.  
Why A is not selected: A standard Aurora cluster requires choosing an instance class — a direct contradiction of the requirement.  
Why C is not selected: Redshift Spectrum reads data in S3 for analytics and is not a transactional MySQL database.  
Why D is not selected: RDS for MySQL also requires choosing an instance class and manual resizing as load grows.

---

315\. A company experienced a breach that affected several applications in its on-premises data center. The attacker took advantage of vulnerabilities in the custom applications that were running on the servers. The company is now migrating its applications to run on Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants to implement a solution that actively scans for vulnerabilities on the EC2 instances and sends a report that details the findings.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Deploy AWS Shield to scan the EC2 instances for vulnerabilities. Create an AWS Lambda function to log any findings to AWS CloudTrail.  
B. Deploy Amazon Macie and AWS Lambda functions to scan the EC2 instances for vulnerabilities. Log any findings to AWS CloudTrail.  
C. Turn on Amazon GuardDuty. Deploy the GuardDuty agents to the EC2 instances. Configure an AWS Lambda function to automate the generation and distribution of reports that detail the findings.  
D. Turn on Amazon Inspector. Deploy the Amazon Inspector agent to the EC2 instances. Configure an AWS Lambda function to automate the generation and distribution of reports that detail the findings.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: The requirement is active scanning for vulnerabilities on the instances plus a report of the findings — that's Amazon Inspector. It runs continuous scanning through the SSM agent, matches installed packages against the CVE database, assesses network reachability of each vulnerability, and produces prioritized findings that can be exported and distributed. The distinction to remember: Inspector finds vulnerabilities, GuardDuty finds signs of compromise, Macie finds sensitive data, and Shield defends against DDoS.  
Why A is not selected: AWS Shield protects against availability attacks and performs no scanning at all.  
Why B is not selected: Macie looks for sensitive data in S3, not vulnerabilities in instance software.  
Why C is not selected: GuardDuty detects suspicious activity and signs of compromise, but it doesn't produce a list of vulnerable packages.

---

316\. A company uses an Amazon EC2 instance to run a script to poll for and process messages in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. The company wants to reduce operational costs while maintaining its ability to process a growing number of messages that are added to the queue.  
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?  
A. Increase the size of the EC2 instance to process messages faster.  
B. Use Amazon EventBridge to turn off the EC2 instance when the instance is underutilized.  
C. Migrate the script on the EC2 instance to an AWS Lambda function with the appropriate runtime.  
D. Use AWS Systems Manager Run Command to run the script on demand.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The script only polls the queue and processes messages, yet the instance is billed around the clock. A Lambda function with SQS as its event source runs only when messages arrive, scales automatically as their number grows, and is billed only for execution time.  
Why A is not selected: A larger instance speeds up processing, but costs would go up, not down.  
Why B is not selected: Turning the instance off on a schedule leaves messages unprocessed during that window and requires its own automation.  
Why D is not selected: Run Command runs the script on demand, but the instance still has to exist and be paid for.

---

317\. A company uses a legacy application to produce data in CSV format. The legacy application stores the output data in Amazon S3. The company is deploying a new commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) application that can perform complex SQL queries to analyze data that is stored in Amazon Redshift and Amazon S3 only. However, the COTS application cannot process the .csv files that the legacy application produces.  
The company cannot update the legacy application to produce data in another format. The company needs to implement a solution so that the COTS application can use the data that the legacy application produces.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Create an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job that runs on a schedule. Configure the ETL job to process the .csv files and store the processed data in Amazon Redshift.  
B. Develop a Python script that runs on Amazon EC2 instances to convert the .csv files to .sql files. Invoke the Python script on a cron schedule to store the output files in Amazon S3.  
C. Create an AWS Lambda function and an Amazon DynamoDB table. Use an S3 event to invoke the Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to perform an extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to process the .csv files and store the processed data in the DynamoDB table.  
D. Use Amazon EventBridge to launch an Amazon EMR cluster on a weekly schedule. Configure the EMR cluster to perform an extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to process the .csv files and store the processed data in an Amazon Redshift table.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The application can only work with Redshift and S3, but the data arrives as CSV. A scheduled AWS Glue job reads the files, transforms them, and loads them into Redshift — a ready-made ETL tool with no custom code and no cluster management.  
Why B is not selected: A custom script on EC2 instances means development and maintenance, and .sql files still wouldn't suit the application anyway.  
Why C is not selected: DynamoDB isn't among the data sources the application understands: it can't run SQL queries against it.  
Why D is not selected: A weekly EMR cluster means both added latency and node management, plus higher cost.

---

318\. A company recently migrated its entire IT environment to the AWS Cloud. The company discovers that users are provisioning oversized Amazon EC2 instances and modifying security group rules without using the appropriate change control process. A solutions architect must devise a strategy to track and audit these inventory and configuration changes.  
Which actions should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)  
A. Enable AWS CloudTrail and use it for auditing.  
B. Use data lifecycle policies for the Amazon EC2 instances.  
C. Enable AWS Trusted Advisor and reference the security dashboard.  
D. Enable AWS Config and create rules for auditing and compliance purposes.  
E. Restore previous resource configurations with an AWS CloudFormation template.  
Answer: AD  
Explanation: There are two separate requirements, met by two separate services. AWS CloudTrail records who called which API and when — for example, who launched an oversized instance or changed a security group rule (A). AWS Config tracks the configuration history of resources and lets you define compliance rules that flag violations — for example, disallowed instance types or overly permissive rules (D).  
Why B is not selected: Data lifecycle policies manage snapshots and images, not change auditing.  
Why C is not selected: Trusted Advisor gives general recommendations about account configuration, but it doesn't keep a change history or enforce compliance rules.  
Why E is not selected: CloudFormation can deploy infrastructure, but it isn't a tool for auditing or rolling back arbitrary changes.

---

319\. A company has hundreds of Amazon EC2 Linux-based instances in the AWS Cloud. Systems administrators have used shared SSH keys to manage the instances. After a recent audit, the company’s security team is mandating the removal of all shared keys. A solutions architect must design a solution that provides secure access to the EC2 instances.  
Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST amount of administrative overhead?  
A. Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to connect to the EC2 instances.  
B. Use AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to generate one-time SSH keys on demand.  
C. Allow shared SSH access to a set of bastion instances. Configure all other instances to allow only SSH access from the bastion instances.  
D. Use an Amazon Cognito custom authorizer to authenticate users. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to generate a temporary SSH key.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Shared SSH keys need to be removed while access is preserved. Session Manager achieves this without a single key and without open ports: an agent on the instance initiates an outbound connection to the service, permissions are described through IAM policies, actions are attributed to individual users, and sessions are logged to CloudWatch Logs or S3. The instance just needs a role with AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore. Administrative overhead is minimal: no bastions, no key distribution, no address lists.  
Why B is not selected: STS issues temporary AWS credentials, not SSH keys. No such mechanism exists.  
Why C is not selected: Bastions with shared keys don't solve the problem: shared keys remain, there are just fewer of them.  
Why D is not selected: Combining Cognito with a custom key-generation function is a homegrown system built around keys — the very thing the company asked to eliminate.

---

320\. A company is using a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances to ingest data from on-premises data sources. The data is in JSON format and ingestion rates can be as high as 1 MB/s. When an EC2 instance is rebooted, the data in-flight is lost. The company’s data science team wants to query ingested data in near-real time.  
Which solution provides near-real-time data querying that is scalable with minimal data loss?  
A. Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Use Kinesis Data Analytics to query the data.  
B. Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose with Amazon Redshift as the destination. Use Amazon Redshift to query the data.  
C. Store ingested data in an EC2 instance store. Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose with Amazon S3 as the destination. Use Amazon Athena to query the data.  
D. Store ingested data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Publish data to Amazon ElastiCache for Redis. Subscribe to the Redis channel to query the data.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The problem is that data is lost the moment the instance reboots, because it lives only in the instance's memory and on its disk. Kinesis Data Streams accepts records and stores them in the stream independently of consumer state, so a restart loses nothing, and Kinesis Data Analytics lets you query the data in near real time.  
Why B is not selected: Firehose buffers data and delivers it to Redshift with a delay of tens of seconds or more: that's no longer near-real time, and the buffer itself can also be lost if the source fails.  
Why C is not selected: Storing ingested data in an instance store keeps the original problem intact: everything disappears when the instance reboots.  
Why D is not selected: An EBS volume and a Redis channel form a homegrown setup with no delivery guarantees and no convenient way to query the ingested data.

---

321\. What should a solutions architect do to ensure that all objects uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket are encrypted?  
A. Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an s3:x-amz-acl header set.  
B. Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an s3:x-amz-acl header set to private.  
C. Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an aws:SecureTransport header set to true.  
D. Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an x-amz-server-side-encryption header set.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: You need to guarantee that an unencrypted object simply never lands in the bucket, rather than fix things after the fact. That's done with a bucket policy that explicitly denies s3:PutObject when the request lacks the x-amz-server-side-encryption header (or when its value isn't the one required — for example, not aws:kms). This Deny fires before the write: the client gets AccessDenied and must retry the request with encryption. Also remember the distinction: default encryption encrypts everything that arrives, while a Deny policy specifically forces the client to request encryption explicitly.  
Why A is not selected: The x-amz-acl header sets the object's access control list. It has nothing to do with encryption.  
Why B is not selected: Same issue: a value of private restricts who can see the object, but the object could still be written unencrypted.  
Why C is not selected: The aws:SecureTransport condition requires TLS, i.e., encryption in transit. Data would arrive over a secure connection and still be written to disk unencrypted — the question is about encryption at rest.

---

322\. A solutions architect is designing a multi-tier application for a company. The application's users upload images from a mobile device. The application generates a thumbnail of each image and returns a message to the user to confirm that the image was uploaded successfully.  
The thumbnail generation can take up to 60 seconds, but the company wants to provide a faster response time to its users to notify them that the original image was received. The solutions architect must design the application to asynchronously dispatch requests to the different application tiers.  
What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?  
A. Write a custom AWS Lambda function to generate the thumbnail and alert the user. Use the image upload process as an event source to invoke the Lambda function.  
B. Create an AWS Step Functions workflow. Configure Step Functions to handle the orchestration between the application tiers and alert the user when thumbnail generation is complete.  
C. Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) message queue. As images are uploaded, place a message on the SQS queue for thumbnail generation. Alert the user through an application message that the image was received.  
D. Create Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification topics and subscriptions. Use one subscription with the application to generate the thumbnail after the image upload is complete. Use a second subscription to message the user's mobile app by way of a push notification after thumbnail generation is complete.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The user needs an immediate response, while thumbnail generation can take up to a minute. An SQS queue solves this: the application places a message about the new image and immediately confirms the upload, while processors generate the thumbnail asynchronously, at their own pace, with a guarantee that the task won't be lost.  
Why A is not selected: A function that both generates the thumbnail and notifies the user leaves a sixty-second wait on the response path.  
Why B is not selected: Step Functions orchestrates the steps, but the user notification is still tied to the completion of generation, and the design is more complex.  
Why D is not selected: SNS doesn't store messages: if a subscriber fails, the thumbnail-generation task is lost.

---

323\. A company’s facility has badge readers at every entrance throughout the building. When badges are scanned, the readers send a message over HTTPS to indicate who attempted to access that particular entrance.  
A solutions architect must design a system to process these messages from the sensors. The solution must be highly available, and the results must be made available for the company’s security team to analyze.  
Which system architecture should the solutions architect recommend?  
A. Launch an Amazon EC2 instance to serve as the HTTPS endpoint and to process the messages. Configure the EC2 instance to save the results to an Amazon S3 bucket.  
B. Create an HTTPS endpoint in Amazon API Gateway. Configure the API Gateway endpoint to invoke an AWS Lambda function to process the messages and save the results to an Amazon DynamoDB table.  
C. Use Amazon Route 53 to direct incoming sensor messages to an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to process the messages and save the results to an Amazon DynamoDB table.  
D. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Configure a Site-to-Site VPN connection from the facility network to the VPC so that sensor data can be written directly to an S3 bucket by way of the VPC endpoint.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The readers send messages over HTTPS, so a managed HTTPS endpoint and a serverless processor are needed. API Gateway accepts the requests and invokes a Lambda function, which parses the message and writes the result to DynamoDB — all three components are highly available by default, scale on their own, and require no administration. The data in DynamoDB is available to the security team for analysis, if needed via export to S3 and Athena.  
Why A is not selected: A single EC2 instance is a single point of failure that requires patching, scaling, and monitoring. The high-availability requirement isn't met.  
Why C is not selected: Route 53 doesn't invoke Lambda functions: it's a DNS service. An HTTP endpoint, such as API Gateway, is needed between the client and the function.  
Why D is not selected: The readers send HTTPS requests, not files written to a bucket, and building a VPN to the building for this purpose is overkill.

---

324\. A company wants to implement a disaster recovery plan for its primary on-premises file storage volume. The file storage volume is mounted from an Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (iSCSI) device on a local storage server. The file storage volume holds hundreds of terabytes (TB) of data.  
The company wants to ensure that end users retain immediate access to all file types from the on-premises systems without experiencing latency.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of change to the company's existing infrastructure?  
A. Provision an Amazon S3 File Gateway as a virtual machine (VM) that is hosted on premises. Set the local cache to 10 TB. Modify existing applications to access the files through the NFS protocol. To recover from a disaster, provision an Amazon EC2 instance and mount the S3 bucket that contains the files.  
B. Provision an AWS Storage Gateway tape gateway. Use a data backup solution to back up all existing data to a virtual tape library. Configure the data backup solution to run nightly after the initial backup is complete. To recover from a disaster, provision an Amazon EC2 instance and restore the data to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume from the volumes in the virtual tape library.  
C. Provision an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway cached volume. Set the local cache to 10 TB. Mount the Volume Gateway cached volume to the existing file server by using iSCSI, and copy all files to the storage volume. Configure scheduled snapshots of the storage volume. To recover from a disaster, restore a snapshot to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume and attach the EBS volume to an Amazon EC2 instance.  
D. Provision an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway stored volume with the same amount of disk space as the existing file storage volume. Mount the Volume Gateway stored volume to the existing file server by using iSCSI, and copy all files to the storage volume. Configure scheduled snapshots of the storage volume. To recover from a disaster, restore a snapshot to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume and attach the EBS volume to an Amazon EC2 instance.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: End users must retain immediate access to all file types without latency, and changes to existing infrastructure must be minimal. Volume Gateway in stored volumes mode connects to the existing file server over the same iSCSI protocol, the full dataset stays on local disks, and scheduled snapshots go to AWS. In a disaster, a snapshot is restored to an EBS volume and attached to an instance.  
Why A is not selected: This involves both switching the protocol to NFS and modifying applications — a direct violation of the minimal-change requirement.  
Why B is not selected: Tape Gateway is designed for backup to a virtual tape library and doesn't provide immediate local access to files.  
Why C is not selected: Cached volumes mode keeps only 10 TB of cache locally out of hundreds of terabytes: access to the rest of the data would go to the cloud with noticeable latency.

---

325\. A company is hosting a web application from an Amazon S3 bucket. The application uses Amazon Cognito as an identity provider to authenticate users and return a JSON Web Token (JWT) that provides access to protected resources that are stored in another S3 bucket.  
Upon deployment of the application, users report errors and are unable to access the protected content. A solutions architect must resolve this issue by providing proper permissions so that users can access the protected content.  
Which solution meets these requirements?  
A. Update the Amazon Cognito identity pool to assume the proper IAM role for access to the protected content.  
B. Update the S3 ACL to allow the application to access the protected content.  
C. Redeploy the application to Amazon S3 to prevent eventually consistent reads in the S3 bucket from affecting the ability of users to access the protected content.  
D. Update the Amazon Cognito pool to use custom attribute mappings within the identity pool and grant users the proper permissions to access the protected content.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: A Cognito token by itself doesn't grant any AWS permissions. The flow works like this: the user authenticates in the user pool and receives a JWT, that token is then exchanged in the identity pool for temporary IAM role credentials, and it's that role that grants s3:GetObject on the protected bucket. An access error means the identity pool's role for authenticated users isn't configured (or is configured incorrectly). Keep the distinction in mind: the user pool handles "who this is," and the identity pool handles "what AWS permissions to give them."  
Why B is not selected: ACLs are a legacy S3 mechanism and can't grant permissions based on Cognito authentication results. The modern approach is a bucket policy plus a user role.  
Why C is not selected: S3 has long provided strong read-after-write consistency, and consistency has nothing to do with access errors.  
Why D is not selected: Custom attribute mapping helps pass along user information, but by itself it doesn't grant any AWS permissions: permissions come from the role that the identity pool issues.

---

326\. An image hosting company uploads its large assets to Amazon S3 Standard buckets. The company uses multipart upload in parallel by using S3 APIs and overwrites if the same object is uploaded again. For the first 30 days after upload, the objects will be accessed frequently. The objects will be used less frequently after 30 days, but the access patterns for each object will be inconsistent. The company must optimize its S3 storage costs while maintaining high availability and resiliency of stored assets.  
Which combination of actions should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)  
A. Move assets to S3 Intelligent-Tiering after 30 days.  
B. Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to clean up incomplete multipart uploads.  
C. Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to clean up expired object delete markers.  
D. Move assets to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 30 days.  
E. Move assets to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 30 days.  
Answer: AB  
Explanation: There are two independent cost items here. The first is the objects themselves: after 30 days access becomes rare but "inconsistent," i.e. unpredictable, which calls for Intelligent-Tiering (A) rather than a class that bills for retrieval. The second is incomplete multipart uploads (B): with parallel multipart uploads, parts of aborted operations remain in the bucket, aren't visible in the object listing, and are still billed as storage until a Lifecycle rule ("AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload") removes them. For large assets this invisible line item can sometimes account for a noticeable share of the bill.  
Why C is not selected: Cleaning up expired delete markers matters in a versioned bucket. The scenario describes overwriting objects, and a delete marker itself takes up zero storage — there's no savings here.  
Why D is not selected: Standard-IA charges a retrieval fee, and access after 30 days is described as inconsistent. Every unexpected access costs money, so Intelligent-Tiering is more cost-effective here.  
Why E is not selected: One Zone-IA stores a single copy in one Availability Zone, and the question requires maintaining high availability and fault tolerance.

---

327\. A solutions architect must secure a VPC network that hosts Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances contain highly sensitive data and run in a private subnet. According to company policy, the EC2 instances that run in the VPC can access only approved third-party software repositories on the internet for software product updates that use the third party’s URL. Other internet traffic must be blocked.  
Which solution meets these requirements?  
A. Update the route table for the private subnet to route the outbound traffic to an AWS Network Firewall firewall. Configure domain list rule groups.  
B. Set up an AWS WAF web ACL. Create a custom set of rules that filter traffic requests based on source and destination IP address range sets.  
C. Implement strict inbound security group rules. Configure an outbound rule that allows traffic only to the authorized software repositories on the internet by specifying the URLs.  
D. Configure an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the EC2 instances. Direct all outbound traffic to the ALB. Use a URL-based rule listener in the ALB’s target group for outbound access to the internet.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The restriction is stated in terms of domain names ("the third party's URL"), and security groups and network ACLs only work with addresses and ports. AWS Network Firewall can distinguish domains: a stateful rule with a domain list allows traffic to the listed names and blocks everything else, and the private subnet's traffic is routed through the firewall endpoint via the route table. This is the standard way to build a domain-based egress filter.  
Why B is not selected: AWS WAF protects inbound HTTP requests to your applications and doesn't filter outbound instance traffic.  
Why C is not selected: Security group rules can't specify a URL or domain name — only CIDR blocks, prefix lists, and other security groups.  
Why D is not selected: A load balancer distributes inbound requests to your targets. Outbound internet traffic isn't routed through it.

---

328\. A company is hosting a three-tier ecommerce application in the AWS Cloud. The company hosts the website on Amazon S3 and integrates the website with an API that handles sales requests.
