Why A is not selected: An Amazon EMR cluster running a Hive job reads the table itself, consuming read capacity units, and adds infrastructure to manage.  
Why C is not selected: Streams plus a Lambda function mean writing and maintaining custom processing code, whereas the built-in export accomplishes the same thing with a single setting.  
Why D is not selected: A periodic export via a Lambda function means both code and reading the table, and it's not a continuous backup but a scheduled snapshot.

---

491\. A solutions architect is designing an asynchronous application to process credit card data validation requests for a bank. The application must be secure and be able to process each request at least once.  
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Use AWS Lambda event source mapping. Set Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queues as the event source. Use AWS Key Management Service (SSE-KMS) for encryption. Add the kms:Decrypt permission for the Lambda execution role.  
B. Use AWS Lambda event source mapping. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queues as the event source. Use SQS managed encryption keys (SSE-SQS) for encryption. Add the encryption key invocation permission for the Lambda function.  
C. Use the AWS Lambda event source mapping. Set Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queues as the event source. Use AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Add the kms:Decrypt permission for the Lambda execution role.  
D. Use the AWS Lambda event source mapping. Set Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queues as the event source. Use AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) for encryption. Add the encryption key invocation permission for the Lambda function.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Three requirements: asynchronous processing, "at least once" delivery, and minimal cost with proper protection. "At least once" is exactly the guarantee that standard SQS queues provide, and standard queues are cheaper than FIFO queues and aren't limited by FIFO's throughput; FIFO is needed when strict ordering and exactly-once processing matter, and this scenario doesn't require that. Encrypting the card data with a KMS key the company manages makes sense here. Finally, the kms:Decrypt permission is granted to the function's execution role — the role, not the "function," is the IAM principal.  
Why B is not selected: A FIFO queue is more expensive than a standard queue and isn't needed here: the requirement is at-least-once delivery, not strict ordering. An SQS managed key also doesn't give the company control over the key, which is usually required for payment data.  
Why C is not selected: The encryption choice is correct, but FIFO again imposes unnecessary guarantees and extra cost compared with a standard queue.  
Why D is not selected: The queue type and encryption are correct, but the permissions are described incorrectly: the permission to use the KMS key (kms:Decrypt) is granted to the Lambda execution role, not to the "function" itself.

---

492\. A company has multiple AWS accounts for development work. Some staff consistently use oversized Amazon EC2 instances, which causes the company to exceed the yearly budget for the development accounts. The company wants to centrally restrict the creation of AWS resources in these accounts.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?  
A. Develop AWS Systems Manager templates that use an approved EC2 creation process. Use the approved Systems Manager templates to provision EC2 instances.  
B. Use AWS Organizations to organize the accounts into organizational units (OUs). Define and attach a service control policy (SCP) to control the usage of EC2 instance types.  
C. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function when an EC2 instance is created. Stop disallowed EC2 instance types.  
D. Set up AWS Service Catalog products for the staff to create the allowed EC2 instance types. Ensure that staff can deploy EC2 instances only by using the Service Catalog products.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The restriction needs to apply centrally across multiple accounts without requiring development work. That calls for an SCP: the development accounts are grouped into a separate OU, and a policy with a Deny on ec2:RunInstances is attached, conditioned on the instance type not being in the allowed list (the ec2:InstanceType condition). The deny applies to every principal in the accounts, including root, and can't be bypassed with local policies. There's no code or product catalog to maintain.  
Why A is not selected: Systems Manager templates describe a process but don't prohibit anything: staff can still launch an instance outside the template.  
Why C is not selected: Reacting with a function after an instance has already been created means writing code and paying for the time a large instance ran before being caught. There's no preventive block.  
Why D is not selected: Service Catalog provides a convenient catalog of approved configurations, but it requires preparing products and doesn't stop instances from being created directly unless permissions are restricted separately.

---

493\. A company wants to use artificial intelligence (AI) to determine the quality of its customer service calls. The company currently manages calls in four different languages, including English. The company will offer new languages in the future. The company does not have the resources to regularly maintain machine learning (ML) models.  
The company needs to create written sentiment analysis reports from the customer service call recordings. The customer service call recording text must be translated into English.  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)  
A. Use Amazon Comprehend to translate the audio recordings into English.  
B. Use Amazon Lex to create the written sentiment analysis reports.  
C. Use Amazon Polly to convert the audio recordings into text.  
D. Use Amazon Transcribe to convert the audio recordings in any language into text.  
E. Use Amazon Translate to translate text in any language to English.  
F. Use Amazon Comprehend to create the sentiment analysis reports.  
Answer: DEF  
Explanation: The pipeline is built from three managed services, each handling one step. Amazon Transcribe converts the call recordings into text in any supported language (D). Amazon Translate translates that text into English (E). Amazon Comprehend performs the sentiment analysis and produces the material for the reports (F). No custom machine learning models need to be maintained at any step.  
Why A is not selected: Comprehend analyzes text — it can neither translate nor transcribe audio.  
Why B is not selected: Amazon Lex builds conversational bots, not sentiment analysis reports.  
Why C is not selected: Amazon Polly works in the opposite direction — it turns text into speech.

---

494\. A company uses Amazon EC2 instances to host its internal systems. As part of a deployment operation, an administrator tries to use the AWS CLI to terminate an EC2 instance. However, the administrator receives a 403 (Access Denied) error message.  
The administrator is using an IAM role that has the following IAM policy attached:  
What is the cause of the unsuccessful request?  
![Exhibit for question 494](images/exhibits/q494.png)  
A. The EC2 instance has a resource-based policy with a Deny statement.  
B. The principal has not been specified in the policy statement.  
C. The "Action" field does not grant the actions that are required to terminate the EC2 instance.  
D. The request to terminate the EC2 instance does not originate from the CIDR blocks 192.0.2.0/24 or 203.0.113.0/24.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: The policy contains two statements: an Allow for ec2:TerminateInstances and an explicit Deny on the same action with a NotIpAddress condition on aws:SourceIp. It reads as "deny everyone whose source IP address is not in 192.0.2.0/24 or 203.0.113.0/24." The administrator is calling the API from a network that isn't on that list, so the Deny fires and a 403 is returned. This is a common pattern: allow an action, then deny it unless the source matches a condition — used to restrict operations to a corporate network or VPN.  
Why A is not selected: The EC2 instance has no resource-based policy — those exist on buckets, queues, topics, and KMS keys. The denial comes from the condition in this same IAM policy.  
Why B is not selected: An identity-based policy never specifies a Principal element — the principal is whoever the policy is attached to. Its absence is not an error.  
Why C is not selected: The action is specified correctly: ec2:TerminateInstances is exactly what's needed to terminate the instance, and it's granted by the first statement.

---

495\. A company is conducting an internal audit. The company wants to ensure that the data in an Amazon S3 bucket that is associated with the company’s AWS Lake Formation data lake does not contain sensitive customer or employee data. The company wants to discover personally identifiable information (PII) or financial information, including passport numbers and credit card numbers.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Configure AWS Audit Manager on the account. Select the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standards (PCI DSS) for auditing.  
B. Configure Amazon S3 Inventory on the S3 bucket Configure Amazon Athena to query the inventory.  
C. Configure Amazon Macie to run a data discovery job that uses managed identifiers for the required data types.  
D. Use Amazon S3 Select to run a report across the S3 bucket.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The task is to find personal and financial data inside S3 objects: passport numbers, card numbers. That's exactly what Amazon Macie with managed data identifiers is for: it runs a discovery job, scans the objects (including sampling, so you don't pay to scan everything), and returns findings with the data type and location. There's no need to write custom rules or regular expressions.  
Why A is not selected: Audit Manager collects evidence of compliance against frameworks, but it doesn't analyze object contents.  
Why B is not selected: S3 Inventory lists objects and their metadata. It doesn't know what's inside the files.  
Why D is not selected: S3 Select runs a query against the content of a single object with a known structure. It's not a tool for searching a bucket for sensitive data.

---

496\. A company uses on-premises servers to host its applications. The company is running out of storage capacity. The applications use both block storage and NFS storage. The company needs a high-performing solution that supports local caching without re-architecting its existing applications.  
Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)  
A. Mount Amazon S3 as a file system to the on-premises servers.  
B. Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway to replace NFS storage.  
C. Deploy AWS Snowball Edge to provision NFS mounts to on-premises servers.  
D. Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway to replace the block storage.  
E. Deploy Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volumes and mount them to on-premises servers.  
Answer: BD  
Explanation: The applications use two different kinds of storage, and they can't be rewritten. So the replacement has to match by protocol: a file gateway replaces the NFS storage, serving data from S3 with local caching (B), and a volume gateway replaces the block storage, serving volumes over iSCSI and also caching active data locally (D). Both gateways provide the local caching the requirement calls for.  
Why A is not selected: S3 can't be mounted as a file system with native tools, and third-party solutions provide neither caching nor file system semantics.  
Why C is not selected: Snowball Edge is meant for data transfer and temporary on-site compute, not for permanently expanding storage.  
Why E is not selected: The EFS file system can only be mounted from an on-premises network over private connectivity and has no local cache: latency is dictated by the link, and it doesn't replace block storage at all.

---

497\. A company has a service that reads and writes large amounts of data from an Amazon S3 bucket in the same AWS Region. The service is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances within the private subnet of a VPC. The service communicates with Amazon S3 over a NAT gateway in the public subnet. However, the company wants a solution that will reduce the data output costs.  
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Provision a dedicated EC2 NAT instance in the public subnet. Configure the route table for the private subnet to use the elastic network interface of this instance as the destination for all S3 traffic.  
B. Provision a dedicated EC2 NAT instance in the private subnet. Configure the route table for the public subnet to use the elastic network interface of this instance as the destination for all S3 traffic.  
C. Provision a VPC gateway endpoint. Configure the route table for the private subnet to use the gateway endpoint as the route for all S3 traffic.  
D. Provision a second NAT gateway. Configure the route table for the private subnet to use this NAT gateway as the destination for all S3 traffic.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The cost here isn't for storage — it's that every gigabyte to and from S3 passes through the NAT gateway: both the gateway's hourly charge and the volume of data processed are billed. A gateway VPC endpoint removes NAT from this path entirely — a route to the S3 prefix is added to the private subnet's route table, traffic travels over the AWS network, and there's no charge for the endpoint or for the data that passes through it. This is the only option that actually reduces cost rather than shifting it around. Related questions: {{q:42,91,612}}.  
Why A is not selected: A NAT instance replaces a managed service with your own machine: you pay for the instance and its traffic, you're responsible for its fault tolerance, and you're limited by a single node's throughput.  
Why B is not selected: This setup isn't possible: NAT must sit in the public subnet, while the route table that needs changing belongs to the private subnet. The option describes a configuration that won't work.  
Why D is not selected: A second NAT gateway doubles the hourly charge and does nothing to reduce the volume of gigabytes processed.

---

498\. A company uses Amazon S3 to store high-resolution pictures in an S3 bucket. To minimize application changes, the company stores the pictures as the latest version of an S3 object. The company needs to retain only the two most recent versions of the pictures.  
The company wants to reduce costs. The company has identified the S3 bucket as a large expense.  
Which solution will reduce the S3 costs with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Use S3 Lifecycle to delete expired object versions and retain the two most recent versions.  
B. Use an AWS Lambda function to check for older versions and delete all but the two most recent versions.  
C. Use S3 Batch Operations to delete noncurrent object versions and retain only the two most recent versions.  
D. Deactivate versioning on the S3 bucket and retain the two most recent versions.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The bucket has versioning enabled, and old (noncurrent) versions of the pictures are what's driving up cost. S3 Lifecycle rules have exactly the pair of settings needed for this: NoncurrentVersionExpiration deletes noncurrent versions, and NewerNoncurrentVersions specifies how many of the most recent ones to keep. Set it to 2, and cleanup happens automatically without a single line of code. The application keeps working with the current version of the object exactly as before.  
Why B is not selected: A Lambda function solves this with code you have to write, schedule, handle errors for, and paginate through version listings for. A Lifecycle rule does the same thing through configuration.  
Why C is not selected: S3 Batch Operations is a one-time job driven by an S3 Inventory report. You'd have to run it again and again, whereas Lifecycle runs continuously on its own.  
Why D is not selected: Deactivating versioning doesn't delete the old versions that have already accumulated — the bill stays the same. And the requirement to keep the two most recent versions becomes impossible to satisfy, since no new versions will ever be created.

---

499\. A company needs to minimize the cost of its 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection. The company's average connection utilization is less than 10%. A solutions architect must recommend a solution that will reduce the cost without compromising security.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Set up a new 1 Gbps Direct Connect connection. Share the connection with another AWS account.  
B. Set up a new 200 Mbps Direct Connect connection in the AWS Management Console.  
C. Contact an AWS Direct Connect Partner to order a 1 Gbps connection. Share the connection with another AWS account.  
D. Contact an AWS Direct Connect Partner to order a 200 Mbps hosted connection for an existing AWS account.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: The connection is used at under a tenth of its capacity, so a lower port speed is what's needed. Dedicated connections can only be ordered at 1, 10, or 100 Gbps, while lower speeds — from 50 Mbps to 500 Mbps — exist only as hosted connections, which an AWS Direct Connect Partner provisions. Ordering a 200 Mbps hosted connection into the existing account lowers the port charge without changing the privacy of the path or its security.  
Why A is not selected: A second connection at the same 1 Gbps doubles the port charge; sharing it with another account doesn't reduce the company's costs.  
Why B is not selected: The console doesn't let you order a dedicated connection at 200 Mbps — only 1 Gbps and above are available there.  
Why C is not selected: A gigabit connection through a partner costs about the same as now. The savings come from lowering the port speed, not from changing how the connection is ordered.

---

500\. A company has multiple Windows file servers on premises. The company wants to migrate and consolidate its files into an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. File permissions must be preserved to ensure that access rights do not change.  
Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)  
A. Deploy AWS DataSync agents on premises. Schedule DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.  
B. Copy the shares on each file server into Amazon S3 buckets by using the AWS CLI. Schedule AWS DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.  
C. Remove the drives from each file server. Ship the drives to AWS for import into Amazon S3. Schedule AWS DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.  
D. Order an AWS Snowcone device. Connect the device to the on-premises network. Launch AWS DataSync agents on the device. Schedule DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.  
E. Order an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device. Connect the device to the on-premises network. Copy data to the device by using the AWS CLI. Ship the device back to AWS for import into Amazon S3. Schedule AWS DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.  
Answer: AD  
Explanation: Windows file permissions have to be preserved, so the migration tool needs to understand ACLs — that's AWS DataSync: it carries access control lists and ownership along with the files and can write directly into the FSx for Windows File Server file system. The agent can be deployed as a virtual machine in the data center (A), or, if the network link is weak, run directly on an AWS Snowcone device connected to the local network (D). Both paths deliver the same result.  
Why B is not selected: Copying to S3 first using the CLI loses the Windows access control lists: the files become objects, and the ACLs never make it to FSx.  
Why C is not selected: Importing the drives into S3 turns the data into objects and loses the permissions the same way, and physically shipping drives gives no control over data integrity.  
Why E is not selected: Copying to a Snowball device with the CLI into S3 again turns the files into objects and loses the ACLs. Snowball is only useful here as a platform to run the agent on, not as an S3 waypoint.

---

501\. A company wants to ingest customer payment data into the company's data lake in Amazon S3. The company receives payment data every minute on average. The company wants to analyze the payment data in real time.  
Then the company wants to ingest the data into the data lake.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?  
A. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest data. Use AWS Lambda to analyze the data in real time.  
B. Use AWS Glue to ingest data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to analyze the data in real time.  
C. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to ingest data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to analyze the data in real time.  
D. Use Amazon API Gateway to ingest data. Use AWS Lambda to analyze the data in real time.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: Data arrives on average once a minute and needs to be analyzed on the fly, then stored in the data lake. Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully managed delivery service: it buffers, transforms, and writes to S3 on its own, and it scales without you managing shards. Real-time analysis on top of that stream is handled by Kinesis Data Analytics with an ordinary SQL query. There is nothing left to operate — that is exactly what maximum operational efficiency looks like.  
Why A is not selected: Data Streams requires shard management, and analysis in Lambda functions requires custom code.  
Why B is not selected: AWS Glue is a batch ETL service; it is not designed to ingest a continuous stream.  
Why D is not selected: API Gateway with functions means hand-built ingestion and hand-built analysis instead of two purpose-built managed services.

---

502\. A company runs a website that uses a content management system (CMS) on Amazon EC2. The CMS runs on a single EC2 instance and uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance for the data tier. Website images are stored on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume that is mounted inside the EC2 instance.  
Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to improve the performance and resilience of the website? (Choose two.)  
A. Move the website images into an Amazon S3 bucket that is mounted on every EC2 instance  
B. Share the website images by using an NFS share from the primary EC2 instance. Mount this share on the other EC2 instances.  
C. Move the website images onto an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system that is mounted on every EC2 instance.  
D. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the existing EC2 instance. Use the AMI to provision new instances behind an Application Load Balancer as part of an Auto Scaling group. Configure the Auto Scaling group to maintain a minimum of two instances. Configure an accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator for the website  
E. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the existing EC2 instance. Use the AMI to provision new instances behind an Application Load Balancer as part of an Auto Scaling group. Configure the Auto Scaling group to maintain a minimum of two instances. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the website.  
Answer: CE  
Explanation: There are two weak points: a single instance, and images on a local volume. Moving the images to Amazon EFS and mounting it on every instance means any instance sees the full set of files (C). The site itself becomes an Auto Scaling group of at least two instances behind an Application Load Balancer, built from an AMI, with CloudFront placed in front to cache the images at edge locations and noticeably speed up delivery (E).  
Why A is not selected: There is no standard way to mount an S3 bucket as a file system on instances; the application would have to be rewritten to work through the API.  
Why B is not selected: Serving files over NFS from the "primary" instance turns it into a single point of failure — resilience gets worse, not better.  
Why D is not selected: Fault tolerance improves, but Global Accelerator optimizes the traffic path and does not cache static content. For a site serving images, the real gain comes from CloudFront's cache.

---

503\. A company runs an infrastructure monitoring service. The company is building a new feature that will enable the service to monitor data in customer AWS accounts. The new feature will call AWS APIs in customer accounts to describe Amazon EC2 instances and read Amazon CloudWatch metrics.  
What should the company do to obtain access to customer accounts in the MOST secure way?  
A. Ensure that the customers create an IAM role in their account with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions and a trust policy to the company’s account.  
B. Create a serverless API that implements a token vending machine to provide temporary AWS credentials for a role with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions.  
C. Ensure that the customers create an IAM user in their account with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions. Encrypt and store customer access and secret keys in a secrets management system.  
D. Ensure that the customers create an Amazon Cognito user in their account to use an IAM role with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions. Encrypt and store the Amazon Cognito user and password in a secrets management system.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: This is the classic pattern for a third-party service accessing customer accounts: the customer creates a role with minimal permissions themselves (here, read-only EC2 and CloudWatch access) and specifies the provider's account in the trust policy. The service calls AssumeRole and operates on temporary credentials. You never store anyone else's keys, and the customer can revoke access at any time simply by deleting the role. One essential addition from real-world practice: use an external ID in the trust policy to protect against the confused deputy attack.  
Why B is not selected: Issuing your own temporary credentials does not solve the underlying problem: to issue them you still need permissions in the customer's account, which again means a role with a trust relationship.  
Why C is not selected: Storing IAM user keys for thousands of customers in your own store is the worst option: long-lived secrets, responsibility for keeping them safe, and manual revocation.  
Why D is not selected: Cognito is meant for application end users, not cross-account access to AWS APIs. A password in a secrets store is again a long-lived secret.

---

504\. A company needs to connect several VPCs in the us-east-1 Region that span hundreds of AWS accounts. The company's networking team has its own AWS account to manage the cloud network.  
What is the MOST operationally efficient solution to connect the VPCs?  
A. Set up VPC peering connections between each VPC. Update each associated subnet’s route table  
B. Configure a NAT gateway and an internet gateway in each VPC to connect each VPC through the internet  
C. Create an AWS Transit Gateway in the networking team’s AWS account. Configure static routes from each VPC.  
D. Deploy VPN gateways in each VPC. Create a transit VPC in the networking team’s AWS account to connect to each VPC.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: Hundreds of accounts and many VPCs in a single Region are exactly the case Transit Gateway was built for. It is deployed in the networking team's account, shared with other accounts through AWS RAM, and each VPC connects with a single attachment. Routing management stays centralized with the networking team — operationally this is the most efficient option.  
Why A is not selected: A full mesh of peering connections across hundreds of VPCs means thousands of connections and edits to every route table. That is practically unmanageable.  
Why B is not selected: Connecting internal networks over the internet means losing privacy, paying for outbound data transfer, and getting worse latency.  
Why D is not selected: A transit VPC built on your own VPN gateways is the legacy pattern that Transit Gateway replaced: it requires its own appliances, is limited by tunnel throughput, and has to be maintained manually.

---

505\. A company has Amazon EC2 instances that run nightly batch jobs to process data. The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group that uses On-Demand billing. If a job fails on one instance, another instance will reprocess the job. The batch jobs run between 12:00 AM and 06:00 AM local time every day.  
Which solution will provide EC2 instances to meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Purchase a 1-year Savings Plan for Amazon EC2 that covers the instance family of the Auto Scaling group that the batch job uses.  
B. Purchase a 1-year Reserved Instance for the specific instance type and operating system of the instances in the Auto Scaling group that the batch job uses.  
C. Create a new launch template for the Auto Scaling group. Set the instances to Spot Instances. Set a policy to scale out based on CPU usage.  
D. Create a new launch template for the Auto Scaling group. Increase the instance size. Set a policy to scale out based on CPU usage.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The jobs run six hours a day and tolerate interruption: if an instance is lost, another instance reprocesses the job. That profile is the textbook use case for Spot Instances — up to 90 percent savings, and the application's own retry logic already absorbs capacity reclamation.  
Why A is not selected: A Savings Plan pays off under round-the-clock load; running only six hours a day would leave the commitment underused.  
Why B is not selected: A Reserved Instance is billed continuously, but the instance only runs a quarter of the day.  
Why D is not selected: Larger On-Demand instances would only raise the bill further: the billing model itself has not changed.

---

506\. A social media company is building a feature for its website. The feature will give users the ability to upload photos. The company expects significant increases in demand during large events and must ensure that the website can handle the upload traffic from users.  
Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST scalability?  
A. Upload files from the user's browser to the application servers. Transfer the files to an Amazon S3 bucket.  
B. Provision an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway. Upload files directly from the user's browser to the file gateway.  
C. Generate Amazon S3 presigned URLs in the application. Upload files directly from the user's browser into an S3 bucket.  
D. Provision an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Upload files directly from the user's browser to the file system.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The bottleneck is files passing through the application servers. A presigned URL removes it entirely: the application only issues a signed link, and the browser uploads the file straight into S3. The servers take no part in the data transfer, so a traffic spike during major events is bounded only by S3's own scalability, which is effectively unlimited.  
Why A is not selected: Files pass through the application servers, and those servers are exactly what becomes the bottleneck during a spike, requiring you to scale out the fleet and its bandwidth.  
Why B is not selected: A file gateway is a hybrid gateway for an on-premises location; it has nothing to do with uploads from users' browsers.  
Why D is not selected: An EFS file system is mounted on instances inside a VPC; you cannot upload to it directly from a browser.

---

507\. A company has a web application for travel ticketing. The application is based on a database that runs in a single data center in North America. The company wants to expand the application to serve a global user base. The company needs to deploy the application to multiple AWS Regions. Average latency must be less than 1 second on updates to the reservation database.  
The company wants to have separate deployments of its web platform across multiple Regions. However, the company must maintain a single primary reservation database that is globally consistent.  
Which solution should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?  
A. Convert the application to use Amazon DynamoDB. Use a global table for the center reservation table. Use the correct Regional endpoint in each Regional deployment.  
B. Migrate the database to an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. Deploy Aurora Read Replicas in each Region. Use the correct Regional endpoint in each Regional deployment for access to the database.  
C. Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. Deploy MySQL read replicas in each Region. Use the correct Regional endpoint in each Regional deployment for access to the database.  
D. Migrate the application to an Amazon Aurora Serverless database. Deploy instances of the database to each Region. Use the correct Regional endpoint in each Regional deployment to access the database. Use AWS Lambda functions to process event streams in each Region to synchronize the databases.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The requirement calls for a single, globally consistent reservation store with update latency under one second, deployed across multiple Regions. DynamoDB global tables let you write in any Region with replication to the others typically completing in under a second, and each deployment talks to its own Regional endpoint.  
Why B is not selected: Aurora Read Replicas only accept reads: reservation writes would still go to the single writer Region, and latency for remote users would exceed one second.  
Why C is not selected: RDS read replicas have the same write problem, and their replication lag is noticeably higher than Aurora's.  
Why D is not selected: Separate independent databases with hand-built synchronization through Lambda functions guarantee conflicts and no single consistent state.

---

508\. A company has migrated multiple Microsoft Windows Server workloads to Amazon EC2 instances that run in the us-west-1 Region. The company manually backs up the workloads to create an image as needed.  
In the event of a natural disaster in the us-west-1 Region, the company wants to recover workloads quickly in the us-west-2 Region. The company wants no more than 24 hours of data loss on the EC2 instances. The company also wants to automate any backups of the EC2 instances.  
Which solutions will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative effort? (Choose two.)  
A. Create an Amazon EC2-backed Amazon Machine Image (AMI) lifecycle policy to create a backup based on tags. Schedule the backup to run twice daily. Copy the image on demand.  
B. Create an Amazon EC2-backed Amazon Machine Image (AMI) lifecycle policy to create a backup based on tags. Schedule the backup to run twice daily. Configure the copy to the us-west-2 Region.  
C. Create backup vaults in us-west-1 and in us-west-2 by using AWS Backup. Create a backup plan for the EC2 instances based on tag values. Create an AWS Lambda function to run as a scheduled job to copy the backup data to us-west-2.  
D. Create a backup vault by using AWS Backup. Use AWS Backup to create a backup plan for the EC2 instances based on tag values. Define the destination for the copy as us-west-2. Specify the backup schedule to run twice daily.  
E. Create a backup vault by using AWS Backup. Use AWS Backup to create a backup plan for the EC2 instances based on tag values. Specify the backup schedule to run twice daily. Copy on demand to us-west-2.  
Answer: BD  
Explanation: The requirement is automated backups plus a ready-made copy in another Region with no more than 24 hours of data loss. Both working options schedule backups twice a day and copy them automatically to us-west-2: an EC2-backed AMI lifecycle policy driven by tags with copy to the other Region configured (B), and an AWS Backup plan driven by tags with the copy destination specified (D). In both cases, once set up, no further intervention is needed.  
Why A is not selected: Copying the image manually on demand is exactly the manual effort the requirement says to avoid, and it gives no guarantee of staying within a day's worth of data.  
Why C is not selected: A custom function to move copies around is unnecessary code where AWS Backup already provides built-in cross-Region copy.  
Why E is not selected: The schedule is automatic, but the copy to the other Region is still done manually.

---

509\. A company operates a two-tier application for image processing. The application uses two Availability Zones, each with one public subnet and one private subnet. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) for the web tier uses the public subnets. Amazon EC2 instances for the application tier use the private subnets.  
Users report that the application is running more slowly than expected. A security audit of the web server log files shows that the application is receiving millions of illegitimate requests from a small number of IP addresses. A solutions architect needs to resolve the immediate performance problem while the company investigates a more permanent solution.  
What should the solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?  
A. Modify the inbound security group for the web tier. Add a deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.  
B. Modify the network ACL for the web tier subnets. Add an inbound deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.  
C. Modify the inbound security group for the application tier. Add a deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.  
D. Modify the network ACL for the application tier subnets. Add an inbound deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The immediate need is to block specific IP addresses. Explicit deny rules only exist on network ACLs, and they need to be applied to the web-tier subnets, where the load balancer sits and where the attacker's traffic arrives.  
Why A is not selected: Security groups have no deny rules: they only allow traffic.  
Why C is not selected: Same security group limitation, plus the application tier is the wrong tier to target.  
Why D is not selected: The network ACL is the right tool, but it's applied to the application-tier subnets — the malicious traffic never reaches them directly and will keep loading the web tier.

---

510\. A global marketing company has applications that run in the ap-southeast-2 Region and the eu-west-1 Region.  
Applications that run in a VPC in eu-west-1 need to communicate securely with databases that run in a VPC in ap- southeast-2.  
Which network design will meet these requirements?  
A. Create a VPC peering connection between the eu-west-1 VPC and the ap-southeast-2 VPC. Create an inbound rule in the eu-west-1 application security group that allows traffic from the database server IP addresses in the ap-southeast-2 security group.  
B. Configure a VPC peering connection between the ap-southeast-2 VPC and the eu-west-1 VPC. Update the subnet route tables. Create an inbound rule in the ap-southeast-2 database security group that references the security group ID of the application servers in eu-west-1.  
C. Configure a VPC peering connection between the ap-southeast-2 VPC and the eu-west-1 VPUpdate the subnet route tables. Create an inbound rule in the ap-southeast-2 database security group that allows traffic from the eu-west-1 application server IP addresses.  
D. Create a transit gateway with a peering attachment between the eu-west-1 VPC and the ap-southeast-2 VPC. After the transit gateways are properly peered and routing is configured, create an inbound rule in the database security group that references the security group ID of the application servers in eu-west-1.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The application in eu-west-1 needs to reach databases in ap-southeast-2 — this calls for inter-Region VPC peering, updated route tables in both networks, and an inbound rule on the database's security group. One important detail: you cannot reference a security group from another Region — inter-Region peering doesn't support that. So the rule has to specify the application servers' IP addresses or range instead.  
Why A is not selected: The rule is added in the wrong place: the inbound allow rule needs to sit on the database side, not the application side. The direction described is also reversed.  
Why B is not selected: Referencing a security group ID over inter-Region peering isn't supported — the rule simply won't be created.  
Why D is not selected: Transit Gateway peering has the same limitation: security group references don't work across Regions, and the gateway itself is overkill for connecting just two networks.

---

511\. A company is developing software that uses a PostgreSQL database schema. The company needs to configure multiple development environments and databases for the company's developers. On average, each development environment is used for half of the 8-hour workday.  
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Configure each development environment with its own Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database  
B. Configure each development environment with its own Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Single-AZ DB instances  
C. Configure each development environment with its own Amazon Aurora On-Demand PostgreSQL-Compatible database  
D. Configure each development environment with its own Amazon S3 bucket by using Amazon S3 Object Select  
Answer: C  
Review status: Disputed key (alternative: B); Low-confidence audit  
Dispute note: Read literally, option C (a regular provisioned Aurora cluster) would actually be more expensive than an RDS Single-AZ instance stopped overnight, since the environment is used only 4 hours out of an 8-hour day  
Source note: Dump defect: option C is printed as "Aurora On-Demand PostgreSQL-Compatible," which duplicates option A as written; based on the intent of the question it should read Aurora Serverless — only that option scales down during idle periods  
Explanation: The environment is used for only four hours out of an eight-hour workday, so whatever avoids paying for idle time wins. The key reads option C as pay-per-use pricing (an Aurora database billed by consumption), and under that reading it is cheaper than any instance that runs around the clock. The wording of the option itself is disputable: "Aurora On-Demand" literally describes ordinary hourly provisioning, in which case B — a small RDS Single-AZ instance that is stopped overnight — turns out cheaper. The question is worded carelessly; remember the underlying principle: irregular, partial utilization means paying for consumption rather than keeping an instance running.  
Why A is not selected: The same Aurora option, but without the pay-per-use qualifier: a provisioned cluster is billed for the entire time it exists, including the four idle hours every day.  
Why B is not selected: A strong alternative: RDS Single-AZ is the cheapest managed PostgreSQL option, and stopping it saves on compute. Its weakness is that RDS automatically restarts a stopped instance after 7 days, requiring a process that stops it again.  
Why D is not selected: S3 with S3 Select is not a PostgreSQL database at all: there is no schema, no transactions, no indexes, and no PostgreSQL protocol connectivity. The requirement is not met in principle.

---

512\. A company uses AWS Organizations with resources tagged by account. The company also uses AWS Backup to back up its AWS infrastructure resources. The company needs to back up all AWS resources.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Use AWS Config to identify all untagged resources. Tag the identified resources programmatically. Use tags in the backup plan.  
B. Use AWS Config to identify all resources that are not running. Add those resources to the backup vault.  
C. Require all AWS account owners to review their resources to identify the resources that need to be backed up.  
D. Use Amazon Inspector to identify all noncompliant resources.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: AWS Backup selects resources by tag, so an untagged resource simply never enters the backup plan. The task boils down to finding such resources and tagging them: AWS Config sees the inventory of all resources across every account in the organization and can identify the ones missing the required tag (the required-tags rule), and remediation can then be automated. From that point on, the backup plan keeps working off tags, and newly created resources are picked up automatically.  
Why B is not selected: "Not running" is the wrong criterion — everything needs to be backed up regardless of state. And manually adding resources to a backup vault does not scale.  
Why C is not selected: A manual audit by account owners is the maximum possible operational overhead and guarantees gaps.  
Why D is not selected: Amazon Inspector looks for workload vulnerabilities and knows nothing about tags or backup plans.

---

513\. A social media company wants to allow its users to upload images in an application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud. The company needs a solution that automatically resizes the images so that the images can be displayed on multiple device types. The application experiences unpredictable traffic patterns throughout the day. The company is seeking a highly available solution that maximizes scalability.  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?  
A. Create a static website hosted in Amazon S3 that invokes AWS Lambda functions to resize the images and store the images in an Amazon S3 bucket.  
B. Create a static website hosted in Amazon CloudFront that invokes AWS Step Functions to resize the images and store the images in an Amazon RDS database.  
C. Create a dynamic website hosted on a web server that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. Configure a process that runs on the EC2 instance to resize the images and store the images in an Amazon S3 bucket.  
D. Create a dynamic website hosted on an automatically scaling Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that creates a resize job in Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS). Set up an image-resizing program that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance to process the resize jobs.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Traffic is unpredictable, so the solution needs services that scale themselves and cost nothing while idle. A static website sits in S3; an image upload triggers a Lambda function that creates the required sizes and writes the results back to the bucket. There are no servers to plan capacity for, and availability is handled by the services themselves.  
Why B is not selected: CloudFront is a content delivery network, not a hosting platform that "invokes" Step Functions, and storing images in a relational database is inappropriate.  
Why C is not selected: A single EC2 instance is a single point of failure that cannot scale to handle traffic spikes.  
Why D is not selected: An ECS cluster plus a handler running on a separate EC2 instance is infrastructure that still needs to be maintained, and the instance again becomes the bottleneck.

---

514\. A company is running a microservices application on Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants to migrate the application to an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster for scalability. The company must configure the Amazon EKS control plane with endpoint private access set to true and endpoint public access set to false to maintain security compliance. The company must also put the data plane in private subnets. However, the company has received error notifications because the node cannot join the cluster.  
Which solution will allow the node to join the cluster?  
A. Grant the required permission in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) to the AmazonEKSNodeRole IAM role.  
B. Create interface VPC endpoints to allow nodes to access the control plane.  
C. Recreate nodes in the public subnet. Restrict security groups for EC2 nodes.  
D. Allow outbound traffic in the security group of the nodes.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: When the EKS control plane's public endpoint is disabled, nodes reach it over its private address inside the VPC — that part works. But the nodes also need access to other services that expose public APIs: ECR (images), S3 (image layers), CloudWatch Logs, STS, EC2. In private subnets with no NAT, the only way to reach those is through a set of interface VPC endpoints (plus a gateway endpoint for S3). Without them, a node cannot pull images or register with the cluster — which is exactly why it fails to join.  
Why A is not selected: The node role's permissions do matter, but their absence would produce a different error, and the scenario specifically describes network isolation in a private cluster. In addition, the AmazonEKSNodeRole role typically already carries the required policies.  
Why C is not selected: Moving the nodes into a public subnet violates the requirement to keep the data plane in private subnets.  
Why D is not selected: Outbound traffic is allowed by security groups by default, and without an endpoint or a NAT gateway it still has nowhere to go.

---

515\. A company is migrating an on-premises application to AWS. The company wants to use Amazon Redshift as a solution.  
Which use cases are suitable for Amazon Redshift in this scenario? (Choose three.)  
A. Supporting data APIs to access data with traditional, containerized, and event-driven applications  
B. Supporting client-side and server-side encryption  
C. Building analytics workloads during specified hours and when the application is not active  
D. Caching data to reduce the pressure on the backend database  
E. Scaling globally to support petabytes of data and tens of millions of requests per minute  
F. Creating a secondary replica of the cluster by using the AWS Management Console  
Answer: ABC  
Review status: Corrected key (source: BCE; reviewed: ABC)  
Correction note: Option E ("global scaling to petabytes and tens of millions of requests per minute") describes Amazon DynamoDB, not Redshift: a Redshift cluster is regional and isn't built for that request rate. The wording of option A is taken from the description of the Redshift Data API, which exists precisely to let regular, containerized, and event-driven applications access the data — so the correct trio is A, B, C  
Explanation: The dump key has been corrected here: the correct set of three is A, B, C. Amazon Redshift does provide a Data API that traditional, containerized, and event-driven applications can use to access data (A); it supports both client-side and server-side encryption (B); and it is well suited to analytics workloads that run during set hours when the primary application is idle, since the cluster can be paused during that time (C).  
Why D is not selected: Caching to reduce load on a backend database is a job for ElastiCache or DAX; Redshift is an analytics data warehouse, not a cache.  
Why E is not selected: The description of global scaling to petabytes of data and tens of millions of requests per minute describes DynamoDB: a Redshift cluster is regional and is not built for that request rate. This is exactly why the dump key was corrected.  
Why F is not selected: Redshift has no concept of a secondary cluster replica: fault tolerance is built on snapshots and cross-region snapshot copies, not on a console-created replica.

---

516\. A company provides an API interface to customers so the customers can retrieve their financial information. The company expects a larger number of requests during peak usage times of the year.  
The company requires the API to respond consistently with low latency to ensure customer satisfaction. The company needs to provide a compute host for the API.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Use an Application Load Balancer and Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS).  
B. Use Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda functions with provisioned concurrency.  
C. Use an Application Load Balancer and an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster.  
D. Use Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda functions with reserved concurrency.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The requirements are consistently low latency at peak load and minimal operational overhead. API Gateway paired with Lambda functions removes server management entirely, and provisioned concurrency keeps a set number of pre-initialized execution environments ready, so there are no cold starts and response time stays flat even under a sudden surge in requests.  
Why A is not selected: An ECS cluster behind a load balancer requires configuring scaling and maintaining the services.  
Why C is not selected: EKS adds Kubernetes cluster management on top — the most operationally heavy option.  
Why D is not selected: Reserved concurrency only reserves and caps a portion of concurrency for a function; it does not pre-warm execution environments, so cold starts remain.

---

517\. A company wants to send all AWS Systems Manager Session Manager logs to an Amazon S3 bucket for archival purposes.  
Which solution will meet this requirement with the MOST operational efficiency?  
A. Enable S3 logging in the Systems Manager console. Choose an S3 bucket to send the session data to.  
B. Install the Amazon CloudWatch agent. Push all logs to a CloudWatch log group. Export the logs to an S3 bucket from the group for archival purposes.  
C. Create a Systems Manager document to upload all server logs to a central S3 bucket. Use Amazon EventBridge to run the Systems Manager document against all servers that are in the account daily.  
D. Install an Amazon CloudWatch agent. Push all logs to a CloudWatch log group. Create a CloudWatch logs subscription that pushes any incoming log events to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Set Amazon S3 as the destination.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Session Manager has built-in session log recording to S3: just point it at a bucket in the settings, and the data flows there on its own. No agent, no intermediate services, and no custom code are required.  
Why B is not selected: An agent plus exporting from a log group is an unnecessary middleman and a manual export where a direct setting already exists.  
Why C is not selected: A Systems Manager document run daily collects server logs, not session logs, and adds custom code and a schedule of its own.  
Why D is not selected: The combination of an agent, a log subscription, and a delivery stream solves the same problem with three unnecessary extra components.

---

518\. An application uses an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance. The RDS database is becoming low on disk space. A solutions architect wants to increase the disk space without downtime.  
Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST amount of effort?  
A. Enable storage autoscaling in RDS  
B. Increase the RDS database instance size  
C. Change the RDS database instance storage type to Provisioned IOPS  
D. Back up the RDS database, increase the storage capacity, restore the database, and stop the previous instance  
Answer: A  
Explanation: RDS storage autoscaling grows the volume automatically as soon as free space runs low, and it does so with no downtime. You only need to turn the setting on once and set an upper limit.  
Why B is not selected: Instance size determines CPU and memory, not disk capacity.  
Why C is not selected: Provisioned IOPS changes I/O performance, not available storage space.  
Why D is not selected: Taking a backup, increasing storage, and restoring means both downtime and the maximum amount of manual work, whereas an RDS volume can be resized on the fly.

---

519\. A consulting company provides professional services to customers worldwide. The company provides solutions and tools for customers to expedite gathering and analyzing data on AWS. The company needs to centrally manage and deploy a common set of solutions and tools for customers to use for self-service purposes.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Create AWS CloudFormation templates for the customers.  
B. Create AWS Service Catalog products for the customers.  
C. Create AWS Systems Manager templates for the customers.  
D. Create AWS Config items for the customers.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: What's needed is a catalog of ready-made solutions that customers deploy themselves while the company manages them centrally. That is exactly what AWS Service Catalog provides: versioned products with launch constraints and access controls, available to users for self-service.  
Why A is not selected: CloudFormation templates are the raw material that catalog products are built from, but on their own they provide neither a self-service storefront nor centralized version and access management.  
Why C is not selected: Systems Manager documents automate operations on managed resources; they do not publish solutions for customers to deploy.  
Why D is not selected: Config items are entries in a resource's configuration history; they have nothing to do with distributing solutions.

---

520\. A company is designing a new web application that will run on Amazon EC2 Instances. The application will use Amazon DynamoDB for backend data storage. The application traffic will be unpredictable. The company expects that the application read and write throughput to the database will be moderate to high. The company needs to scale in response to application traffic.  
Which DynamoDB table configuration will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Configure DynamoDB with provisioned read and write by using the DynamoDB Standard table class. Set DynamoDB auto scaling to a maximum defined capacity.  
B. Configure DynamoDB in on-demand mode by using the DynamoDB Standard table class.  
C. Configure DynamoDB with provisioned read and write by using the DynamoDB Standard Infrequent Access (DynamoDB Standard-IA) table class. Set DynamoDB auto scaling to a maximum defined capacity.  
D. Configure DynamoDB in on-demand mode by using the DynamoDB Standard Infrequent Access (DynamoDB Standard-IA) table class.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The key detail is unpredictable traffic. In on-demand mode, DynamoDB instantly adapts to any spike, and you pay only for the requests actually made: with a load profile that can't be predicted in advance, this ends up cheaper than keeping provisioned capacity with headroom to spare.  
Why A is not selected: Provisioned capacity with auto scaling pays off under predictable load; with sudden spikes it either can't scale up fast enough or ends up paying for unused capacity.  
Why C is not selected: The same problem is compounded by the Standard-IA table class, whose requests cost more — and the read/write load here is moderate to high.  
Why D is not selected: The Standard-IA table class lowers storage cost at the expense of more expensive requests and is meant for infrequently accessed data, not an active web application.

---

521\. A retail company has several businesses. The IT team for each business manages its own AWS account. Each team account is part of an organization in AWS Organizations. Each team monitors its product inventory levels in an Amazon DynamoDB table in the team's own AWS account.  
The company is deploying a central inventory reporting application into a shared AWS account. The application must be able to read items from all the teams' DynamoDB tables.  
Which authentication option will meet these requirements MOST securely?  
A. Integrate DynamoDB with AWS Secrets Manager in the inventory application account. Configure the application to use the correct secret from Secrets Manager to authenticate and read the DynamoDB table. Schedule secret rotation for every 30 days.  
B. In every business account, create an IAM user that has programmatic access. Configure the application to use the correct IAM user access key ID and secret access key to authenticate and read the DynamoDB table. Manually rotate IAM access keys every 30 days.  
C. In every business account, create an IAM role named BU_ROLE with a policy that gives the role access to the DynamoDB table and a trust policy to trust a specific role in the inventory application account. In the inventory account, create a role named APP_ROLE that allows access to the STS AssumeRole API operation. Configure the application to use APP_ROLE and assume the crossaccount role BU_ROLE to read the DynamoDB table.  
D. Integrate DynamoDB with AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Generate identity certificates to authenticate DynamoDB. Configure the application to use the correct certificate to authenticate and read the DynamoDB table.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: Cross-account access within an organization is built on roles and STS, not on handing out long-lived keys. In each business unit's account, a role is created with a policy granting read access to that account's DynamoDB table and a trust policy allowing a specific role in the reporting account to assume it. The application runs under its own role and calls AssumeRole for the target account, obtaining temporary credentials for the duration of the session. There are no keys to rotate, and revoking access is a single edit to the trust policy.  
Why A is not selected: Access to DynamoDB is authorized through IAM, not through a password or connection string. There is simply nothing to store in Secrets Manager.  
Why B is not selected: Programmatic IAM users in every account mean long-lived keys that have to be stored somewhere, distributed, and manually rotated every month. That is exactly what the "MOST securely" requirement is asking you to avoid.  
Why D is not selected: DynamoDB does not authenticate clients using ACM certificates. No such mechanism exists.

---

522\. A company runs container applications by using Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The company's workload is not consistent throughout the day. The company wants Amazon EKS to scale in and out according to the workload.  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)  
A. Use an AWS Lambda function to resize the EKS cluster.  
B. Use the Kubernetes Metrics Server to activate horizontal pod autoscaling.  
C. Use the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler to manage the number of nodes in the cluster.  
D. Use Amazon API Gateway and connect it to Amazon EKS.  
E. Use AWS App Mesh to observe network activity.  
Answer: BC  
Explanation: Scaling needs to happen at two levels. Inside the cluster, horizontal pod autoscaling controls the number of pods, and it needs metrics from the Kubernetes Metrics Server (B). When pods run out of room, the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler grows the number of nodes (C). Both are standard components and require no custom code.  
Why A is not selected: A custom function that resizes the cluster means code to write and maintain instead of using a built-in mechanism.  
Why D is not selected: API Gateway handles incoming requests and has nothing to do with cluster scaling.  
Why E is not selected: App Mesh provides observability and traffic management between services, but it does not manage capacity.

---

523\. A company runs a microservice-based serverless web application. The application must be able to retrieve data from multiple Amazon DynamoDB tables A solutions architect needs to give the application the ability to retrieve the data with no impact on the baseline performance of the application.  
Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?  
A. AWS AppSync pipeline resolvers  
B. Amazon CloudFront with [email protected] functions  
C. Edge-optimized Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions  
D. Amazon Athena Federated Query with a DynamoDB connector  
Answer: B  
Review status: Disputed key (alternative: A)  
Dispute note: Pipeline resolvers in AWS AppSync exist precisely to assemble data from multiple sources — including several DynamoDB tables — in a single request, and they require no custom code at the edge. The case for key B is that edge-location processing doesn't touch the existing application at all and therefore has no effect on its baseline performance  
Explanation: This is a disputed question. The dump key is option B: the fetching logic is pushed out to CloudFront edge locations, so the baseline application is never touched at all, and responses can be cached closer to the user. A strong alternative is option A: AppSync pipeline resolvers exist precisely to reach multiple data sources — including several DynamoDB tables — in sequence within a single request, and they require neither custom edge code nor managing its replication. By the operational-efficiency criterion, A looks like the more natural fit; by the "don't touch the existing application" criterion, it's B.  
Why A is not selected: Technically this is the most direct way to gather data from several tables in one request, which is why the question is flagged as disputed: the only objection is that it introduces a new API layer in front of the application.  
Why C is not selected: An edge-optimized API Gateway only brings the entry point closer to users; gathering data from multiple tables would still have to be done in the function's own code, so efficiency is no better.  
Why D is not selected: Athena Federated Query is built for analytical queries and runs with latency measured in seconds, which makes it unsuitable for serving data to the application in real time.

---

524\. A company wants to analyze and troubleshoot Access Denied errors and Unauthorized errors that are related to IAM permissions. The company has AWS CloudTrail turned on.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST effort?  
A. Use AWS Glue and write custom scripts to query CloudTrail logs for the errors.  
B. Use AWS Batch and write custom scripts to query CloudTrail logs for the errors.  
C. Search CloudTrail logs with Amazon Athena queries to identify the errors.  
D. Search CloudTrail logs with Amazon QuickSight. Create a dashboard to identify the errors.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: CloudTrail logs sit in S3 as compressed JSON files, and the simplest way to search them is Amazon Athena: the CloudTrail console has a built-in "Create Athena table" action, after which you can search for errors with ordinary SQL over the errorCode and errorMessage fields (AccessDenied, UnauthorizedOperation), filtered by user and time. No cluster and no code — you pay only for the data scanned, and partitioning by date limits how much gets scanned.  
Why A is not selected: AWS Glue with custom scripts means building an ETL pipeline where a SQL query against a ready-made table would do.  
Why B is not selected: AWS Batch runs containerized jobs. For parsing logs, that's unnecessary infrastructure and unnecessary code.  
Why D is not selected: QuickSight builds visualizations, but it still needs a table as its source (typically that same Athena table). For a one-off error search, a dashboard is overkill.

---

525\. A company wants to add its existing AWS usage cost to its operation cost dashboard. A solutions architect needs to recommend a solution that will give the company access to its usage cost programmatically. The company must be able to access cost data for the current year and forecast costs for the next 12 months.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Access usage cost-related data by using the AWS Cost Explorer API with pagination.  
B. Access usage cost-related data by using downloadable AWS Cost Explorer report .csv files.  
C. Configure AWS Budgets actions to send usage cost data to the company through FTP.  
D. Create AWS Budgets reports for usage cost data. Send the data to the company through SMTP.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The key phrase is "programmatically": the cost data is needed by an application that builds a dashboard. Cost Explorer has an API (GetCostAndUsage for actual spend and GetCostForecast for forecasts), with results returned in pages via NextPageToken. Cost Explorer can also generate a 12-month forecast on its own. There is nothing to deploy, hence the minimal operational overhead.  
Why B is not selected: Downloadable CSV files mean a manual process: someone has to export them and load them into the dashboard. That is not programmatic access.  
Why C is not selected: AWS Budgets actions apply policies and send notifications, but they don't export data and don't work over FTP.  
Why D is not selected: Budgets reports are sent as emails and contain budget status, not the full cost and forecast data needed for programmatic processing.

---

526\. A solutions architect is reviewing the resilience of an application. The solutions architect notices that a database administrator recently failed over the application's Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database writer instance as part of a scaling exercise. The failover resulted in 3 minutes of downtime for the application.  
Which solution will reduce the downtime for scaling exercises with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Create more Aurora PostgreSQL read replicas in the cluster to handle the load during failover.  
B. Set up a secondary Aurora PostgreSQL cluster in the same AWS Region. During failover, update the application to use the secondary cluster's writer endpoint.  
C. Create an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached cluster to handle the load during failover.  
D. Set up an Amazon RDS proxy for the database. Update the application to use the proxy endpoint.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: The three minutes of downtime happened because, after the failover, the application kept holding connections to the old writer instance and had to re-establish them manually. RDS Proxy maintains a connection pool and routes it to the current writer instance itself, so the failover becomes nearly invisible to the application. The change amounts to swapping in the proxy endpoint.  
Why A is not selected: Additional read replicas have no effect on how long the writer instance failover takes.  
Why B is not selected: A second cluster with manual application failover means extra cost, more operations to manage, and no speed improvement.  
Why C is not selected: Memcached caches reads and does nothing to speed up a writer instance failover.

---

527\. A company has a regional subscription-based streaming service that runs in a single AWS Region. The architecture consists of web servers and application servers on Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in Auto Scaling groups behind Elastic Load Balancers. The architecture includes an Amazon Aurora global database cluster that extends across multiple Availability Zones.  
The company wants to expand globally and to ensure that its application has minimal downtime.  
Which solution will provide the MOST fault tolerance?  
A. Extend the Auto Scaling groups for the web tier and the application tier to deploy instances in Availability Zones in a second Region. Use an Aurora global database to deploy the database in the primary Region and the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region.  
B. Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Add an Aurora PostgreSQL cross-Region Aurora Replica in the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region. Promote the secondary to primary as needed.  
C. Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Create an Aurora PostgreSQL database in the second Region. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to replicate the primary database to the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region.  
D. Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Use an Amazon Aurora global database to deploy the database in the primary Region and the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region. Promote the secondary to primary as needed.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: Maximum fault tolerance comes from a full second site: the web tier and application tier are deployed in a second Region, the database uses an Aurora global database with storage-level replication (typically under one second of lag), and Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy shift traffic, after which the secondary cluster is promoted to primary.  
Why A is not selected: An Auto Scaling group exists within a single Region and cannot launch instances in Availability Zones belonging to a different Region. This option is technically impossible.  
Why B is not selected: A cross-Region Aurora replica created the standard way replicates data at the logical layer and is slower than a global database, while the requirement specifically calls for maximum fault tolerance.  
Why C is not selected: AWS DMS is a migration tool, not a built-in mechanism for ongoing cross-Region Aurora replication. It's an extra moving part that can become a point of failure itself.

---

528\. A data analytics company wants to migrate its batch processing system to AWS. The company receives thousands of small data files periodically during the day through FTP. An on-premises batch job processes the data files overnight. However, the batch job takes hours to finish running.  
The company wants the AWS solution to process incoming data files as soon as possible with minimal changes to the FTP clients that send the files. The solution must delete the incoming data files after the files have been processed successfully. Processing for each file needs to take 3-8 minutes.  
Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?  
A. Use an Amazon EC2 instance that runs an FTP server to store incoming files as objects in Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch. Use Amazon EventBridge rules to invoke the job to process the objects nightly from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. Delete the objects after the job has processed the objects.  
B. Use an Amazon EC2 instance that runs an FTP server to store incoming files on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch. Use Amazon EventBridge rules to invoke the job to process the files nightly from the EBS volume. Delete the files after the job has processed the files.  
C. Use AWS Transfer Family to create an FTP server to store incoming files on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch. Use an Amazon S3 event notification when each file arrives to invoke the job in AWS Batch. Delete the files after the job has processed the files.  
D. Use AWS Transfer Family to create an FTP server to store incoming files in Amazon S3 Standard. Create an AWS Lambda function to process the files and to delete the files after they are processed. Use an S3 event notification to invoke the Lambda function when the files arrive.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: The FTP clients can't be changed, and processing must start immediately and takes three to eight minutes. AWS Transfer Family provides a managed FTP server that writes files directly to S3; an object-created event notification triggers a Lambda function that processes the file and then deletes it. Eight minutes fits comfortably within Lambda's fifteen-minute execution limit, and there are no servers in the solution at all.  
Why A is not selected: The Glacier Flexible Retrieval class requires a retrieval step, and a nightly run contradicts the requirement to process files right away.  
Why B is not selected: A self-managed FTP server on an instance plus a nightly run means both extra operational burden and a violation of the immediate-processing requirement.  
Why C is not selected: AWS Transfer Family cannot write to an EBS volume: only S3 and EFS are supported as storage targets. And S3 event notifications don't apply to files on a volume.

---

529\. A company is migrating its workloads to AWS. The company has transactional and sensitive data in its databases.  
The company wants to use AWS Cloud solutions to increase security and reduce operational overhead for the databases.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Migrate the databases to Amazon EC2. Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) AWS managed key for encryption.  
B. Migrate the databases to Amazon RDS Configure encryption at rest.  
C. Migrate the data to Amazon S3 Use Amazon Macie for data security and protection  
D. Migrate the database to Amazon RDS. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs for data security and protection.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: There are two requirements: increase security and reduce operational load on the databases, while keeping the transactional workload. Managed Amazon RDS addresses both: the service handles patching, backups, Multi-AZ, and monitoring, and encryption at rest is enabled with a KMS key and covers storage, snapshots, backups, and replicas. The connection to the database also uses TLS in transit. Self-managing a database engine on EC2 gets you the same level of security only if you build it yourself.  
Why A is not selected: A database on EC2 leaves patching, backups, fault tolerance, and monitoring on you. Operational load goes up, not down.  
Why C is not selected: S3 with Macie is object storage plus data classification, not a transactional database. There's nowhere for the application to run queries and transactions.  
Why D is not selected: CloudWatch Logs collects logs. It provides neither encryption at rest nor data protection.

---

530\. A company has an online gaming application that has TCP and UDP multiplayer gaming capabilities. The company uses Amazon Route 53 to point the application traffic to multiple Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in different AWS Regions. The company needs to improve application performance and decrease latency for the online game in preparation for user growth.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the NLBs. Increase the Cache-Control max-age parameter.  
B. Replace the NLBs with Application Load Balancers (ALBs). Configure Route 53 to use latency-based routing.  
C. Add AWS Global Accelerator in front of the NLBs. Configure a Global Accelerator endpoint to use the correct listener ports.  
D. Add an Amazon API Gateway endpoint behind the NLBs. Enable API caching. Override method caching for the different stages.  
Answer: C
