Explanation: The traffic is gaming traffic over TCP and UDP, the load balancers already sit in multiple Regions, and the goal is to improve latency. Global Accelerator ingests packets at the edge location closest to the player, routes them over the AWS backbone to the right Region, and operates at layer 4, meaning it supports both TCP and UDP. To set this up, its listeners are configured on the same ports as the NLBs.  
Why A is not selected: CloudFront is built for HTTP and caching static content; it doesn't handle the game's UDP traffic, and the max-age parameter doesn't apply to dynamic game sessions.  
Why B is not selected: An Application Load Balancer only handles HTTP and HTTPS — replacing the NLBs with it would drop UDP support.  
Why D is not selected: API Gateway is a front end for HTTP APIs; it isn't deployed "behind" load balancers and has nothing to do with game traffic.

---

531\. A company needs to integrate with a third-party data feed. The data feed sends a webhook to notify an external service when new data is ready for consumption. A developer wrote an AWS Lambda function to retrieve data when the company receives a webhook callback. The developer must make the Lambda function available for the third party to call.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?  
A. Create a function URL for the Lambda function. Provide the Lambda function URL to the third party for the webhook.  
B. Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the Lambda function. Provide the ALB URL to the third party for the webhook.  
C. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Attach the topic to the Lambda function. Provide the public hostname of the SNS topic to the third party for the webhook.  
D. Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Attach the queue to the Lambda function. Provide the public hostname of the SQS queue to the third party for the webhook.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The third party just needs an ordinary HTTPS address it can call to invoke the function. A function URL provides exactly that directly on the Lambda function, along with authentication and CORS configuration, and requires neither a load balancer nor a gateway — the minimum possible operational overhead.  
Why B is not selected: A load balancer runs and is billed around the clock and adds a target group and rules where a single function setting would suffice.  
Why C is not selected: An SNS topic has no public hostname for incoming calls: it delivers messages outward, it doesn't accept arbitrary web requests.  
Why D is not selected: An SQS queue is invoked through the signed AWS API; you can't send an arbitrary webhook to it.

---

532\. A company has a workload in an AWS Region. Customers connect to and access the workload by using an Amazon API Gateway REST API. The company uses Amazon Route 53 as its DNS provider. The company wants to provide individual and secure URLs for all customers.  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency? (Choose three.)  
A. Register the required domain in a registrar. Create a wildcard custom domain name in a Route 53 hosted zone and record in the zone that points to the API Gateway endpoint.  
B. Request a wildcard certificate that matches the domains in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in a different Region.  
C. Create hosted zones for each customer as required in Route 53. Create zone records that point to the API Gateway endpoint.  
D. Request a wildcard certificate that matches the custom domain name in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the same Region.  
E. Create multiple API endpoints for each customer in API Gateway.  
F. Create a custom domain name in API Gateway for the REST API. Import the certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM).  
Answer: ADF  
Explanation: The most operationally efficient way to give every customer an individual, secure URL is a wildcard subdomain pattern. Register the domain, create a record like *.example.com in the Route 53 hosted zone pointing to the API Gateway endpoint (A); request a wildcard certificate in ACM in the same Region, since a Regional API's certificate must live in the API's own Region (D); and create a custom domain name in API Gateway for the REST API, importing that certificate (F). From there, every new customer gets their own subdomain with no infrastructure changes at all.  
Why B is not selected: Region matters here: a Regional API needs its certificate in the same Region, and a certificate in us-east-1 is required only for edge-optimized APIs.  
Why C is not selected: A separate hosted zone per customer means hundreds of zones, each billed and manually maintained — the opposite of operational efficiency.  
Why E is not selected: A separate API endpoint per customer duplicates the same configuration over and over and makes rolling out changes painful.

---

533\. A company stores data in Amazon S3. According to regulations, the data must not contain personally identifiable information (PII). The company recently discovered that S3 buckets have some objects that contain PII. The company needs to automatically detect PII in S3 buckets and to notify the company’s security team.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Use Amazon Macie. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to filter the SensitiveData event type from Macie findings and to send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification to the security team.  
B. Use Amazon GuardDuty. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to filter the CRITICAL event type from GuardDuty findings and to send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification to the security team.  
C. Use Amazon Macie. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to filter the SensitiveData:S3Object/Personal event type from Macie findings and to send an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) notification to the security team.  
D. Use Amazon GuardDuty. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to filter the CRITICAL event type from GuardDuty findings and to send an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) notification to the security team.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Detecting personal data in S3 is Macie's job, and delivering the notification to people is SNS's job. It's the standard pattern: Macie publishes findings to EventBridge, a rule filters events by the SensitiveData type and sends a message to an SNS topic that the security team is subscribed to. Note the key difference between the options: SQS puts a message on a queue that someone still has to read, while an SNS topic delivers the notification straight away, e.g. by email.  
Why B is not selected: GuardDuty looks for signs of compromise, not personal data inside objects. The wrong finding type is selected.  
Why C is not selected: The service choice is correct and the filter is even more precise, but an SQS queue doesn't notify people — it needs a consumer. SNS is what's used to alert the team.  
Why D is not selected: Both the service and the notification delivery method are wrong.

---

534\. A company wants to build a logging solution for its multiple AWS accounts. The company currently stores the logs from all accounts in a centralized account. The company has created an Amazon S3 bucket in the centralized account to store the VPC flow logs and AWS CloudTrail logs. All logs must be highly available for 30 days for frequent analysis, retained for an additional 60 days for backup purposes, and deleted 90 days after creation.  
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Transition objects to the S3 Standard storage class 30 days after creation. Write an expiration action that directs Amazon S3 to delete objects after 90 days.  
B. Transition objects to the S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage class 30 days after creation. Move all objects to the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval storage class after 90 days. Write an expiration action that directs Amazon S3 to delete objects after 90 days.  
C. Transition objects to the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval storage class 30 days after creation. Write an expiration action that directs Amazon S3 to delete objects after 90 days.  
D. Transition objects to the S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) storage class 30 days after creation. Move all objects to the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval storage class after 90 days. Write an expiration action that directs Amazon S3 to delete objects after 90 days.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The logs need to be accessed frequently for the first 30 days, are kept as backup for the next 60, and are deleted on day 90. That means they can already move to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval on day 30 — the cheapest suitable storage class. Even accounting for the 90-day minimum storage duration charge, this is cheaper than keeping the data in Standard-Infrequent Access for all 60 remaining days.  
Why A is not selected: Transitioning to the same Standard class the objects are already in changes nothing and saves nothing.  
Why B is not selected: Standard-IA costs more per gigabyte than the archive class, and moving to Glacier on day 90 at the same time as deletion is pointless — the rule contradicts itself.  
Why D is not selected: The One Zone-IA class stores data in a single Availability Zone, which contradicts the high-availability requirement, and it has the same self-contradictory pair of rules on day 90.

---

535\. A company is building an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster for its workloads. All secrets that are stored in Amazon EKS must be encrypted in the Kubernetes etcd key-value store.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. Use AWS Secrets Manager to manage, rotate, and store all secrets in Amazon EKS.  
B. Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. Enable Amazon EKS KMS secrets encryption on the Amazon EKS cluster.  
C. Create the Amazon EKS cluster with default options. Use the Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver as an add-on.  
D. Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key with the alias/aws/ebs alias. Enable default Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume encryption for the account.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The requirement is very specific: Kubernetes secrets must be encrypted specifically inside the EKS cluster's etcd store. There's a dedicated feature for exactly this — envelope encryption of secrets using a KMS key: it's enabled on the cluster with a customer managed key specified, after which EKS encrypts Secret objects before writing them to etcd. Don't confuse this with storing application secrets: AWS Secrets Manager stores them outside Kubernetes and has no effect on what's in etcd.  
Why A is not selected: Secrets Manager stores secrets in its own service and does not encrypt what's stored in the cluster's etcd. The requirement is specifically about etcd.  
Why C is not selected: The EBS CSI driver attaches volumes to pods. It has nothing to do with encrypting Secret objects in the control plane's store.  
Why D is not selected: Default EBS volume encryption protects node disks, not the control plane's etcd, which EKS manages itself.

---

536\. A company wants to provide data scientists with near real-time read-only access to the company's production Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database. The database is currently configured as a Single-AZ database. The data scientists use complex queries that will not affect the production database. The company needs a solution that is highly available.  
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Scale the existing production database in a maintenance window to provide enough power for the data scientists.  
B. Change the setup from a Single-AZ to a Multi-AZ instance deployment with a larger secondary standby instance. Provide the data scientists access to the secondary instance.  
C. Change the setup from a Single-AZ to a Multi-AZ instance deployment. Provide two additional read replicas for the data scientists.  
D. Change the setup from a Single-AZ to a Multi-AZ cluster deployment with two readable standby instances. Provide read endpoints to the data scientists.  
Answer: C  
Review status: Disputed key (alternative: D)  
Dispute note: A Multi-AZ DB cluster with two readable standbys (D) delivers both HA and read endpoints using three instances, versus four in option C  
Explanation: Three things are needed at once: high availability, a separate place for heavy queries, and minimum cost. The key answer is C: a Multi-AZ instance deployment covers availability, and two read replicas serve the analysts — four instances total. This is disputable because option D solves the same problem with three instances: a Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment with two readable standby instances provides both automatic failover and a reader endpoint for the analysts. Per current documentation, D is cheaper and simpler, and most of the community picks it. Keep the two flavors of Multi-AZ straight: instance deployment has an unreadable standby, cluster deployment has readable standbys.  
Why A is not selected: Scaling up a single instance provides no high availability at all, and the analysts' heavy queries still hit the production database — exactly what the requirement says to avoid.  
Why B is not selected: In a Multi-AZ instance deployment, the standby is not readable: you cannot connect to it for queries. This option describes something that doesn't exist in this deployment type.  
Why D is not selected: A strong alternative, and arguably the better answer: three instances instead of four, HA, and a built-in reader endpoint. The dump key predates the introduction of the Multi-AZ DB cluster with readable standbys, which is why it picks C.

---

537\. A company runs a three-tier web application in the AWS Cloud that operates across three Availability Zones. The application architecture has an Application Load Balancer, an Amazon EC2 web server that hosts user session states, and a MySQL database that runs on an EC2 instance. The company expects sudden increases in application traffic. The company wants to be able to scale to meet future application capacity demands and to ensure high availability across all three Availability Zones.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with high availability to store session data and to cache reads. Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.  
B. Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached with high availability to store session data and to cache reads. Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.  
C. Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon DynamoDB Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) to cache reads. Store the session data in DynamoDB. Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.  
D. Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL in a single Availability Zone. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with high availability to store session data and to cache reads. Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Both scaling and high availability across all three Availability Zones are required. The database moves to RDS for MySQL in a Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment, the web tier moves to an Auto Scaling group spanning three Availability Zones, and session state is moved out of the instances into ElastiCache for Redis: Redis is the one that supports replication and automatic failover, so losing a node doesn't mean losing sessions.  
Why B is not selected: Memcached does not replicate data and has no high-availability mode: a node failure means the sessions stored on it are gone.  
Why C is not selected: Moving MySQL to DynamoDB means reworking the data model and queries, which the requirement doesn't call for.  
Why D is not selected: A database in a single Availability Zone directly contradicts the high-availability requirement.

---

538\. A global video streaming company uses Amazon CloudFront as a content distribution network (CDN). The company wants to roll out content in a phased manner across multiple countries. The company needs to ensure that viewers who are outside the countries to which the company rolls out content are not able to view the content.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Add geographic restrictions to the content in CloudFront by using an allow list. Set up a custom error message.  
B. Set up a new URL tor restricted content. Authorize access by using a signed URL and cookies. Set up a custom error message.  
C. Encrypt the data for the content that the company distributes. Set up a custom error message.  
D. Create a new URL for restricted content. Set up a time-restricted access policy for signed URLs.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: CloudFront can restrict access based on the requester's country: the distribution is configured with a list of allowed countries, and users from anywhere else get a denial with a customizable error page. Rolling content out to countries in phases just means editing that list over time.  
Why B is not selected: Signed URLs and cookies restrict access for specific users, but they can't determine country.  
Why C is not selected: Encryption protects the data but doesn't stop viewing by anyone who already has access through the application — it provides no geographic restriction.  
Why D is not selected: A time-limited link controls how long access lasts, not where the viewer is located.

---

539\. A company wants to use the AWS Cloud to improve its on-premises disaster recovery (DR) configuration. The company's core production business application uses Microsoft SQL Server Standard, which runs on a virtual machine (VM). The application has a recovery point objective (RPO) of 30 seconds or fewer and a recovery time objective (RTO) of 60 minutes. The DR solution needs to minimize costs wherever possible.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Configure a multi-site active/active setup between the on-premises server and AWS by using Microsoft SQL Server Enterprise with Always On availability groups.  
B. Configure a warm standby Amazon RDS for SQL Server database on AWS. Configure AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to use change data capture (CDC).  
C. Use AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery configured to replicate disk changes to AWS as a pilot light.  
D. Use third-party backup software to capture backups every night. Store a secondary set of backups in Amazon S3.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: A 30-second recovery point objective rules out nightly backups, while a one-hour recovery time objective means an active-active setup isn't necessary. A warm standby in the form of RDS for SQL Server, kept current through continuous change data capture replication via AWS DMS, gives a lag measured in seconds and lets you fail over within minutes. This also lets you keep the Standard edition, and you only pay for one small instance.  
Why A is not selected: Always On availability groups require the Enterprise edition — a licensing change — and an active-active setup is the most expensive option of all.  
Why C is not selected: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery replicates disks and is a workable approach, but a pilot light configuration means a longer recovery time, and you'd still need to bring your own SQL Server license; the key distinction is that transaction-level replication is more reliable for a database than block-level replication.  
Why D is not selected: Nightly backups give a recovery point measured in a full day — that misses the 30-second requirement by four orders of magnitude.

---

540\. A company has an on-premises server that uses an Oracle database to process and store customer information.  
The company wants to use an AWS database service to achieve higher availability and to improve application performance. The company also wants to offload reporting from its primary database system.  
Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?  
A. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create an Amazon RDS DB instance in multiple AWS Regions. Point the reporting functions toward a separate DB instance from the primary DB instance.  
B. Use Amazon RDS in a Single-AZ deployment to create an Oracle database. Create a read replica in the same zone as the primary DB instance. Direct the reporting functions to the read replica.  
C. Use Amazon RDS deployed in a Multi-AZ cluster deployment to create an Oracle database. Direct the reporting functions to use the reader instance in the cluster deployment.  
D. Use Amazon RDS deployed in a Multi-AZ instance deployment to create an Amazon Aurora database. Direct the reporting functions to the reader instances.  
Answer: C  
Source note: Question inaccuracy: Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment in Amazon RDS is only supported for MySQL and PostgreSQL — no such mode exists for Oracle. Option C is still the best of the choices given, since it's the only one that provides both high availability and a separate instance for reporting  
Explanation: There are three requirements: higher availability, better application performance, and offloading reporting from the primary database. Deploying RDS as a Multi-AZ cluster covers both: two standbys in different Availability Zones with synchronous replication, plus readable instances that reporting can be pointed at. Note that the question is worded imprecisely — Multi-AZ DB cluster deployments exist only for MySQL and PostgreSQL, not for Oracle; see the audit log for details. Even so, among the options given, C is still the only one that satisfies both requirements at once.  
Why A is not selected: Different Regions address disaster recovery, not availability within a Region, and require ongoing maintenance of DMS tasks.  
Why B is not selected: A single Availability Zone means no high availability, and a replica in that same zone doesn't help if the zone itself fails.  
Why D is not selected: Aurora isn't compatible with Oracle: migrating would require schema conversion and code rewrites, and the phrase "Multi-AZ instance deployment for Aurora" describes a deployment mode that doesn't exist.

---

541\. A company wants to build a web application on AWS. Client access requests to the website are not predictable and can be idle for a long time. Only customers who have paid a subscription fee can have the ability to sign in and use the web application.  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose three.)  
A. Create an AWS Lambda function to retrieve user information from Amazon DynamoDB. Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint to accept RESTful APIs. Send the API calls to the Lambda function.  
B. Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) service behind an Application Load Balancer to retrieve user information from Amazon RDS. Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint to accept RESTful APIs. Send the API calls to the Lambda function.  
C. Create an Amazon Cognito user pool to authenticate users.  
D. Create an Amazon Cognito identity pool to authenticate users.  
E. Use AWS Amplify to serve the frontend web content with HTML, CSS, and JS. Use an integrated Amazon CloudFront configuration.  
F. Use Amazon S3 static web hosting with PHP, CSS, and JS. Use Amazon CloudFront to serve the frontend web content.  
Answer: ACE  
Explanation: Load is unpredictable and can be idle for long stretches, so the company should pay only for actual requests. The backend is a Lambda function behind API Gateway that reads data from DynamoDB (A). Authenticating subscribers requires an Amazon Cognito user pool, which stores accounts and issues tokens (C). The frontend is a static site deployed through AWS Amplify with built-in CloudFront integration (E).  
Why B is not selected: The ECS service behind a load balancer and the RDS database are billed around the clock, even when there is no traffic; the option is also self-contradictory, since it still mentions a Lambda function.  
Why D is not selected: An identity pool issues temporary AWS credentials to already-authenticated users; authentication itself is handled by a user pool.  
Why F is not selected: PHP is a server-side language, and S3 static website hosting cannot execute it: the site would not work.

---

542\. A media company uses an Amazon CloudFront distribution to deliver content over the internet. The company wants only premium customers to have access to the media streams and file content. The company stores all content in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company also delivers content on demand to customers for a specific purpose, such as movie rentals or music downloads.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Generate and provide S3 signed cookies to premium customers.  
B. Generate and provide CloudFront signed URLs to premium customers.  
C. Use origin access control (OAC) to limit the access of non-premium customers.  
D. Generate and activate field-level encryption to block non-premium customers.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: Content is served through CloudFront, so access must be restricted at CloudFront, not at S3. There are two mechanisms: a signed URL grants access to a single specific file for a limited time, and signed cookies grant access to a group of files without changing the URL. The scenario describes granting rights to an individual piece of content "for a specific purpose, such as movie rentals or music downloads" — that is, to a specific object for a specific period — which is a signed URL. Rule of thumb: a single file or a streaming link to one specific resource calls for a signed URL; an entire library or whole site calls for signed cookies.  
Why A is not selected: "S3 signed cookies" doesn't exist: S3 has presigned URLs, while cookies are signed by CloudFront. And even an S3 presigned URL would bypass the distribution, going around the CDN.  
Why C is not selected: Origin access control blocks access to the bucket for everyone except the CloudFront distribution itself. It doesn't distinguish a premium customer from a random viewer — both reach the content through CloudFront.  
Why D is not selected: Field-level encryption encrypts specific fields in users' POST requests (such as a card number) so that intermediate services can't see them. It has nothing to do with restricting access to content.

---

543\. A company runs Amazon EC2 instances in multiple AWS accounts that are individually bled. The company recently purchased a Savings Pian. Because of changes in the company’s business requirements, the company has decommissioned a large number of EC2 instances. The company wants to use its Savings Plan discounts on its other AWS accounts.  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)  
A. From the AWS Account Management Console of the management account, turn on discount sharing from the billing preferences section.  
B. From the AWS Account Management Console of the account that purchased the existing Savings Plan, turn on discount sharing from the billing preferences section. Include all accounts.  
C. From the AWS Organizations management account, use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the Savings Plan with other accounts.  
D. Create an organization in AWS Organizations in a new payer account. Invite the other AWS accounts to join the organization from the management account.  
E. Create an organization in AWS Organizations in the existing AWS account with the existing EC2 instances and Savings Plan. Invite the other AWS accounts to join the organization from the management account.  
Answer: AE  
Explanation: Savings Plans discounts are shared across accounts only within a single organization with consolidated billing. Right now the accounts are billed separately, so the company must first create an organization — specifically in the account that already owns the plan and runs the instances (E), otherwise the commitment stays outside the sharing boundary — and invite the other accounts. After that, discount sharing is turned on in the management account (A), and the unused commitment starts covering the other accounts' usage. Compare with {{q:467}}.  
Why B is not selected: The discount-sharing toggle is available only in the organization's management account, not in the account that purchased the Savings Plan.  
Why C is not selected: AWS RAM shares resources such as subnets, prefix lists, and Transit Gateway. Savings Plans are not shared through it.  
Why D is not selected: A new payer account is possible, but then the account with the purchased plan would need to join the organization as a member account; option E is simpler and keeps the commitment inside the sharing boundary from day one.

---

544\. A retail company uses a regional Amazon API Gateway API for its public REST APIs. The API Gateway endpoint is a custom domain name that points to an Amazon Route 53 alias record. A solutions architect needs to create a solution that has minimal effects on customers and minimal data loss to release the new version of APIs.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Create a canary release deployment stage for API Gateway. Deploy the latest API version. Point an appropriate percentage of traffic to the canary stage. After API verification, promote the canary stage to the production stage.  
B. Create a new API Gateway endpoint with a new version of the API in OpenAPI YAML file format. Use the import-to-update operation in merge mode into the API in API Gateway. Deploy the new version of the API to the production stage.  
C. Create a new API Gateway endpoint with a new version of the API in OpenAPI JSON file format. Use the import-to-update operation in overwrite mode into the API in API Gateway. Deploy the new version of the API to the production stage.  
D. Create a new API Gateway endpoint with new versions of the API definitions. Create a custom domain name for the new API Gateway API. Point the Route 53 alias record to the new API Gateway API custom domain name.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The task is to release a new API version with minimal impact on customers and minimal data loss. API Gateway has a built-in mechanism for this: a canary release deployment on the same stage, which receives a set percentage of traffic, has separate metrics and logs, and is promoted to the production stage after verification. Neither the domain name nor the Route 53 record changes, and rollback is instant.  
Why B is not selected: Importing in merge mode updates the live API in place, all at once, for everyone: there's no gradual traffic shift, and rollback is complicated.  
Why C is not selected: Overwrite mode is even riskier — it replaces the entire API definition, so a mistake affects one hundred percent of customers immediately.  
Why D is not selected: A new endpoint with a new domain name and a Route 53 record switch runs into DNS caching: some clients keep hitting the old version for a while, the cutover is uncontrolled, and there's no way to shift a percentage of traffic.

---

545\. A company wants to direct its users to a backup static error page if the company's primary website is unavailable.  
The primary website's DNS records are hosted in Amazon Route 53. The domain is pointing to an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company needs a solution that minimizes changes and infrastructure overhead.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Update the Route 53 records to use a latency routing policy. Add a static error page that is hosted in an Amazon S3 bucket to the records so that the traffic is sent to the most responsive endpoints.  
B. Set up a Route 53 active-passive failover configuration. Direct traffic to a static error page that is hosted in an Amazon S3 bucket when Route 53 health checks determine that the ALB endpoint is unhealthy.  
C. Set up a Route 53 active-active configuration with the ALB and an Amazon EC2 instance that hosts a static error page as endpoints. Configure Route 53 to send requests to the instance only if the health checks fail for the ALB.  
D. Update the Route 53 records to use a multivalue answer routing policy. Create a health check. Direct traffic to the website if the health check passes. Direct traffic to a static error page that is hosted in Amazon S3 if the health check does not pass.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The company needs a fallback error page when the primary site is unavailable, with minimal changes and no new infrastructure. This is exactly what a standard active-passive failover in Route 53 provides: the primary record points to the load balancer and is tied to a health check, while the secondary record points to a static site in an S3 bucket. As long as the health check passes, the primary record answers; once the load balancer is deemed unhealthy, Route 53 starts returning the bucket's address.  
Why A is not selected: Latency-based routing picks the fastest endpoint, not the working one. Some users would land on the error page even while the site is healthy.  
Why C is not selected: An EC2 instance just for a static page is unnecessary infrastructure to maintain, and an active-active configuration conflicts with the requirement to fail over "only when health checks fail."  
Why D is not selected: Multivalue answer returns several records at once and gives no priority to the primary: users could randomly land on the error page even when the site is healthy.

---

546\. A recent analysis of a company's IT expenses highlights the need to reduce backup costs. The company's chief information officer wants to simplify the on-premises backup infrastructure and reduce costs by eliminating the use of physical backup tapes. The company must preserve the existing investment in the on-premises backup applications and workflows.  
What should a solutions architect recommend?  
A. Set up AWS Storage Gateway to connect with the backup applications using the NFS interface.  
B. Set up an Amazon EFS file system that connects with the backup applications using the NFS interface.  
C. Set up an Amazon EFS file system that connects with the backup applications using the iSCSI interface.  
D. Set up AWS Storage Gateway to connect with the backup applications using the iSCSI-virtual tape library (VTL) interface.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: The key requirement is to keep the existing on-premises backup applications and workflows while eliminating physical tapes. That's exactly what Tape Gateway is for: it presents the backup software with a virtual tape library over the iSCSI protocol, while storing the virtual tapes in S3 and then in archival storage classes. The software and processes stay the same; the physical tapes disappear.  
Why A is not selected: NFS access through Storage Gateway is file-based, but the backup applications are configured to work with a tape library: the workflows would need to be redesigned.  
Why B is not selected: EFS over NFS means the same rework of procedures, and file storage costs noticeably more than S3's archival storage classes.  
Why C is not selected: EFS has no iSCSI interface at all: it's a file system that uses the NFS protocol.

---

547\. A company has data collection sensors at different locations. The data collection sensors stream a high volume of data to the company. The company wants to design a platform on AWS to ingest and process high-volume streaming data. The solution must be scalable and support data collection in near real time. The company must store the data in Amazon S3 for future reporting.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to deliver streaming data to Amazon S3.  
B. Use AWS Glue to deliver streaming data to Amazon S3.  
C. Use AWS Lambda to deliver streaming data and store the data to Amazon S3.  
D. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to deliver streaming data to Amazon S3.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: A high-volume data stream needs to be ingested and landed in S3 with the least operational effort. Kinesis Data Firehose does exactly that: a fully managed delivery stream that scales itself, buffers records by time or size, optionally compresses and transforms them, and writes them to a bucket. No clusters, no shards, no code.  
Why B is not selected: AWS Glue is an ETL service for batch processing and cataloging, not a receiver for streaming data from sensors.  
Why C is not selected: Lambda functions would have to be written and wired together by hand, including buffering and retries, whereas Firehose provides this out of the box.  
Why D is not selected: DMS migrates data from databases; it doesn't ingest a stream from sensors.

---

548\. A company has separate AWS accounts for its finance, data analytics, and development departments. Because of costs and security concerns, the company wants to control which services each AWS account can use.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Use AWS Systems Manager templates to control which AWS services each department can use.  
B. Create organization units (OUs) for each department in AWS Organizations. Attach service control policies (SCPs) to the OUs.  
C. Use AWS CloudFormation to automatically provision only the AWS services that each department can use.  
D. Set up a list of products in AWS Service Catalog in the AWS accounts to manage and control the usage of specific AWS services.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The requirement is to centrally restrict which services each department's account can use, without building anything. In AWS Organizations this is done with an OU structure and SCPs: department accounts are grouped into organizational units, and a policy with an allow or deny list of services is attached to each unit. SCPs apply to every principal in the account, including root, and can't be bypassed with local IAM policies. Remember: an SCP restricts but never grants permissions — the effective permissions are the intersection of the SCP and the IAM policies.  
Why A is not selected: Systems Manager templates automate operations, but they don't prevent the use of services that aren't in the template.  
Why C is not selected: CloudFormation describes and provisions resources. It doesn't stop someone from creating something manually outside the template.  
Why D is not selected: Service Catalog is convenient for offering pre-built configurations, but it requires maintaining a product catalog in every account and doesn't restrict direct access to the services' APIs.

---

549\. A company has created a multi-tier application for its ecommerce website. The website uses an Application Load Balancer that resides in the public subnets, a web tier in the public subnets, and a MySQL cluster hosted on Amazon EC2 instances in the private subnets. The MySQL database needs to retrieve product catalog and pricing information that is hosted on the internet by a third-party provider. A solutions architect must devise a strategy that maximizes security without increasing operational overhead.  
What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?  
A. Deploy a NAT instance in the VPC. Route all the internet-based traffic through the NAT instance.  
B. Deploy a NAT gateway in the public subnets. Modify the private subnet route table to direct all internet- bound traffic to the NAT gateway.  
C. Configure an internet gateway and attach it to the VPModify the private subnet route table to direct internet- bound traffic to the internet gateway.  
D. Configure a virtual private gateway and attach it to the VPC. Modify the private subnet route table to direct internet-bound traffic to the virtual private gateway.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The database cluster in the private subnets needs outbound access to an external catalog provider, while inbound connections from outside must remain blocked and operational overhead must not increase. A NAT gateway in the public subnets, with a default route from the private subnets, delivers exactly that: a managed service where connections can only be initiated from inside.  
Why A is not selected: A NAT instance is a regular machine that has to be patched, scaled, and made redundant: operational overhead goes up.  
Why C is not selected: Routing to an internet gateway from a private subnet makes it effectively public and requires public addresses — security goes down.  
Why D is not selected: A virtual private gateway is for connecting a VPN or Direct Connect to your site, and it doesn't provide internet access.

---

550\. A company is using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to encrypt AWS Lambda environment variables. A solutions architect needs to ensure that the required permissions are in place to decrypt and use the environment variables.  
Which steps must the solutions architect take to implement the correct permissions? (Choose two.)  
A. Add AWS KMS permissions in the Lambda resource policy.  
B. Add AWS KMS permissions in the Lambda execution role.  
C. Add AWS KMS permissions in the Lambda function policy.  
D. Allow the Lambda execution role in the AWS KMS key policy.  
E. Allow the Lambda resource policy in the AWS KMS key policy.  
Answer: BD  
Explanation: Access to a KMS key in AWS is always two-sided: the principal needs permission in its IAM policy, and it must also be allowed in the key's own policy. For Lambda environment variables this means two settings: kms:Decrypt permission in the function's execution role (B), and an explicit allow for that role in the key's key policy (D). Missing either half causes an access error when the function runs. Don't confuse the execution role with the function's resource-based policy: the former describes what the function can do, the latter describes who can invoke it.  
Why A is not selected: A Lambda function's resource policy defines which services and accounts are allowed to invoke it. It doesn't grant permissions to use a KMS key.  
Why C is not selected: Function policy is just another name for the same resource-based policy governing who can invoke the function. It has nothing to do with decrypting environment variables.  
Why E is not selected: In a key policy, permission is granted to a principal — a role or an account — not to a "function policy." No such construct exists in KMS.

---

551\. A company has a financial application that produces reports. The reports average 50 KB in size and are stored in Amazon S3. The reports are frequently accessed during the first week after production and must be stored for several years. The reports must be retrievable within 6 hours.  
Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Use S3 Standard. Use an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the reports to S3 Glacier after 7 days.  
B. Use S3 Standard. Use an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the reports to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 7 days.  
C. Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Configure S3 Intelligent-Tiering to transition the reports to S3 Standard- Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) and S3 Glacier.  
D. Use S3 Standard. Use an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the reports to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 7 days.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Notice the size: 50 KB reports. S3 Standard-IA and Glacier Instant Retrieval both have a 128 KB minimum billable object size, so a 50 KB file is billed as if it were 128 KB, which shrinks the savings from a "cheap" tier by nearly two-thirds. The retrieval requirement is lenient — 6 hours — while the data must be kept for years. So the cheapest path is Standard for the first week, then Glacier Flexible Retrieval: its standard retrieval time of 3–5 hours fits within the 6-hour window, and storage costs roughly six times less than Standard-IA.  
Why B is not selected: Standard-IA provides millisecond access that isn't needed here, and it costs noticeably more than Glacier. On 50 KB objects, its 128 KB minimum billable size further erodes the savings.  
Why C is not selected: Intelligent-Tiering charges a monitoring fee per object, and it never moves objects smaller than 128 KB to the cheaper tiers at all. Across millions of small reports, that's cost with no benefit.  
Why D is not selected: Deep Archive delivers an object in 12 hours for standard retrieval and up to 48 hours for bulk retrieval. That doesn't meet the 6-hour requirement.

---

552\. A company needs to optimize the cost of its Amazon EC2 instances. The company also needs to change the type and family of its EC2 instances every 2-3 months.  
What should the company do to meet these requirements?  
A. Purchase Partial Upfront Reserved Instances for a 3-year term.  
B. Purchase a No Upfront Compute Savings Plan for a 1-year term.  
C. Purchase All Upfront Reserved Instances for a 1-year term.  
D. Purchase an All Upfront EC2 Instance Savings Plan for a 1-year term.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The instance type and family change every two to three months, so the commitment must not be tied to them. A Compute Savings Plan gives a discount regardless of instance family, size, Region, or even service, and the no-upfront, 1-year option is the most flexible choice compatible with such frequent changes.  
Why A is not selected: Reserved Instances for a 3-year term lock in a specific family and type: with changes every two to three months, the discount would go unused.  
Why C is not selected: Paying all upfront for Reserved Instances makes the same problem worse — the money is committed to a specific instance type.  
Why D is not selected: An EC2 Instance Savings Plan is tied to an instance family in a specific Region, and it's exactly the family that keeps changing here.

---

553\. A solutions architect needs to review a company's Amazon S3 buckets to discover personally identifiable information (PII). The company stores the PII data in the us-east-1 Region and us-west-2 Region.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Configure Amazon Macie in each Region. Create a job to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.  
B. Configure AWS Security Hub for all Regions. Create an AWS Config rule to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.  
C. Configure Amazon Inspector to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.  
D. Configure Amazon GuardDuty to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Discovering PII across buckets is a job for Amazon Macie. The detail being tested here is that Macie is Regional, so it must be turned on in every Region where the data resides, with a discovery job created in each one. Using a delegated administrator in an organization, this can be managed centrally, but the Regions still have to be listed explicitly.  
Why B is not selected: Security Hub aggregates findings from other services, and AWS Config rules check resource configuration, not object content.  
Why C is not selected: Inspector scans workloads for vulnerabilities and doesn't analyze data in S3.  
Why D is not selected: GuardDuty watches for suspicious activity, including around S3 data, but it doesn't classify personal data inside objects.

---

554\. A company's SAP application has a backend SQL Server database in an on-premises environment. The company wants to migrate its on-premises application and database server to AWS. The company needs an instance type that meets the high demands of its SAP database. On-premises performance data shows that both the SAP application and the database have high memory utilization.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Use the compute optimized instance family for the application. Use the memory optimized instance family for the database.  
B. Use the storage optimized instance family for both the application and the database.  
C. Use the memory optimized instance family for both the application and the database.  
D. Use the high performance computing (HPC) optimized instance family for the application. Use the memory optimized instance family for the database.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: On-premises performance data shows high memory utilization for both the SAP application and the database. So both tiers should move to memory-optimized instances — this is also AWS's recommended choice for SAP.  
Why A is not selected: Compute-optimized instances provide little memory per core and aren't a fit for a memory-hungry SAP application.  
Why B is not selected: Storage-optimized instances are meant for heavy local I/O, but the bottleneck here is memory.  
Why D is not selected: HPC-optimized instances are designed for tightly coupled, network-intensive compute workloads, not for SAP applications.

---

555\. A company runs an application in a VPC with public and private subnets. The VPC extends across multiple Availability Zones. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets. The application uses an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue.  
A solutions architect needs to design a secure solution to establish a connection between the EC2 instances and the SQS queue.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Implement an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon SQS. Configure the endpoint to use the private subnets. Add to the endpoint a security group that has an inbound access rule that allows traffic from the EC2 instances that are in the private subnets.  
B. Implement an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon SQS. Configure the endpoint to use the public subnets. Attach to the interface endpoint a VPC endpoint policy that allows access from the EC2 instances that are in the private subnets.  
C. Implement an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon SQS. Configure the endpoint to use the public subnets. Attach an Amazon SQS access policy to the interface VPC endpoint that allows requests from only a specified VPC endpoint.  
D. Implement a gateway endpoint for Amazon SQS. Add a NAT gateway to the private subnets. Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instances that allows access to the SQS queue.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: SQS is a service with a public API, so instances in private subnets reach it either through NAT or privately through an interface VPC endpoint (PrivateLink). The correct option places the endpoint in the same private subnets where the instances run and protects it with a security group that has an inbound rule for those instances — that's exactly how access to an interface endpoint is controlled. An endpoint policy can additionally be attached to restrict which queues are reachable.  
Why B is not selected: Placing the endpoint in public subnets makes no sense: interfaces need to sit where the clients are — in the private subnets.  
Why C is not selected: Same mistake with public subnets, plus a queue access policy is attached to the queue, not to the endpoint.  
Why D is not selected: A gateway endpoint exists only for S3 and DynamoDB — there is no gateway endpoint for SQS. And a NAT gateway would send the traffic back out to the internet, which is what needs to be avoided.

---

556\. A solutions architect is using an AWS CloudFormation template to deploy a three-tier web application. The web application consists of a web tier and an application tier that stores and retrieves user data in Amazon DynamoDB tables. The web and application tiers are hosted on Amazon EC2 instances, and the database tier is not publicly accessible. The application EC2 instances need to access the DynamoDB tables without exposing API credentials in the template.  
What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?  
A. Create an IAM role to read the DynamoDB tables. Associate the role with the application instances by referencing an instance profile.  
B. Create an IAM role that has the required permissions to read and write from the DynamoDB tables. Add the role to the EC2 instance profile, and associate the instance profile with the application instances.  
C. Use the parameter section in the AWS CloudFormation template to have the user input access and secret keys from an already-created IAM user that has the required permissions to read and write from the DynamoDB tables.  
D. Create an IAM user in the AWS CloudFormation template that has the required permissions to read and write from the DynamoDB tables. Use the GetAtt function to retrieve the access and secret keys, and pass them to the application instances through the user data.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The instances need to read from and write to DynamoDB without any credentials appearing in the template. The standard approach: an IAM role with the required permissions, an instance profile carrying that role, and a reference to the profile on the instances. The application then gets temporary credentials from instance metadata. Note the difference from the neighboring option: there the role grants read-only access, but the application also stores user data, so write access is needed too.  
Why A is not selected: A read-only role wouldn't let the application store user data, and the requirement calls for storing and retrieving it.  
Why C is not selected: Entering access keys as a template parameter is exactly what the requirement asks to avoid: the secret ends up in the stack's parameters and in the hands of whoever deploys it.  
Why D is not selected: The GetAtt function can indeed return a created user's access key, but passing the secret through user data leaves it in plaintext in the instance's metadata.

---

557\. A solutions architect manages an analytics application. The application stores large amounts of semistructured data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The solutions architect wants to use parallel data processing to process the data more quickly. The solutions architect also wants to use information that is stored in an Amazon Redshift database to enrich the data.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Use Amazon Athena to process the S3 data. Use AWS Glue with the Amazon Redshift data to enrich the S3 data.  
B. Use Amazon EMR to process the S3 data. Use Amazon EMR with the Amazon Redshift data to enrich the S3 data.  
C. Use Amazon EMR to process the S3 data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to move the S3 data into Amazon Redshift so that the data can be enriched.  
D. Use AWS Glue to process the S3 data. Use AWS Lake Formation with the Amazon Redshift data to enrich the S3 data.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Semi-structured data lives in S3 and needs to be processed in parallel: Amazon Athena runs queries against S3 in a distributed, serverless way. Enriching the data with information from Redshift is handled by AWS Glue, which has connectors to both S3 and Redshift, so the join happens within a single ETL job.  
Why B is not selected: EMR would work, but it's a cluster that has to be provisioned, configured, and maintained, whereas both steps here are covered by serverless services.  
Why C is not selected: Kinesis Data Streams is meant for streaming data; using it to move files that already sit in S3 into Redshift doesn't fit.  
Why D is not selected: Lake Formation manages access and the data lake catalog — it doesn't enrich data.

---

558\. A company has two VPCs that are located in the us-west-2 Region within the same AWS account. The company needs to allow network traffic between these VPCs. Approximately 500 GB of data transfer will occur between the VPCs each month.  
What is the MOST cost-effective solution to connect these VPCs?  
A. Implement AWS Transit Gateway to connect the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the transit gateway for inter-VPC communication.  
B. Implement an AWS Site-to-Site VPN tunnel between the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the VPN tunnel for inter-VPC communication.  
C. Set up a VPC peering connection between the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the VPC peering connection for inter-VPC communication.  
D. Set up a 1 GB AWS Direct Connect connection between the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the Direct Connect connection for inter-VPC communication.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: Two networks in the same Region and the same account, with about 500 GB of monthly data transfer — the cheapest way to connect them is VPC peering. There's no charge for the connection itself, only for the data transferred, and there are no hourly fees. It's set up in one step, plus routes in both route tables.  
Why A is not selected: Transit Gateway charges an hourly fee per attachment plus a per-GB data processing charge. For two VPCs, that's noticeably more expensive than peering.  
Why B is not selected: A VPN between two VPCs adds an hourly connection charge, encryption overhead, and a tunnel bandwidth limit — unnecessary when private connectivity is already available within the Region.  
Why D is not selected: Direct Connect is for connecting your own site to AWS. It can't be used to connect two VPCs within the same Region, and it costs disproportionately more.

---

559\. A company hosts multiple applications on AWS for different product lines. The applications use different compute resources, including Amazon EC2 instances and Application Load Balancers. The applications run in different AWS accounts under the same organization in AWS Organizations across multiple AWS Regions. Teams for each product line have tagged each compute resource in the individual accounts.  
The company wants more details about the cost for each product line from the consolidated billing feature in Organizations.  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)  
A. Select a specific AWS generated tag in the AWS Billing console.  
B. Select a specific user-defined tag in the AWS Billing console.  
C. Select a specific user-defined tag in the AWS Resource Groups console.  
D. Activate the selected tag from each AWS account.  
E. Activate the selected tag from the Organizations management account.  
Answer: BE  
Explanation: Tags that teams apply only affect billing once they're activated as cost allocation tags. They're activated in the Billing console (B — select the desired user-defined tag), specifically in the organization's management account (E); after that, Cost Explorer and consolidated billing reports can group costs by that tag across all accounts and Regions. Keep the distinction in mind: AWS-generated tags start with the aws: prefix and are created by the platform, while user-defined tags are ones you create yourself. Related question: {{q:459}}.  
Why A is not selected: AWS-generated tags are the platform's own internal labels. The product lines here are tagged with the company's own tags — that is, user-defined ones.  
Why C is not selected: Resource Groups helps group resources for operations, but activating cost allocation tags is done in the Billing console.  
Why D is not selected: Member accounts have no such activation option: cost allocation tags are turned on centrally, in the management account.

---

560\. A company's solutions architect is designing an AWS multi-account solution that uses AWS Organizations. The solutions architect has organized the company's accounts into organizational units (OUs).  
The solutions architect needs a solution that will identify any changes to the OU hierarchy. The solution also needs to notify the company's operations team of any changes.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Provision the AWS accounts by using AWS Control Tower. Use account drift notifications to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.  
B. Provision the AWS accounts by using AWS Control Tower. Use AWS Config aggregated rules to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.  
C. Use AWS Service Catalog to create accounts in Organizations. Use an AWS CloudTrail organization trail to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.  
D. Use AWS CloudFormation templates to create accounts in Organizations. Use the drift detection operation on a stack to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Changes to the organization's OU structure need to be detected and reported to the operations team, without building a custom system for it. AWS Control Tower maintains a baseline of the landscape and reports drift itself — including accounts moving between OUs, hierarchy changes, and guardrail edits. Notifications are published to an SNS topic that the operations team subscribes to. No custom code or rules are required.  
Why B is not selected: AWS Config rules work with resource configuration inside accounts. They don't track the organization's OU hierarchy.  
Why C is not selected: An organization trail in CloudTrail would show API calls like MoveAccount, but the filtering, metrics, and notifications would all have to be built from scratch — more work than the ready-made drift notifications.  
Why D is not selected: CloudFormation drift detection compares a stack's resources against its template. It has nothing to do with an organization's OU structure.

---

561\. A company's website handles millions of requests each day, and the number of requests continues to increase. A solutions architect needs to improve the response time of the web application. The solutions architect determines that the application needs to decrease latency when retrieving product details from the Amazon DynamoDB table.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?  
A. Set up a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster. Route all read requests through DAX.  
B. Set up Amazon ElastiCache for Redis between the DynamoDB table and the web application. Route all read requests through Redis.  
C. Set up Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached between the DynamoDB table and the web application. Route all read requests through Memcached.  
D. Set up Amazon DynamoDB Streams on the table, and have AWS Lambda read from the table and populate Amazon ElastiCache. Route all read requests through ElastiCache.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The goal is to reduce read latency from DynamoDB with the least operational overhead. DAX was built exactly for this: a managed cache sitting directly in front of the table, compatible with the same API, so no loading or invalidation logic needs to be written — it's built in.  
Why B is not selected: Redis would deliver low latency, but caching, expiration, and consistency would have to be managed in application code.  
Why C is not selected: Same issue with Memcached, plus no data replication.  
Why D is not selected: Populating a cache through a stream and a function is the most complex of the proposed designs and the most to maintain.

---

562\. A solutions architect needs to ensure that API calls to Amazon DynamoDB from Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC do not travel across the internet.  
Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet this requirement? (Choose two.)  
A. Create a route table entry for the endpoint.  
B. Create a gateway endpoint for DynamoDB.  
C. Create an interface endpoint for Amazon EC2.  
D. Create an elastic network interface for the endpoint in each of the subnets of the VPC.  
E. Create a security group entry in the endpoint's security group to provide access.  
Answer: AB  
Explanation: A gateway endpoint for DynamoDB (B) provides private access, and adding a route table entry with the service prefix (A) routes traffic through it. These two steps are enough: calls to the tables stop leaving the internet.  
Why C is not selected: An interface endpoint for EC2 gives private access to the instance-management API, not to DynamoDB.  
Why D is not selected: Elastic network interfaces are created for interface endpoints; a gateway endpoint works through routes and has no interfaces.  
Why E is not selected: Security groups apply to interface endpoints. A gateway endpoint has none — access is restricted through an endpoint policy instead.

---

563\. A company runs its applications on both Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) clusters and on- premises Kubernetes clusters. The company wants to view all clusters and workloads from a central location.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Use Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights to collect and group the cluster information.  
B. Use Amazon EKS Connector to register and connect all Kubernetes clusters.  
C. Use AWS Systems Manager to collect and view the cluster information.  
D. Use Amazon EKS Anywhere as the primary cluster to view the other clusters with native Kubernetes commands.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: Kubernetes clusters run both in AWS and on premises, and they need to be viewed from one place. Amazon EKS Connector registers external clusters in the EKS console, after which those clusters and their workloads appear alongside the managed ones. An agent is installed; no other infrastructure is required.  
Why A is not selected: Container Insights collects metrics and logs, but it doesn't provide a unified list of clusters and their workloads.  
Why C is not selected: Systems Manager manages nodes, not Kubernetes objects: it won't show cluster information in the needed form.  
Why D is not selected: EKS Anywhere is a way to run clusters on your own site, not a tool for observing other people's clusters.

---

564\. A company is building an ecommerce application and needs to store sensitive customer information. The company needs to give customers the ability to complete purchase transactions on the website. The company also needs to ensure that sensitive customer data is protected, even from database administrators.  
Which solution meets these requirements?  
A. Store sensitive data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Use EBS encryption to encrypt the data. Use an IAM instance role to restrict access.  
B. Store sensitive data in Amazon RDS for MySQL. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) client-side encryption to encrypt the data.  
C. Store sensitive data in Amazon S3. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) server-side encryption to encrypt the data. Use S3 bucket policies to restrict access.  
D. Store sensitive data in Amazon FSx for Windows Server. Mount the file share on application servers. Use Windows file permissions to restrict access.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The discriminator is "even from database administrators." Any transparent storage-level encryption (EBS, RDS, S3 SSE) decrypts data automatically for anyone with access to the service, so a database administrator would see the content as usual. The only way to protect data from a privileged operator is client-side encryption: the application encrypts the field with a KMS key before writing it, and the table stores ciphertext that's useless without access to the key. Control over the key is kept separate from control over the database — that's the whole point of the separation of duties.  
Why A is not selected: EBS volume encryption is transparent to the operating system and to anyone who gains access to the instance. It doesn't protect against an administrator.  
Why C is not selected: S3 server-side encryption decrypts the object for anyone allowed access to the bucket and the key. Plus, S3 isn't a transactional store for purchases.  
Why D is not selected: Windows file system permissions are bypassed by the server administrator, and there's no data encryption here at all.

---

565\. A company has an on-premises MySQL database that handles transactional data. The company is migrating the database to the AWS Cloud. The migrated database must maintain compatibility with the company's applications that use the database. The migrated database also must scale automatically during periods of increased demand.  
Which migration solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Use native MySQL tools to migrate the database to Amazon RDS for MySQL. Configure elastic storage scaling.  
B. Migrate the database to Amazon Redshift by using the mysqldump utility. Turn on Auto Scaling for the Amazon Redshift cluster.  
C. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the database to Amazon Aurora. Turn on Aurora Auto Scaling.  
D. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB. Configure an Auto Scaling policy.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The applications must keep working without changes, so the target needs an engine compatible with MySQL that also scales automatically. Aurora MySQL is compatible at the protocol and query level, its storage grows on its own, and Aurora Auto Scaling adds and removes read replicas based on load. AWS DMS migrates the data while letting the source database keep running during the migration.  
Why A is not selected: RDS for MySQL is compatible, but storage scaling is about space, not performance: compute capacity still has to be scaled manually.  
Why B is not selected: Redshift is an analytics warehouse; it doesn't suit transactional workloads and isn't compatible with the application.  
Why D is not selected: DynamoDB is a non-relational store: every SQL query would have to be rewritten.

---

566\. A company runs multiple Amazon EC2 Linux instances in a VPC across two Availability Zones. The instances host applications that use a hierarchical directory structure. The applications need to read and write rapidly and concurrently to shared storage.  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?  
A. Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Allow access from all the EC2 instances in the VPC.  
B. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system from each EC2 instance.  
C. Create a file system on a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Attach the EBS volume to all the EC2 instances.  
D. Create file systems on Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes that are attached to each EC2 instance. Synchronize the EBS volumes across the different EC2 instances.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The requirements are a hierarchical directory structure and fast, concurrent writes from instances in two Availability Zones. That's the profile of Amazon EFS: a file system using the NFS protocol, mountable on every instance, with mount targets in each zone and consistency under concurrent writes.  
Why A is not selected: S3 is object storage: it has no real directory hierarchy or file operations, and the application is built specifically around those.  
Why C is not selected: An io2 volume attaches within a single Availability Zone, so instances in the second zone can't reach it, and a regular file system isn't designed for concurrent writes from multiple machines.  
Why D is not selected: Synchronizing separate volumes between instances causes data drift and lag: it doesn't provide concurrent writes.

---

567\. A solutions architect is designing a workload that will store hourly energy consumption by business tenants in a building. The sensors will feed a database through HTTP requests that will add up usage for each tenant. The solutions architect must use managed services when possible. The workload will receive more features in the future as the solutions architect adds independent components.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Use Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions to receive the data from the sensors, process the data, and store the data in an Amazon DynamoDB table.  
B. Use an Elastic Load Balancer that is supported by an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to receive and process the data from the sensors. Use an Amazon S3 bucket to store the processed data.  
C. Use Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions to receive the data from the sensors, process the data, and store the data in a Microsoft SQL Server Express database on an Amazon EC2 instance.  
D. Use an Elastic Load Balancer that is supported by an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to receive and process the data from the sensors. Use an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) shared file system to store the processed data.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Sensors send readings over HTTP, the volume is small and uneven, and the solution needs managed services plus the ability to add components easily. API Gateway receives the requests, a Lambda function processes and totals the readings, and DynamoDB stores the result. There are no servers to operate, scaling is automatic, and new independent components can be added just by subscribing to events.  
Why B is not selected: A fleet of instances behind a load balancer needs patching, monitoring, and scaling, and storing aggregates in S3 is awkward for frequently updated per-tenant counters.  
Why C is not selected: The first half is right, but SQL Server Express on an EC2 instance means a machine and a database that have to be managed by hand, and a single point of failure.  
Why D is not selected: Again a self-managed fleet of instances, and a shared file system is the wrong storage model for consumption counters.

---

568\. A solutions architect is designing the storage architecture for a new web application used for storing and viewing engineering drawings. All application components will be deployed on the AWS infrastructure.  
The application design must support caching to minimize the amount of time that users wait for the engineering drawings to load. The application must be able to store petabytes of data.  
Which combination of storage and caching should the solutions architect use?  
A. Amazon S3 with Amazon CloudFront  
B. Amazon S3 Glacier with Amazon ElastiCache  
C. Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes with Amazon CloudFront  
D. AWS Storage Gateway with Amazon ElastiCache  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The requirements are petabytes of storage and caching so drawings load quickly. S3 stores an unlimited amount of data without capacity planning, and CloudFront caches it at edge locations close to users. The pairing is standard and requires no servers or capacity tuning.  
Why B is not selected: Glacier is an archive with retrieval times measured in minutes to hours, and ElastiCache caches in memory within a Region — not built for large files.  
Why C is not selected: EBS volumes are capacity-limited, tied to a single Availability Zone, and don't scale to petabytes.  
Why D is not selected: Storage Gateway is a hybrid gateway for an on-premises site, while every component of this application is stated to run in AWS.

---

569\. An Amazon EventBridge rule targets a third-party API. The third-party API has not received any incoming traffic. A solutions architect needs to determine whether the rule conditions are being met and if the rule's target is being invoked.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Check for metrics in Amazon CloudWatch in the namespace for AWS/Events.  
B. Review events in the Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) dead-letter queue.  
C. Check for the events in Amazon CloudWatch Logs.  
D. Check the trails in AWS CloudTrail for the EventBridge events.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: EventBridge publishes its own metrics to CloudWatch under the AWS/Events namespace: TriggeredRules shows whether the rule fired at all, while Invocations and FailedInvocations show whether the target was actually called. Those are exactly the two questions that need to be told apart.  
Why B is not selected: The dead-letter queue only holds failed invocations and stays empty if the rule never fired in the first place.  
Why C is not selected: CloudWatch Logs stores logs, not rule-invocation statistics; logging for EventBridge events has to be set up separately.  
Why D is not selected: CloudTrail records management API calls, not whether the rule fired and invoked its target.

---

570\. A company has a large workload that runs every Friday evening. The workload runs on Amazon EC2 instances that are in two Availability Zones in the us-east-1 Region. Normally, the company must run no more than two instances at all times. However, the company wants to scale up to six instances each Friday to handle a regularly repeating increased workload.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Create a reminder in Amazon EventBridge to scale the instances.  
B. Create an Auto Scaling group that has a scheduled action.  
C. Create an Auto Scaling group that uses manual scaling.  
D. Create an Auto Scaling group that uses automatic scaling.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The spike repeats on a known schedule — every Friday evening. An Auto Scaling group's scheduled actions change the desired and minimum capacity at a set time and then revert it. It's configured once and runs itself.  
Why A is not selected: A reminder just means someone will scale the group by hand every week.  
Why C is not selected: Manual scaling is the same thing: weekly human intervention.  
Why D is not selected: A metric-based automatic policy would only react after the load appears and requires tuning thresholds, whereas the timing of the spike is already known in advance.

---

571\. A company is creating a REST API. The company has strict requirements for the use of TLS. The company requires TLSv1.3 on the API endpoints. The company also requires a specific public third-party certificate authority (CA) to sign the TLS certificate.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Use a local machine to create a certificate that is signed by the third-party CImport the certificate into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Create an HTTP API in Amazon API Gateway with a custom domain. Configure the custom domain to use the certificate.  
B. Create a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) that is signed by the third-party CA. Create an HTTP API in Amazon API Gateway with a custom domain. Configure the custom domain to use the certificate.  
C. Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a certificate that is signed by the third-party CA. Import the certificate into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Create an AWS Lambda function with a Lambda function URL. Configure the Lambda function URL to use the certificate.  
D. Create a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) that is signed by the third-party CA. Create an AWS Lambda function with a Lambda function URL. Configure the Lambda function URL to use the certificate.  
Answer: A  
Review status: Corrected key (source: B; reviewed: A)  
Correction note: ACM doesn't issue certificates signed by a third-party CA — it only imports them; options B and D are technically impossible. examtopics t1 q571
