Explanation: ACM does not issue certificates signed by a third-party public CA: it either issues its own or accepts an imported one. So the only workable path is to obtain the certificate from the required CA outside of ACM, import it into ACM, and attach it to a custom domain in API Gateway (A).  
Why B is not selected: Creating a certificate in ACM that is signed by a third-party CA is not technically possible: ACM only signs certificates with its own certificate authority.  
Why C is not selected: Same impossible premise about issuing the certificate in ACM, plus a Lambda function URL does not support a custom domain or certificate.  
Why D is not selected: Repeats the same mistake: ACM cannot create a certificate from a third-party CA, and a function URL cannot be configured with a custom certificate.

---

572\. A company runs an application on AWS. The application receives inconsistent amounts of usage. The application uses AWS Direct Connect to connect to an on-premises MySQL-compatible database. The on-premises database consistently uses a minimum of 2 GiB of memory.  
The company wants to migrate the on-premises database to a managed AWS service. The company wants to use auto scaling capabilities to manage unexpected workload increases.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?  
A. Provision an Amazon DynamoDB database with default read and write capacity settings.  
B. Provision an Amazon Aurora database with a minimum capacity of 1 Aurora capacity unit (ACU).  
C. Provision an Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 database with a minimum capacity of 1 Aurora capacity unit (ACU).  
D. Provision an Amazon RDS for MySQL database with 2 GiB of memory.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The workload is inconsistent, the database is MySQL-compatible, and the company needs auto scaling with minimal administration. Aurora Serverless v2 fits exactly: capacity is measured in Aurora capacity units (ACUs), and each ACU provides roughly 2 GiB of memory, so a minimum of 1 ACU covers the stated steady-state 2 GiB, while the cluster scales up smoothly with no interruption in service.  
Why A is not selected: DynamoDB is a non-relational data store: an application built for MySQL would have to be rewritten, and 'default capacity settings' means fixed provisioned capacity with no auto scaling.  
Why B is not selected: A standard provisioned Aurora cluster is sized by instance class, not ACUs: this option describes a configuration that doesn't exist, and provisioned Aurora has no automatic compute scaling.  
Why D is not selected: RDS for MySQL with a fixed memory size does not scale for sudden workload increases: changing the instance class requires a manual change and downtime.

---

573\. A company wants to use an event-driven programming model with AWS Lambda. The company wants to reduce startup latency for Lambda functions that run on Java 11. The company does not have strict latency requirements for the applications. The company wants to reduce cold starts and outlier latencies when a function scales up.  
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Configure Lambda provisioned concurrency.  
B. Increase the timeout of the Lambda functions.  
C. Increase the memory of the Lambda functions.  
D. Configure Lambda SnapStart.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: This is about cold-start latency for Java functions, with no strict latency requirements and a need for the most cost-effective option. Lambda SnapStart takes a snapshot of the initialized execution environment and restores it at invocation, cutting cold-start time dramatically — and it is not billed as continuously maintained capacity.  
Why A is not selected: Provisioned concurrency solves the same problem, but you pay for the entire time the instances are reserved: without strict latency requirements, that's overpaying.  
Why B is not selected: The timeout setting limits the maximum execution duration and has no effect on startup.  
Why C is not selected: More memory speeds up initialization slightly, but it also raises the cost of every invocation and doesn't address the root cause of the cold start.

---

574\. A financial services company launched a new application that uses an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. The company uses the application to track stock market trends. The company needs to operate the application for only 2 hours at the end of each week. The company needs to optimize the cost of running the database.  
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Aurora Serverless v2 MySQL database cluster.  
B. Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Aurora MySQL database cluster.  
C. Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Amazon EC2 instance that runs MySQL. Purchase an instance reservation for the EC2 instance.  
D. Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that uses MySQL container images to run tasks.  
Answer: B  
Review status: Disputed key (alternative: A)  
Dispute note: 2 hours of use per week: Aurora Serverless v2 scales down but not to zero; a provisioned cluster can be stopped for at most 7 days — both options are debatable  
Explanation: The database is needed for two hours a week — paying for the other 166 hours makes no sense. The answer key picks B: a provisioned Aurora cluster can be stopped, and a stopped cluster is not billed for compute (you pay only for storage). Two details make this debatable: AWS automatically restarts a stopped Aurora cluster after 7 days, and at the version of Aurora Serverless v2 this dump reflects, it scaled down but not to zero, so the minimum capacity was billed continuously. Today Serverless v2 can scale to zero, which makes option A the stronger answer on a current exam. The underlying principle stays the same: for rare, short-lived workloads, either pay only for what you consume or stop the cluster entirely.  
Why A is not selected: A strong alternative. At the service version this question reflects, Serverless v2 could not scale below its minimum ACU, meaning it was billed around the clock — so the answer key preferred a cluster that can be stopped entirely.  
Why C is not selected: A Reserved Instance is billed regardless of whether the machine is running — the worst choice for two hours a week of use. It also means self-managing MySQL instead of using a managed database.  
Why D is not selected: Running MySQL in ECS containers again means self-managing the database, plus you still need to solve persistent storage. There's no cost savings compared with a stopped managed cluster.

---

575\. A company deploys its applications on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) behind an Application Load Balancer in an AWS Region. The application needs to store data in a PostgreSQL database engine. The company wants the data in the database to be highly available. The company also needs increased capacity for read workloads.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?  
A. Create an Amazon DynamoDB database table configured with global tables.  
B. Create an Amazon RDS database with Multi-AZ deployments.  
C. Create an Amazon RDS database with Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment.  
D. Create an Amazon RDS database configured with cross-Region read replicas.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: Both high availability and extra read capacity are required, with minimal operational effort. The RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment provides exactly that: a primary instance plus two standby instances in other Availability Zones, with the standbys available for read traffic through a dedicated reader endpoint. A single configuration covers both requirements.  
Why A is not selected: DynamoDB is not PostgreSQL: the application would have to be rewritten.  
Why B is not selected: A standard Multi-AZ deployment provides availability, but the standby instance doesn't serve read traffic, so it adds no read capacity.  
Why D is not selected: Cross-Region read replicas are meant for readers in other parts of the world and for disaster recovery; for availability within a single Region, they add unnecessary cost and latency.

---

576\. A company is building a RESTful serverless web application on AWS by using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The users of this web application will be geographically distributed, and the company wants to reduce the latency of API requests to these users.  
Which type of endpoint should a solutions architect use to meet these requirements?  
A. Private endpoint  
B. Regional endpoint  
C. Interface VPC endpoint  
D. Edge-optimized endpoint  
Answer: D  
Explanation: Users are distributed worldwide, and API request latency needs to be reduced. An edge-optimized endpoint routes requests through the nearest CloudFront edge location, from which they travel to the Region over the AWS backbone: the TLS connection is established close to the user, and overall request latency drops significantly.  
Why A is not selected: A private endpoint is accessible only from within a VPC — it doesn't work for public users.  
Why B is not selected: A Regional endpoint receives requests directly in the Region: remote users would experience the full latency to reach it.  
Why C is not selected: An interface VPC endpoint is a way to reach a private API from within a network, not a way to speed things up for internet users.

---

577\. A company uses an Amazon CloudFront distribution to serve content pages for its website. The company needs to ensure that clients use a TLS certificate when accessing the company's website. The company wants to automate the creation and renewal of the TLS certificates.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?  
A. Use a CloudFront security policy to create a certificate.  
B. Use a CloudFront origin access control (OAC) to create a certificate.  
C. Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a certificate. Use DNS validation for the domain.  
D. Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a certificate. Use email validation for the domain.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: Certificates for CloudFront are issued by AWS Certificate Manager, at no charge. The key detail is domain ownership validation via DNS: with DNS validation, ACM renews the certificate automatically as long as the CNAME record stays in the hosted zone. That's exactly the automated issuance and renewal the requirement calls for.  
Why A is not selected: A security policy sets the minimum TLS version and cipher suite; it doesn't issue certificates.  
Why B is not selected: Origin access control restricts access to an origin, such as an S3 bucket, and has nothing to do with certificates.  
Why D is not selected: Email validation requires manual confirmation at every renewal, so it doesn't provide automation.

---

578\. A company deployed a serverless application that uses Amazon DynamoDB as a database layer. The application has experienced a large increase in users. The company wants to improve database response time from milliseconds to microseconds and to cache requests to the database.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX).  
B. Migrate the database to Amazon Redshift.  
C. Migrate the database to Amazon RDS.  
D. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The requirement to go 'from milliseconds to microseconds' and 'cache requests to the database' describes DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) almost word for word: a managed, API-compatible cache in front of the table, so the application only needs to change its endpoint.  
Why B is not selected: Redshift is an analytics warehouse for large-scale queries, not a fast database for an application.  
Why C is not selected: Migrating to RDS means reworking the data model, and it still doesn't deliver microsecond response times.  
Why D is not selected: Redis can deliver the needed speed, but it requires building custom caching and invalidation logic, meaning more operational overhead.

---

579\. A company runs an application that uses Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The application receives traffic only on weekdays during business hours. The company wants to optimize costs and reduce operational overhead based on this usage.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Use the Instance Scheduler on AWS to configure start and stop schedules.  
B. Turn off automatic backups. Create weekly manual snapshots of the database.  
C. Create a custom AWS Lambda function to start and stop the database based on minimum CPU utilization.  
D. Purchase All Upfront reserved DB instances.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The database is needed only during business hours on weekdays, and the company doesn't want to spend effort building automation. The ready-made Instance Scheduler on AWS solution deploys from a template and automatically starts and stops RDS and EC2 instances on a schedule — no custom code required.  
Why B is not selected: Turning off automatic backups saves pennies while also giving up point-in-time recovery.  
Why C is not selected: A custom function means code that has to be written and maintained; on top of that, CPU utilization is a poor signal for deciding when to stop the database.  
Why D is not selected: All Upfront reserved pricing pays off with round-the-clock usage, but here the database is needed for only about a quarter of the week.

---

580\. A company uses locally attached storage to run a latency-sensitive application on premises. The company is using a lift and shift method to move the application to the AWS Cloud. The company does not want to change the application architecture.  
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Configure an Auto Scaling group with an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system to run the application.  
B. Host the application on an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) GP2 volume to run the application.  
C. Configure an Auto Scaling group with an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system to run the application.  
D. Host the application on an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) GP3 volume to run the application.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: A lift-and-shift migration with no architecture changes means the locally attached storage is replaced with a block volume on the instance. Among general purpose volumes, gp3 is the cheapest: for the same size it costs roughly 20% less than gp2 while providing baseline performance of 3,000 IOPS and 125 MB/s regardless of volume size, whereas gp2 performance scales with volume size.  
Why A is not selected: FSx for Lustre is an expensive file system built for high-performance computing, while the application was designed for a local disk, not a shared resource.  
Why B is not selected: A gp2 volume solves the problem technically, but it costs more than gp3 at the same capacity, and cost is the deciding requirement here.  
Why C is not selected: FSx for OpenZFS is also a shared file system and also costs more than a block volume; it would require changing the architecture as well.

---

581\. A company runs a stateful production application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application requires at least two EC2 instances to always be running.  
A solutions architect needs to design a highly available and fault-tolerant architecture for the application. The solutions architect creates an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances.  
Which set of additional steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements?  
A. Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to two. Deploy one On-Demand Instance in one Availability Zone and one On-Demand Instance in a second Availability Zone.  
B. Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to four. Deploy two On-Demand Instances in one Availability Zone and two On-Demand Instances in a second Availability Zone.  
C. Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to two. Deploy four Spot Instances in one Availability Zone.  
D. Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to four. Deploy two On-Demand Instances in one Availability Zone and two Spot Instances in a second Availability Zone.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The requirement is for at least two instances to always be running, and for the architecture to survive an Availability Zone failure. That means each of the two zones needs two instances, with the group's minimum capacity set to four: if an entire zone is lost, exactly two instances remain running, as required.  
Why A is not selected: One instance per zone: the failure of either zone leaves only one instance running, but the requirement is at least two.  
Why C is not selected: All four instances in a single Availability Zone would not survive that zone's failure, and Spot capacity can be reclaimed at any time — unacceptable for a stateful production application.  
Why D is not selected: Spot Instances in the second zone can be reclaimed at any time, so there's no guarantee that two instances remain running.

---

582\. An ecommerce company uses Amazon Route 53 as its DNS provider. The company hosts its website on premises and in the AWS Cloud. The company's on-premises data center is near the us-west-1 Region. The company uses the eu-central-1 Region to host the website. The company wants to minimize load time for the website as much as possible.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Set up a geolocation routing policy. Send the traffic that is near us-west-1 to the on-premises data center. Send the traffic that is near eu-central-1 to eu-central-1.  
B. Set up a simple routing policy that routes all traffic that is near eu-central-1 to eu-central-1 and routes all traffic that is near the on-premises datacenter to the on-premises data center.  
C. Set up a latency routing policy. Associate the policy with us-west-1.  
D. Set up a weighted routing policy. Split the traffic evenly between eu-central-1 and the on-premises data center.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: There are two locations: the company's own data center near us-west-1 and the website in eu-central-1. Route 53 can route based on the requester's geographic location — a geolocation routing policy sends users in North America to the data center and users in Europe to eu-central-1. Each visitor lands on the nearest location, minimizing load time. It's also worth keeping geoproximity routing in mind, covered in the walkthrough for {{q:120,142}}.  
Why B is not selected: A simple routing policy returns records without regard to the client's location: it simply doesn't provide the behavior described in this option.  
Why C is not selected: A single record with a latency-based policy tied to us-west-1 keeps all traffic going to one location. The second location doesn't participate at all.  
Why D is not selected: A weighted routing policy splits traffic evenly regardless of geography: half of the European users would be routed across the ocean to the U.S. data center.

---

583\. A company has 5 PB of archived data on physical tapes. The company needs to preserve the data on the tapes for another 10 years for compliance purposes. The company wants to migrate to AWS in the next 6 months. The data center that stores the tapes has a 1 Gbps uplink internet connectivity.  
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Read the data from the tapes on premises. Stage the data in a local NFS storage. Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.  
B. Use an on-premises backup application to read the data from the tapes and to write directly to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.  
C. Order multiple AWS Snowball devices that have Tape Gateway. Copy the physical tapes to virtual tapes in Snowball. Ship the Snowball devices to AWS. Create a lifecycle policy to move the tapes to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.  
D. Configure an on-premises Tape Gateway. Create virtual tapes in the AWS Cloud. Use backup software to copy the physical tape to the virtual tape.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: Do the math: 5 PB over a 1 Gbps link works out to roughly 10 TB a day, or about 485 days even at full uplink utilization — against a 6-month deadline. That rules out any online transfer option on arithmetic alone. Snowball with Tape Gateway is built exactly for this case: physical tapes are read into virtual tapes right on the device, the devices are shipped to AWS, and a lifecycle policy then moves the virtual tapes into S3 Glacier Deep Archive — the cheapest storage class, matching the ten-year compliance retention requirement.  
Why A is not selected: DataSync would transfer over the same link, so the six-month deadline still can't be met. It would also require an intermediate 5 PB NFS staging store, which the company doesn't have.  
Why B is not selected: Writing directly to Deep Archive still goes over the same uplink: about 485 days versus the six months available.  
Why D is not selected: An on-premises Tape Gateway creates virtual tapes in the cloud, but the data still travels over the internet link — the same math, and the same timeline failure.

---

584\. A company is deploying an application that processes large quantities of data in parallel. The company plans to use Amazon EC2 instances for the workload. The network architecture must be configurable to prevent groups of nodes from sharing the same underlying hardware.  
Which networking solution meets these requirements?  
A. Run the EC2 instances in a spread placement group.  
B. Group the EC2 instances in separate accounts.  
C. Configure the EC2 instances with dedicated tenancy.  
D. Configure the EC2 instances with shared tenancy.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The requirement is that groups of nodes must not end up on the same underlying hardware. That's exactly what a spread placement group does: each instance is placed on separate hardware with its own power and networking, so a single hardware failure affects only one node.  
Why B is not selected: Separate accounts have no effect on physical placement: the instances could still end up on the same host.  
Why C is not selected: Dedicated tenancy only guarantees that no other customer's instances share the host — your own nodes can still end up on the same hardware.  
Why D is not selected: Shared tenancy is the default mode and provides no placement guarantees at all.

---

585\. A solutions architect is designing a disaster recovery (DR) strategy to provide Amazon EC2 capacity in a failover AWS Region. Business requirements state that the DR strategy must meet capacity in the failover Region.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Purchase On-Demand Instances in the failover Region.  
B. Purchase an EC2 Savings Plan in the failover Region.  
C. Purchase regional Reserved Instances in the failover Region.  
D. Purchase a Capacity Reservation in the failover Region.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: The requirement is framed as a guarantee of capacity in the failover Region. Only a Capacity Reservation reserves the actual compute capacity in a specific Availability Zone: instances are guaranteed to launch at the moment of failover.  
Why A is not selected: On-Demand Instances aren't reserved in advance: at the moment of a regional outage, the needed capacity might simply not be available.  
Why B is not selected: A Savings Plan is a financial commitment made for a discount; it doesn't guarantee capacity.  
Why C is not selected: Regional Reserved Instances provide a discount and flexibility across zones, but they don't reserve capacity; only zonal Reserved Instances or a Capacity Reservation do that.

---

586\. A company has five organizational units (OUs) as part of its organization in AWS Organizations. Each OU correlates to the five businesses that the company owns. The company's research and development (R&amp;D) business is separating from the company and will need its own organization. A solutions architect creates a separate new management account for this purpose.  
What should the solutions architect do next in the new management account?  
A. Have the R&amp;D AWS account be part of both organizations during the transition.  
B. Invite the R&amp;D AWS account to be part of the new organization after the R&amp;D AWS account has left the prior organization.  
C. Create a new R&amp;D AWS account in the new organization. Migrate resources from the prior R&amp;D AWS account to the new R&amp;D AWS account.  
D. Have the R&amp;D AWS account join the new organization. Make the new management account a member of the prior organization.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The key rule: an AWS account can belong to only one organization at a time. So the sequence has to be strict — the R&amp;D account first leaves the prior organization (which requires it to have valid billing information and contact details on file, or it can't leave), and only then does the new organization's management account send it an invitation, which the account accepts. The resources themselves stay in place: only the account's organization membership changes.  
Why A is not selected: Simultaneous membership in two organizations is not technically possible.  
Why C is not selected: Creating a new account and migrating resources is a project involving downtime and risk, when simply moving the existing account is enough.  
Why D is not selected: The new organization's management account cannot be a member of another organization: it too is subject to the one-organization rule.

---

587\. A company is designing a solution to capture customer activity in different web applications to process analytics and make predictions. Customer activity in the web applications is unpredictable and can increase suddenly. The company requires a solution that integrates with other web applications. The solution must include an authorization step for security purposes.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Configure a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) in front of an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) container instance that stores the information that the company receives in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Authorization is resolved at the GWLB.  
B. Configure an Amazon API Gateway endpoint in front of an Amazon Kinesis data stream that stores the information that the company receives in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use an AWS Lambda function to resolve authorization.  
C. Configure an Amazon API Gateway endpoint in front of an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose that stores the information that the company receives in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use an API Gateway Lambda authorizer to resolve authorization.  
D. Configure a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) in front of an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) container instance that stores the information that the company receives on an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Use an AWS Lambda function to resolve authorization.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: Traffic is unpredictable and can spike suddenly, integration with multiple web applications is needed, and an authorization step is required. API Gateway provides a single entry point, and a Lambda authorizer — a built-in mechanism of the gateway itself — handles authorization. From there, data flows into Kinesis Data Firehose, which buffers it and delivers it into S3 for analytics with no administration required.  
Why A is not selected: A Gateway Load Balancer is designed to route traffic to inspection appliances and doesn't perform request authorization, and containers backed by EFS require ongoing operations.  
Why B is not selected: A Kinesis Data Stream doesn't write to S3 on its own — it needs a consumer to do that, and using a separate authorization function instead of API Gateway's built-in authorizer adds unnecessary complexity.  
Why D is not selected: This repeats the same mistake of using a Gateway Load Balancer as the entry point for client requests, plus unnecessary container infrastructure.

---

588\. An ecommerce company wants a disaster recovery solution for its Amazon RDS DB instances that run Microsoft SQL Server Enterprise Edition. The company's current recovery point objective (RPO) and recovery time objective (RTO) are 24 hours.  
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Create a cross-Region read replica and promote the read replica to the primary instance.  
B. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create RDS cross-Region replication.  
C. Use cross-Region replication every 24 hours to copy native backups to an Amazon S3 bucket.  
D. Copy automatic snapshots to another Region every 24 hours.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: The recovery targets are lenient: up to 24 hours of data loss and downtime are both acceptable. That makes copying automated snapshots to another Region once a day the cheapest option — you pay only for snapshot storage, with no running database copy in the second Region.  
Why A is not selected: A cross-Region read replica is a continuously running instance billed around the clock, delivering far tighter RPO/RTO than what's actually required.  
Why B is not selected: DMS requires a replication instance and a target database running continuously — again, unnecessary expense.  
Why C is not selected: Native engine backups copied to a bucket with cross-Region replication add an extra layer of automation and storage for the same outcome that built-in snapshot copying already provides.

---

589\. A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer that has sticky sessions enabled. The web server currently hosts the user session state. The company wants to ensure high availability and avoid user session state loss in the event of a web server outage.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Use an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached instance to store the session data. Update the application to use ElastiCache for Memcached to store the session state.  
B. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis to store the session state. Update the application to use ElastiCache for Redis to store the session state.  
C. Use an AWS Storage Gateway cached volume to store session data. Update the application to use AWS Storage Gateway cached volume to store the session state.  
D. Use Amazon RDS to store the session state. Update the application to use Amazon RDS to store the session state.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: Session state currently lives on the web servers themselves, so a server failure loses user sessions. The right fix is to move it to an external store: ElastiCache for Redis supports replication, automatic failover to a replica node, and data persistence, so sessions survive the failure of either a cache node or a web server.  
Why A is not selected: Memcached supports neither replication nor data persistence: sessions are lost if a node fails.  
Why C is not selected: Storage Gateway is a hybrid gateway for on-premises environments; it isn't designed for storing web application session state.  
Why D is not selected: A relational database can technically store sessions, but it's slower than an in-memory cache and more expensive; the standard choice for session storage is Redis.

---

590\. A company migrated a MySQL database from the company's on-premises data center to an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. The company sized the RDS DB instance to meet the company's average daily workload. Once a month, the database performs slowly when the company runs queries for a report. The company wants to have the ability to run reports and maintain the performance of the daily workloads.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Create a read replica of the database. Direct the queries to the read replica.  
B. Create a backup of the database. Restore the backup to another DB instance. Direct the queries to the new database.  
C. Export the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the S3 bucket.  
D. Resize the DB instance to accommodate the additional workload.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Heavy reporting queries run once a month and interfere with the everyday workload. A read replica absorbs these queries, leaving the primary instance free to handle the daily workload it was sized for.  
Why B is not selected: Restoring from a backup gives a point-in-time snapshot of the data and requires a manual operation every month.  
Why C is not selected: Exporting to S3 and querying through Athena means building a separate export pipeline and working with stale data.  
Why D is not selected: Resizing the instance for just one day a month means paying the higher cost for all thirty days, and it doesn't separate the workloads.

---

591\. A company runs a container application by using Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The application includes microservices that manage customers and place orders. The company needs to route incoming requests to the appropriate microservices.  
Which solution will meet this requirement MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Use the AWS Load Balancer Controller to provision a Network Load Balancer.  
B. Use the AWS Load Balancer Controller to provision an Application Load Balancer.  
C. Use an AWS Lambda function to connect the requests to Amazon EKS.  
D. Use Amazon API Gateway to connect the requests to Amazon EKS.  
Answer: D  
Review status: Disputed key (alternative: B)  
Dispute note: The standard way to route to microservices in EKS is ALB via the AWS Load Balancer Controller; API Gateway is generally more expensive  
Explanation: The task is to route incoming requests to different microservices within EKS — that is, choose a backend based on path or host. That's a job for a layer 7 load balancer. The standard approach in EKS is an Ingress resource, which the AWS Load Balancer Controller provisions as an Application Load Balancer: a single ALB serves every service in the cluster, billed hourly plus LCU usage. The dump's answer key points to D (API Gateway), and that's debatable: API Gateway is billed per request and adds a separate component in front of the cluster. The rule of thumb: reach for API Gateway when you actually need its features — API keys, throttling, authorizers, request transformation; otherwise, ALB is the standard choice for EKS.  
Why A is not selected: A Network Load Balancer operates at layer 4 and distinguishes only ports and protocols. It cannot route requests to microservices based on URL.  
Why B is not selected: A strong alternative and the canonical solution for EKS: the same controller, but provisioning an ALB, which supports path- and host-based routing and is typically cheaper than API Gateway for steady traffic.  
Why C is not selected: Putting Lambda in front of EKS means building a custom proxy: per-invocation billing, extra latency, and hand-written routing logic instead of the load balancer's built-in rules.

---

592\. A company uses AWS and sells access to copyrighted images. The company’s global customer base needs to be able to access these images quickly. The company must deny access to users from specific countries. The company wants to minimize costs as much as possible.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Use Amazon S3 to store the images. Turn on multi-factor authentication (MFA) and public bucket access. Provide customers with a link to the S3 bucket.  
B. Use Amazon S3 to store the images. Create an IAM user for each customer. Add the users to a group that has permission to access the S3 bucket.  
C. Use Amazon EC2 instances that are behind Application Load Balancers (ALBs) to store the images. Deploy the instances only in the countries the company services. Provide customers with links to the ALBs for their specific country's instances.  
D. Use Amazon S3 to store the images. Use Amazon CloudFront to distribute the images with geographic restrictions. Provide a signed URL for each customer to access the data in CloudFront.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: There are three requirements: fast delivery to a global audience, blocking access from specific countries, and minimizing cost. CloudFront covers all three: content is served from edge locations (faster and cheaper than serving data-transfer-out directly from S3), geographic restrictions block requests from the listed countries, and signed URLs restrict access to a specific customer for a limited time. The bucket itself is locked down to direct access via origin access control (OAC), so the restrictions can't be bypassed.  
Why A is not selected: A public bucket serves images to everyone with no country restrictions, and MFA has nothing to do with anonymous read access. For paid content, this means lost revenue.  
Why B is not selected: An IAM user for every customer is an administrative nightmare at a global customer scale, and it still provides neither faster delivery nor country-level blocking.  
Why C is not selected: A fleet of instances behind load balancers in every country is the most expensive and labor-intensive option, and separate links per country are easily circumvented.

---

593\. A solutions architect is designing a highly available Amazon ElastiCache for Redis based solution. The solutions architect needs to ensure that failures do not result in performance degradation or loss of data locally and within an AWS Region. The solution needs to provide high availability at the node level and at the Region level.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Use Multi-AZ Redis replication groups with shards that contain multiple nodes.  
B. Use Redis shards that contain multiple nodes with Redis append only files (AOF) turned on.  
C. Use a Multi-AZ Redis cluster with more than one read replica in the replication group.  
D. Use Redis shards that contain multiple nodes with Auto Scaling turned on.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Fault tolerance is required at both the node level and within the Region, with no data loss. That calls for Redis replication groups with Multi-AZ enabled, where each shard consists of a primary node and replicas spread across different Availability Zones: a node failure triggers automatic failover to a replica, and the data is preserved.  
Why B is not selected: Append-only files (AOF) protect data on a single node, but if that node or its Availability Zone fails, access to the cluster is lost.  
Why C is not selected: This option sounds close, but it describes a cluster with read replicas without explicitly spreading shards across multiple nodes; the correct construct is specifically Multi-AZ replication groups with multi-node shards.  
Why D is not selected: Auto scaling adjusts capacity to match load and has nothing to do with fault tolerance.

---

594\. A company plans to migrate to AWS and use Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances for its application. During the migration testing phase, a technical team observes that the application takes a long time to launch and load memory to become fully productive.  
Which solution will reduce the launch time of the application during the next testing phase?  
A. Launch two or more EC2 On-Demand Instances. Turn on auto scaling features and make the EC2 On-Demand Instances available during the next testing phase.  
B. Launch EC2 Spot Instances to support the application and to scale the application so it is available during the next testing phase.  
C. Launch the EC2 On-Demand Instances with hibernation turned on. Configure EC2 Auto Scaling warm pools during the next testing phase.  
D. Launch EC2 On-Demand Instances with Capacity Reservations. Start additional EC2 instances during the next testing phase.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: It's not the instance launch that's slow, but the application reaching a fully productive state — it needs to warm up memory. Hibernation saves the in-memory state to disk, and an Auto Scaling warm pool keeps already-initialized instances on standby, which resume in seconds instead of going through a full application load.  
Why A is not selected: Auto scaling will add more instances, but each new one still has to go through the same slow warm-up.  
Why B is not selected: Spot Instances only change the price; initialization time stays the same.  
Why D is not selected: A Capacity Reservation guarantees instance availability but doesn't speed up loading the application into memory.

---

595\. A company's applications run on Amazon EC2 instances in Auto Scaling groups. The company notices that its applications experience sudden traffic increases on random days of the week. The company wants to maintain application performance during sudden traffic increases.  
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Use manual scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.  
B. Use predictive scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.  
C. Use dynamic scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.  
D. Use schedule scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The traffic spikes happen on random days, so neither a fixed schedule nor a history-based forecast will work. Dynamic scaling reacts to an actual metric and adds instances only when the load has actually increased — delivering the needed performance without paying for idle capacity.  
Why A is not selected: Manually resizing the group requires someone to be on standby waiting for a random spike.  
Why B is not selected: Predictive scaling relies on recurring patterns, but the spikes here are random.  
Why D is not selected: Scheduled scaling doesn't apply for the same reason: there's no known time for the spike in advance.

---

596\. An ecommerce application uses a PostgreSQL database that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. During a monthly sales event, database usage increases and causes database connection issues for the application. The traffic is unpredictable for subsequent monthly sales events, which impacts the sales forecast. The company needs to maintain performance when there is an unpredictable increase in traffic.  
Which solution resolves this issue in the MOST cost-effective way?  
A. Migrate the PostgreSQL database to Amazon Aurora Serverless v2.  
B. Enable auto scaling for the PostgreSQL database on the EC2 instance to accommodate increased usage.  
C. Migrate the PostgreSQL database to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with a larger instance type.  
D. Migrate the PostgreSQL database to Amazon Redshift to accommodate increased usage.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The problem is connection exhaustion during an unpredictable monthly spike. Aurora Serverless v2 adjusts capacity to match load within seconds and scales back down during quiet periods, so there's no need to pay for peak-sized capacity year-round. The engine is PostgreSQL-compatible, so the application doesn't need to be rewritten.  
Why B is not selected: There's no such thing as auto scaling for a database running on an EC2 instance: only the instance itself can be resized, and only manually, with downtime.  
Why C is not selected: A larger RDS instance is billed around the clock for a peak that occurs only once a month: this is more expensive.  
Why D is not selected: Redshift is an analytics warehouse; it isn't suited to the transactional workload of an ecommerce application.

---

597\. A company hosts an internal serverless application on AWS by using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The company’s employees report issues with high latency when they begin using the application each day. The company wants to reduce latency.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Increase the API Gateway throttling limit.  
B. Set up a scheduled scaling to increase Lambda provisioned concurrency before employees begin to use the application each day.  
C. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to initiate a Lambda function as a target for the alarm at the beginning of each day.  
D. Increase the Lambda function memory.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The latency appears specifically at the start of the workday — a classic cold-start pattern, since employees arrive at roughly the same time. Provisioned concurrency keeps function instances initialized, and scheduled scaling turns it on shortly before the workday begins, so the company isn't paying for the reserved capacity around the clock.  
Why A is not selected: The API Gateway throttling limit protects against overload and has no effect on function initialization time.  
Why C is not selected: Periodically invoking the function on a timer would warm up only a single instance, while employees generate dozens of concurrent requests.  
Why D is not selected: More memory speeds up computation, but the latency spike at the start of the day is caused by the creation of new execution environments.

---

598\. A research company uses on-premises devices to generate data for analysis. The company wants to use the AWS Cloud to analyze the data. The devices generate .csv files and support writing the data to an SMB file share.  
Company analysts must be able to use SQL commands to query the data. The analysts will run queries periodically throughout the day.  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose three.)  
A. Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway on premises in Amazon S3 File Gateway mode.  
B. Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway on premises in Amazon FSx File Gateway made.  
C. Set up an AWS Glue crawler to create a table based on the data that is in Amazon S3.  
D. Set up an Amazon EMR cluster with EMR File System (EMRFS) to query the data that is in Amazon S3. Provide access to analysts.  
E. Set up an Amazon Redshift cluster to query the data that is in Amazon S3. Provide access to analysts.  
F. Setup Amazon Athena to query the data that is in Amazon S3. Provide access to analysts.  
Answer: ACF  
Explanation: The devices can only write to an SMB share, so an on-premises Storage Gateway is deployed in Amazon S3 File Gateway mode: the CSV files land directly as objects in the bucket (A). From there, an AWS Glue crawler determines the schema and creates a table in the data catalog (C), and analysts run SQL queries through Amazon Athena, paying only for the bytes scanned (F). No continuously running cluster is involved — for periodic queries, this is the most cost-effective path.  
Why B is not selected: FSx File Gateway caches access to FSx file systems, and the data doesn't end up in S3 where Glue and Athena could read it.  
Why D is not selected: An EMR cluster is billed for node run time, but queries are run only a few times a day: the money goes toward idle capacity.  
Why E is not selected: A Redshift cluster is also billed continuously; for periodic queries, it's noticeably more expensive than Athena's pay-per-scan pricing.

---

599\. A company wants to use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) clusters and Amazon RDS DB instances to build and run a payment processing application. The company will run the application in its on-premises data center for compliance purposes.  
A solutions architect wants to use AWS Outposts as part of the solution. The solutions architect is working with the company's operational team to build the application.  
Which activities are the responsibility of the company's operational team? (Choose three.)  
A. Providing resilient power and network connectivity to the Outposts racks  
B. Managing the virtualization hypervisor, storage systems, and the AWS services that run on Outposts  
C. Physical security and access controls of the data center environment  
D. Availability of the Outposts infrastructure including the power supplies, servers, and networking equipment within the Outposts racks  
E. Physical maintenance of Outposts components  
F. Providing extra capacity for Amazon ECS clusters to mitigate server failures and maintenance events  
Answer: ACF  
Review status: Corrected key (source: ACE; reviewed: ACF)  
Correction note: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, physical maintenance of the rack's components (option E) and the availability of the Outposts infrastructure itself are AWS's responsibility; on the customer's side are power and connectivity, physical security of the site, and keeping spare capacity on hand in case a server fails — that is, A, C, and F  
Explanation: AWS Outposts sits in the customer's own facility, so the line of responsibility runs along the rack. It's the customer's job to provide the rack with resilient power and network connectivity (A), physical security and access control for the facility itself (C), and extra capacity in the ECS clusters so that a server failure or maintenance event doesn't take down the application (F): Outposts is a fixed pool of capacity that doesn't expand automatically.  
Why B is not selected: AWS itself manages the virtualization hypervisor, storage systems, and the AWS services running on Outposts — the customer has no access to that layer.  
Why D is not selected: AWS is responsible for the availability of the Outposts infrastructure, including the power supplies, servers, and networking equipment inside the rack.  
Why E is not selected: Physical maintenance of Outposts components is performed by AWS technicians who come on-site. The dump's answer key attributed this item to the customer — that's an error noted in the audit log.

---

600\. A company is planning to migrate a TCP-based application into the company's VPC. The application is publicly accessible on a nonstandard TCP port through a hardware appliance in the company's data center. This public endpoint can process up to 3 million requests per second with low latency. The company requires the same level of performance for the new public endpoint in AWS.  
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?  
A. Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Configure the NLB to be publicly accessible over the TCP port that the application requires.  
B. Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Configure the ALB to be publicly accessible over the TCP port that the application requires.  
C. Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution that listens on the TCP port that the application requires. Use an Application Load Balancer as the origin.  
D. Deploy an Amazon API Gateway API that is configured with the TCP port that the application requires. Configure AWS Lambda functions with provisioned concurrency to process the requests.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The application runs over TCP on a nonstandard port and must handle millions of requests per second with low latency. That's a Network Load Balancer's profile: it operates at layer 4, handles millions of connections per second, adds minimal latency, and can listen on any port.  
Why B is not selected: An Application Load Balancer understands only HTTP and HTTPS: it doesn't handle an arbitrary TCP protocol.  
Why C is not selected: CloudFront works only with HTTP and HTTPS and cannot listen on an arbitrary TCP port.  
Why D is not selected: API Gateway handles HTTP and WebSocket, not arbitrary TCP, and it can't deliver that level of throughput.

---

601\. A company runs its critical database on an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. The company wants to migrate to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with minimal downtime and data loss.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Create a DB snapshot of the RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance to populate a new Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.  
B. Create an Aurora read replica of the RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. Promote the Aurora read replicate to a new Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.  
C. Use data import from Amazon S3 to migrate the database to an Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.  
D. Use the pg_dump utility to back up the RDS for PostgreSQL database. Restore the backup to a new Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The standard path from RDS for PostgreSQL to Aurora PostgreSQL is an Aurora read replica: it is created from the running instance, catches up, and stays in sync, after which it is promoted to a standalone cluster. Downtime is reduced to the minutes it takes to switch over, there is no data loss, and the whole process uses built-in console tools.  
Why A is not selected: Restoring from a snapshot gives you a point-in-time copy: changes made after the snapshot are lost, and the downtime is noticeably longer.  
Why C is not selected: Importing from S3 requires exporting the data beforehand and a lengthy write freeze.  
Why D is not selected: Dumping with pg_dump and restoring is the slowest path, with a large downtime window and manual steps.

---

602\. A company's infrastructure consists of hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances that use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage. A solutions architect must ensure that every EC2 instance can be recovered after a disaster.  
What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement with the LEAST amount of effort?  
A. Take a snapshot of the EBS storage that is attached to each EC2 instance. Create an AWS CloudFormation template to launch new EC2 instances from the EBS storage.  
B. Take a snapshot of the EBS storage that is attached to each EC2 instance. Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to set the environment based on the EC2 template and attach the EBS storage.  
C. Use AWS Backup to set up a backup plan for the entire group of EC2 instances. Use the AWS Backup API or the AWS CLI to speed up the restore process for multiple EC2 instances.  
D. Create an AWS Lambda function to take a snapshot of the EBS storage that is attached to each EC2 instance and copy the Amazon Machine Images (AMIs). Create another Lambda function to perform the restores with the copied AMIs and attach the EBS storage.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: There are hundreds of instances, and minimal effort is required. AWS Backup lets a single backup plan cover the entire fleet of instances, automatically backing up both the configuration and the attached volumes, and bulk restores can be kicked off through the API or CLI. There is no need to write any custom scripts or templates.  
Why A is not selected: Volume snapshots do not preserve instance configuration, and a CloudFormation template for hundreds of machines would have to be written and maintained by hand.  
Why B is not selected: Elastic Beanstalk deploys applications from code and is not designed to restore arbitrary instances from snapshots.  
Why D is not selected: Two custom Lambda functions handling snapshots and AMIs mean code, schedules, and error handling - that is the most effort, not the least.

---

603\. A company recently migrated to the AWS Cloud. The company wants a serverless solution for large-scale parallel on-demand processing of a semistructured dataset. The data consists of logs, media files, sales transactions, and IoT sensor data that is stored in Amazon S3. The company wants the solution to process thousands of items in the dataset in parallel.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?  
A. Use the AWS Step Functions Map state in Inline mode to process the data in parallel.  
B. Use the AWS Step Functions Map state in Distributed mode to process the data in parallel.  
C. Use AWS Glue to process the data in parallel.  
D. Use several AWS Lambda functions to process the data in parallel.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: The requirement is a serverless solution that processes thousands of items in an S3 dataset in parallel. The Step Functions Map state in Distributed mode is built exactly for this: it reads the list of objects from the bucket itself and launches up to ten thousand parallel child executions, with no cluster and no custom distribution code required.  
Why A is not selected: Inline mode for the Map state is limited to forty concurrent branches and keeps all the data in the execution state - it cannot handle thousands of items.  
Why C is not selected: AWS Glue can do the job, but it is Spark-based ETL with its own jobs and configuration - more operational overhead than the built-in Distributed Map.  
Why D is not selected: Multiple Lambda functions would require manually partitioning the work, tracking concurrency, and collecting results - you would have to build the entire orchestrator yourself.

---

604\. A company will migrate 10 PB of data to Amazon S3 in 6 weeks. The current data center has a 500 Mbps uplink to the internet. Other on-premises applications share the uplink. The company can use 80% of the internet bandwidth for this one-time migration task.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Configure AWS DataSync to migrate the data to Amazon S3 and to automatically verify the data.  
B. Use rsync to transfer the data directly to Amazon S3.  
C. Use the AWS CLI and multiple copy processes to send the data directly to Amazon S3.  
D. Order multiple AWS Snowball devices. Copy the data to the devices. Send the devices to AWS to copy the data to Amazon S3.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: This again comes down to unforgiving arithmetic: 80% of 500 Mbps is 400 Mbps, or roughly 4.3 TB per day. At that rate, ten petabytes would take thousands of days, but the deadline is six weeks. No amount of online transfer optimization helps here - this calls for physical shipping: multiple Snowball devices loaded in parallel. Rule of thumb: divide the data volume using "1 Gbps ≈ 10 TB per day," and if that exceeds the allotted time, the answer is an offline transfer.  
Why A is not selected: DataSync speeds up and verifies the transfer, but it still runs over the same 400 Mbps uplink. The timeline is off by two orders of magnitude.  
Why B is not selected: rsync also does not work with S3 directly as a file system, and either way it is limited by the same bandwidth.  
Why C is not selected: Multiple parallel CLI copy processes share the same link: the combined throughput will not exceed 400 Mbps.

---

605\. A company has several on-premises Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (ISCSI) network storage servers.  
The company wants to reduce the number of these servers by moving to the AWS Cloud. A solutions architect must provide low-latency access to frequently used data and reduce the dependency on on-premises servers with a minimal number of infrastructure changes.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Deploy an Amazon S3 File Gateway.  
B. Deploy Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage with backups to Amazon S3.  
C. Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway that is configured with stored volumes.  
D. Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway that is configured with cached volumes.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: The requirements are fewer servers, low-latency access to frequently used data, and minimal infrastructure changes. A Volume Gateway configured with cached volumes presents volumes over the same iSCSI protocol, so clients notice no difference, while the bulk of the data is stored in S3 and only the active portion stays in the local cache. This is exactly how dependency on on-premises storage servers is reduced.  
Why A is not selected: S3 File Gateway presents shares over NFS and SMB: the protocol would change, and the requirement calls for minimal changes.  
Why B is not selected: EBS volumes live inside AWS and attach to instances, not to the company's on-premises servers.  
Why C is not selected: Stored volumes keep the entire dataset on local disks, so the number and capacity of on-premises storage servers are not reduced.

---

606\. A solutions architect is designing an application that will allow business users to upload objects to Amazon S3. The solution needs to maximize object durability. Objects also must be readily available at any time and for any length of time. Users will access objects frequently within the first 30 days after the objects are uploaded, but users are much less likely to access objects that are older than 30 days.  
Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Store all the objects in S3 Standard with an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the objects to S3 Glacier after 30 days.  
B. Store all the objects in S3 Standard with an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the objects to S3 Standard- Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 30 days.  
C. Store all the objects in S3 Standard with an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the objects to S3 One Zone- Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 30 days.  
D. Store all the objects in S3 Intelligent-Tiering with an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 30 days.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: "Maximize object durability" and "readily available at any time" set the frame: the storage class must keep copies across three Availability Zones and return objects instantly. That leaves S3 Standard and Standard-IA in play. The access pattern is known and tied to object age - heavy access for the first 30 days, then infrequent - so an explicit Lifecycle rule into Standard-IA is cheaper than automated tiering with its monitoring fee.  
Why A is not selected: S3 Glacier retrieval takes minutes to hours. That violates the "readily available at any time" requirement.  
Why C is not selected: One Zone-IA keeps a single copy in a single Availability Zone. That directly contradicts the requirement to maximize object durability.  
Why D is not selected: This combination does not make sense: Intelligent-Tiering already moves objects between tiers on its own, and layering a Lifecycle rule on top pushes them into IA anyway - after you have already paid for the monitoring. With a known access pattern, a plain transition straight to Standard-IA is cheaper.

---

607\. A company has migrated a two-tier application from its on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud. The data tier is a Multi-AZ deployment of Amazon RDS for Oracle with 12 TB of General Purpose SSD Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage. The application is designed to process and store documents in the database as binary large objects (blobs) with an average document size of 6 MB.  
The database size has grown over time, reducing the performance and increasing the cost of storage. The company must improve the database performance and needs a solution that is highly available and resilient.  
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?  
A. Reduce the RDS DB instance size. Increase the storage capacity to 24 TiB. Change the storage type to Magnetic.  
B. Increase the RDS DB instance size. Increase the storage capacity to 24 TiChange the storage type to Provisioned IOPS.  
C. Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Update the application to store documents in the S3 bucket. Store the object metadata in the existing database.  
D. Create an Amazon DynamoDB table. Update the application to use DynamoDB. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate data from the Oracle database to DynamoDB.  
Answer: C  
Explanation: The core problem is that 6 MB documents are stored in the database as binary large objects: the database bloats, performance drops, and RDS storage gets expensive. The right fix is to split the data: store the documents themselves in S3 and keep only metadata and references in the database. This sharply shrinks the database size, improves performance, costs far less to store in S3, and keeps the Multi-AZ configuration intact.  
Why A is not selected: Magnetic storage is slower, and doubling the capacity just raises the cost - performance would get worse, not better.  
Why B is not selected: A larger instance and Provisioned IOPS would speed things up, but it is the most expensive path, and the root cause - binary objects in the database - remains unaddressed.  
Why D is not selected: Moving to DynamoDB means rewriting the application, and the 400 KB item size limit makes storing six-megabyte documents impossible.

---

608\. A company has an application that serves clients that are deployed in more than 20.000 retail storefront locations around the world. The application consists of backend web services that are exposed over HTTPS on port 443. The application is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The retail locations communicate with the web application over the public internet. The company allows each retail location to register the IP address that the retail location has been allocated by its local ISP.  
The company's security team recommends to increase the security of the application endpoint by restricting access to only the IP addresses registered by the retail locations.  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?  
A. Associate an AWS WAF web ACL with the ALB. Use IP rule sets on the ALB to filter traffic. Update the IP addresses in the rule to include the registered IP addresses.  
B. Deploy AWS Firewall Manager to manage the ALConfigure firewall rules to restrict traffic to the ALModify the firewall rules to include the registered IP addresses.  
C. Store the IP addresses in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Configure an AWS Lambda authorization function on the ALB to validate that incoming requests are from the registered IP addresses.  
D. Configure the network ACL on the subnet that contains the public interface of the ALB. Update the ingress rules on the network ACL with entries for each of the registered IP addresses.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: Only registered store IP addresses need to be allowed through, there are thousands of them, and the list keeps changing. AWS WAF with IP sets is built for exactly this: the set of addresses is maintained separately from the rule, supports tens of thousands of entries, and can be updated through the API without touching the web ACL itself. The web ACL is associated with the load balancer, and anything not in the set is blocked before it reaches the application.  
Why B is not selected: Firewall Manager centrally distributes WAF policies across accounts, but it does not do the filtering itself - WAF remains the underlying service either way.  
Why C is not selected: The Application Load Balancer has no Lambda-based authorization mechanism: it routes requests, and building custom validation would require code inside the application.  
Why D is not selected: Network ACLs are limited to roughly twenty rules per list (the maximum can be raised only slightly) - twenty thousand addresses will not fit.

---

609\. A company is building a data analysis platform on AWS by using AWS Lake Formation. The platform will ingest data from different sources such as Amazon S3 and Amazon RDS. The company needs a secure solution to prevent access to portions of the data that contain sensitive information.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Create an IAM role that includes permissions to access Lake Formation tables.  
B. Create data filters to implement row-level security and cell-level security.  
C. Create an AWS Lambda function that removes sensitive information before Lake Formation ingests the data.  
D. Create an AWS Lambda function that periodically queries and removes sensitive information from Lake Formation tables.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: What needs hiding is not entire tables but parts of them, and it must be done without rewriting the data. Lake Formation provides a built-in mechanism for this - data filters: they define which columns are visible (column-level security), which rows are returned based on a condition (row-level security), and, as a result, which individual cells a given principal can access. The filter is enforced at the service level, so it works the same way for Athena, Redshift Spectrum, and EMR. The underlying data stays untouched, and no copies are created.  
Why A is not selected: A role with permissions on tables grants access on an all-or-nothing basis. The requirement is to hide parts of the data within a table.  
Why C is not selected: Stripping sensitive data before ingestion means losing information that other teams might need, plus building and maintaining a custom processing pipeline.  
Why D is not selected: Periodically purging tables with a function both destroys data and leaves a window during which the sensitive information is still exposed.

---

610\. A company deploys Amazon EC2 instances that run in a VPC. The EC2 instances load source data into Amazon S3 buckets so that the data can be processed in the future. According to compliance laws, the data must not be transmitted over the public internet. Servers in the company's on-premises data center will consume the output from an application that runs on the EC2 instances.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Deploy an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon EC2. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the company and the VPC.  
B. Deploy a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection between the on- premises network and the VPC.  
C. Set up an AWS Transit Gateway connection from the VPC to the S3 buckets. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the company and the VPC.  
D. Set up proxy EC2 instances that have routes to NAT gateways. Configure the proxy EC2 instances to fetch S3 data and feed the application instances.  
Answer: B  
Explanation: There are two requirements here, and they are met by two different mechanisms. Traffic from the instances to S3 must not go over the internet - that calls for a gateway VPC endpoint for S3, with a route added to the subnet route table. The company's on-premises servers must receive the application's output - that calls for a Direct Connect connection between the on-premises location and the VPC, a private link that bypasses the internet.  
Why A is not selected: An interface endpoint for EC2 gives private access to the EC2 management API, not to S3. Uploading data to the bucket would still go over the internet.  
Why C is not selected: Transit Gateway connects networks to each other, not a network to the S3 service. There is no way to attach a bucket to it.  
Why D is not selected: A NAT gateway is itself a path out to the public internet: that directly violates the requirement, and the proxy instances add extra work and cost.

---

611\. A company has an application with a REST-based interface that allows data to be received in near-real time from a third-party vendor. Once received, the application processes and stores the data for further analysis. The application is running on Amazon EC2 instances.  
The third-party vendor has received many 503 Service Unavailable Errors when sending data to the application.  
When the data volume spikes, the compute capacity reaches its maximum limit and the application is unable to process all requests.  
Which design should a solutions architect recommend to provide a more scalable solution?  
A. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest the data. Process the data using AWS Lambda functions.  
B. Use Amazon API Gateway on top of the existing application. Create a usage plan with a quota limit for the third-party vendor.  
C. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to ingest the data. Put the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer.  
D. Repackage the application as a container. Deploy the application using Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) using the EC2 launch type with an Auto Scaling group.  
Answer: A  
Explanation: The 503 errors mean data ingestion is bottlenecked by compute capacity. Kinesis Data Streams ingests the stream independently of processing speed and retains records, while Lambda functions process them in parallel and scale automatically. Spikes stop causing failures because ingestion and processing are decoupled.  
Why B is not selected: A usage plan with a quota throttles the vendor, meaning it drops part of the data instead of accepting it.  
Why C is not selected: SNS delivers messages immediately and does not buffer them: during a spike, the instances would still get hit with the same storm of requests.  
Why D is not selected: Containers on EC2 instances scale over minutes and still require managing capacity: peak spikes would still get dropped.

---

612\. A company has an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances in a private subnet. The application needs to process sensitive information from an Amazon S3 bucket. The application must not use the internet to connect to the S3 bucket.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Configure an internet gateway. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the internet gateway. Update the application to use the new internet gateway.  
B. Configure a VPN connection. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the VPN connection. Update the application to use the new VPN connection.  
C. Configure a NAT gateway. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the NAT gateway. Update the application to use the new NAT gateway.  
D. Configure a VPC endpoint. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the VPC endpoint. Update the application to use the new VPC endpoint.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: The application in the private subnet needs to reach S3 without going out to the internet. A VPC endpoint is the only mechanism that provides such a path: traffic to S3 travels over the AWS network, with no public addresses or NAT required. The bucket policy can additionally be tightened with an aws:SourceVpce condition, so the bucket holding sensitive data will not respond to requests that do not come through this endpoint. For S3, a gateway endpoint is typically used since it is free; an interface endpoint is needed when access must also come from an on-premises network over Direct Connect.  
Why A is not selected: An internet gateway exists to send traffic out to the internet, and a bucket policy has no way to describe such a source in the first place. This directly violates the requirement.  
Why B is not selected: A VPN connects the VPC to an external network, not the VPC to S3. Requests to S3 would still go through the public endpoint.  
Why C is not selected: A NAT gateway is an internet egress path with address translation. It violates the requirement, and on top of that it is billed per gigabyte processed.

---

613\. A company uses Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) to run a container application. The EKS cluster stores sensitive information in the Kubernetes secrets object. The company wants to ensure that the information is encrypted.  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?  
A. Use the container application to encrypt the information by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).  
B. Enable secrets encryption in the EKS cluster by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).  
C. Implement an AWS Lambda function to encrypt the information by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).  
D. Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to encrypt the information by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).  
Answer: B  
Explanation: This is about a built-in EKS feature: secrets encryption with a KMS key. The cluster is configured once, after which Secret objects are encrypted using envelope encryption before being written to etcd - handled by the control plane, not the application. No code and no extra services are needed, hence "least operational overhead." The same mechanism is covered in {{q:535}}; do not confuse it with storing application secrets in Secrets Manager or Parameter Store.  
Why A is not selected: Encrypting inside the application means every container has to work with KMS directly, and other cluster components would still read the secrets from etcd in plaintext.  
Why C is not selected: A separate Lambda function for encryption means your own code and an extra hop in the chain, whereas EKS can do the same thing through configuration alone.  
Why D is not selected: Parameter Store stores parameters outside of Kubernetes. The Secret objects in etcd would remain unencrypted, and the requirement is specifically about those.

---

614\. A company is designing a new multi-tier web application that consists of the following components:  
•Web and application servers that run on Amazon EC2 instances as part of Auto Scaling groups  
•An Amazon RDS DB instance for data storage A solutions architect needs to limit access to the application servers so that only the web servers can access them.  
Which solution will meet these requirements?  
A. Deploy AWS PrivateLink in front of the application servers. Configure the network ACL to allow only the web servers to access the application servers.  
B. Deploy a VPC endpoint in front of the application servers. Configure the security group to allow only the web servers to access the application servers.  
C. Deploy a Network Load Balancer with a target group that contains the application servers' Auto Scaling group. Configure the network ACL to allow only the web servers to access the application servers.  
D. Deploy an Application Load Balancer with a target group that contains the application servers' Auto Scaling group. Configure the security group to allow only the web servers to access the application servers.  
Answer: D  
Explanation: An Application Load Balancer is placed between the web tier and the application tier, with a target group containing the application servers' Auto Scaling group, and access is restricted using security groups: the inbound rule on the load balancer and on the application servers allows traffic only from the web servers' security group. This rule keeps working no matter how the number or addresses of instances change, because it references a security group rather than specific addresses.  
Why A is not selected: PrivateLink is for publishing a service to other VPCs or accounts, not for separating tiers within a single network. A network ACL also operates on subnets and address ranges and has no concept of a dynamic Auto Scaling group.  
Why B is not selected: A VPC endpoint provides access to AWS services or to services published through PrivateLink; you cannot place one "in front of" your own instances within the same VPC.  
Why C is not selected: The load balancer setup itself is sound, but the rule is expressed through a network ACL - which operates on address ranges and subnets and cannot reference the web servers' security group, so it stops being accurate whenever the fleet's composition changes.

---

615\. A company runs a critical, customer-facing application on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The application has a microservices architecture. The company needs to implement a solution that collects, aggregates, and summarizes metrics and logs from the application in a centralized location.  
Which solution meets these requirements?
